⭐⭐每一冊都留一個可打開的鏈接**。**③ ⭐⭐⭐ **把方法選擇寫成一段有來有回的推理**——逐字要點：其他工具用**全部控制點**＋最小二乘（「你提供的每一個控制點都會影響模型」）；它自己**用每一對控制點擬合一個候選模型**、**最好的一對被選中、其餘被丟棄**（「它們對擬合沒有直接影響」）；理由是「**我們對自家控制點的**信心遠低於對人的**」**；**「**把正確與錯誤的控制點平均起來不太可能得到好模型。而用 RANSAC 這種對離群點極其穩健的方法，我們可以從噪聲中找出哪怕一點點信號」；最後逐條列出它為什麼會錯（OCR 誤讀／街道在到達交叉口前轉彎使外推失效／標籤被誤解為另一條街）**三處**：**① ⭐⭐⭐「我們對自家控制點的信心遠低於對人的」是本條最誠實的一句**；**② ⭐⭐⭐細讀後才會發現的方法差別**（六參數仿射對四參數 Helmert、全部控制點對每對取最優），且給出量級證據（人類配準結果裡尺度各向異性多小於 3%、斜切多小於 3°，「兩者都足夠接近零，以至於不清楚它們是真實的還是配準不準確的產物」，故去掉這兩個參數只需兩個控制點而非三個）；**③ ⭐⭐失敗機制被逐條列出並歸因到具體組件**（短街名之所以難，歸因於底層 OCR 庫對長文本更好、而單個字母 O／X／M／W 的方向是歧義的）。**④ ⭐⭐⭐ **把「這個模型是怎麼做出來的」也寫出來**——逐字要點：最初想用某大模型 API 直接找交叉口，「它做得還行，但慢（每題約 3 分鐘）、貴（每張約 0.10 美元）且並不總是準確。它在非骨架圖上表現不好，而且過程不透明，所以很難改進」；隨後意識到自己其實是在用眼睛追蹤街道標籤來評價它找到的交叉口，於是改讓 OCR 做這件事；再後來發現「細化那一步並沒有幫助」，遂收斂到現在的模型**三處**：**① ⭐⭐⭐放棄一條路線的三個可數理由**（慢／貴／不透明——「過程不透明，所以難以改進」是很少見的工程判斷）；**② ⭐⭐⭐說明為什麼最終回到本地 OCR**（「評價方式」決定了「實現方式」）；**③ ⭐⭐如實記錄了一個被刪掉的步驟**。**⑤ ⭐⭐ 其餘**：有一節**與前人工作的對照**（另一篇論文先用自訂模型檢測交叉口再用另一套 OCR 讀條帶裡的街名，「本質上無法找到斜向街道」；並給出數字對照「至少對新奧爾良 1951，Mapsnap 在它配準的圖幅上有 76% 落在 15 英尺以內，而該論文是 14%」，⚠️ 並逐字自加保留「我不確定他們測的是哪些地圖，而且他們還有別的判據，所以這可能不是一個公平的比較」——**第二處最值得抄的地方**）；有一節**明確列出考慮過的替代方案**（羅盤玫瑰、比例尺）及各自為何不用；有一個**只有三個問題的問答節**（能否用於其他地圖／與某志願者站點的關係／它用 AI 嗎）；並如實寫出**開發所借助的 AI 編程工具**。**⑥ ⭐⭐ 可與 [[oldinsurancemaps]]、[[asgs]]、[[pyincore]]、[[duckdb-fema-nfip]]、[[openquake-engine]] 並讀**。

⚠️ **如實標注**：**① ⭐ 許可為 Apache-2.0**（實測內含 LICENSE，raw 探測 HTTP 200，GitHub 字段一致；⚠️ 未讀該文件內容），**⚠️ 亦未核實其測試數據與圖幅影像的權利**（其中含來自公共機構的掃描地圖——「代碼許可」與「其中資料權利」是兩件事）。**② ⚠️⚠️⚠️ **本次沒有運行它的任何一步****——**未安裝其命令行工具、未下載任何清單或影像、未運行 mapsnap、未打開其任何查看器鏈接、未打開任何圖**；**故不主张**其地理配準、其評測數字或其 IIIF 產物按所述工作**。**③ ⚠️⚠️ **未讀其任何源碼或 `docs/` 下的文檔****（未核對其地址解析率、RANSAC 實現與閾值選取、四參數模型是否如其所述）——**這是本條目最需要後續核實的一處**。**④ ⚠️ **未核實**其性能表的數字**（每一行均未覆核，也未打開那些標為「查看」的鏈接）。**⑤ ⭐ ⚠️ **不主张**其方法可用於任何特定城市或年代**（其自述已逐字給出失敗情形，本詞條只是轉述）。**⑥ ⚠️ **★10、fork 0**，且**未核實作者背景**。**⑦ ⚠️ **創建與推送均在解凍窗口之內（2026-05-14／2026-09-11）****。**⑧ ⚠️ **本條目所記為**2026-09-11 所見****。**核實說明**：repo 於 2026-09-11 經倉庫檢索接口與 GitHub API 實測讀取；README 33,514 位元組經 raw 實測逐字核對（含其性能表、How it Works、Notes on the model、Prior Art 與 Questions 各節）；`LICENSE` 的存在經 raw 探測確認（HTTP 200）；**文件清單經 GitHub API tree 接口實測（387 個文件、30 個目錄，`truncated` 為 false）**；**未克隆、未安裝任何依賴、未運行任何命令、未下載任何清單或影像、未打開任何查看器或圖、未讀任何源碼或文檔內容、未做其他網絡觀察**。
entries.body_en:
**mapsnap-georeferencer** (repository `danvk/mapsnap`) **is a tool that georeferences Sanborn insurance maps automatically**, stating its goal verbatim as automatically georeferencing Sanborn insurance maps. **Measured 10 stars, the highest-attention entry of this round, 0 forks, licence Apache-2.0 with a licence file measurably present and answering 200 to a raw probe and the GitHub field agreeing, primary language Python, a 160,321 KB repository, created 2026-05-14, last pushed 2026-09-11, default branch main** (all GitHub API measurements; ⭐ **creation and push both inside the thaw window**); **the README measures 33,514 bytes**; **the repository measures 387 files and 30 directories**, read through the trees endpoint with truncation false, holding a package directory, an application directory, test data, a gallery, images, models, scripts, baselines and small documentation and workflow directories. This entry belongs to this round’s theme of **wiring something up so that another system can use it**, and ⭐⭐⭐ **of the four it is the only one that measures the connection in distance**.

Verifiable details (**read from the README and measured in the tree**): ⭐⭐⭐ **① It connects the maps to coordinates automatically and says what comes out** — verbatim, after a few minutes depending on the number of images in the volume, **you get a IIIF Georeference AnnotationPage that you can view on Allmaps** ⭐⭐⭐ **Four things**: ⭐⭐⭐ **the product is a standardised annotation page rather than a picture, so other map tools can read it**, ⭐ **which is exactly this round’s theme of connecting to an existing viewer**; ⭐⭐⭐ **a minimal two-line usage is given**, installing a command-line tool, creating a directory, downloading a manifest, finding an open-map relation containing the map area and running one command, ⭐ **so the wiring is compressed into one command**; ⭐⭐ **one input is a relation identifier on an open map, so it borrows someone else’s boundary data to establish the rough extent**; **and ⭐⭐ the running time is stated honestly as minutes depending on the volume’s page count**, ⭐ **with no speed promised**. **② ⭐⭐⭐ It evaluates by distance rather than proportion and reports both ends** — a per-volume table gives pages placed at 27 of 33, 103 of 109 and 124 of 129, **the share within twenty-five feet and the share beyond two hundred feet**, a score and a clickable viewer link ⭐⭐⭐ **Four things**: ⭐⭐⭐ **the metric is a share under a distance threshold, so how well the georeferencing went is translated into a countable geographic error**; ⭐⭐⭐ **it also reports how badly wrong the failures are**, ⭐ **which this entry considers the most copyable evaluation design here, since knowing how accurate it is, is not enough without knowing how wrong it can be**; ⭐⭐⭐ **the test data come from hand geocoding by volunteers, so the reference is a human result**; **and ⭐⭐ every volume carries a link a reader can open to judge for themselves**. **③ ⭐⭐⭐ It presents its method choice as an argument with both sides** — verbatim, other tools fit using all control points and least squares, **so every point you provide influences the model**, whereas this tool **fits a candidate model from each pair of points, chooses the best pair and discards the rest, which then have no direct influence on the fit**, **the stated reason being that confidence in its own control points is far lower than in a human’s, so averaging a mix of correct and incorrect points is unlikely to produce a good model, while a method extremely robust to outliers can find a little signal through the noise**, followed by an itemised list of why it errs, from misread text through a street turning before an intersection to a label being taken for a different street ⭐⭐⭐ **Three things**: ⭐⭐⭐ **the sentence about confidence in its own control points being lower than in a human’s is the most honest line here**, ⭐ **since it explains why the human practice cannot be borrowed**; ⭐⭐⭐ **the method difference is only visible on close reading, a six-parameter affine model against a four-parameter one, all control points against the best pair**, **and it supplies magnitude evidence verbatim**, human georeferencing showing scale anisotropy mostly under three percent and skew mostly under three degrees, **both close enough to zero that it is unclear whether they are real or artefacts of inaccurate georeferencing**, so dropping them needs two control points rather than three; **and ⭐⭐ failure mechanisms are itemised and attributed to specific components**, short street names being hard verbatim because the underlying recogniser works better with longer runs of text and **the orientation of a single letter is ambiguous**. **④ ⭐⭐⭐ It also writes how the model was developed** — verbatim, the initial idea was to ask a large-model interface to find intersections, which **did an acceptable job but was slow at about three minutes per task, expensive at about ten cents per image and not always accurate**, doing poorly on maps that are not skeletons, **and whose process was opaque, making it hard to improve on**, after which the author realised he was evaluating its intersections by mentally tracing street labels, so the labels were handed to optical recognition instead, and later that **the refinement step was not helping**, leaving the present model ⭐⭐⭐ **Three things**: ⭐⭐⭐ **three countable reasons are given for abandoning a route, slow, expensive and opaque**, ⭐ **of which opaque and therefore hard to improve on is a rare piece of engineering judgement**; ⭐⭐⭐ **it says why it ended up with local recognition, so how it was evaluated determined how it was implemented**; **and ⭐⭐ a deleted step is recorded rather than hidden**. **⑤ ⭐⭐ Other details**: **a prior-art section contrasts an earlier paper’s essentially reversed approach**, detecting intersections with a custom model and then reading street labels in horizontal or vertical strips, **which it notes inherently cannot find diagonal streets**, and gives a numeric comparison — **at least for one 1951 volume, this tool places 76 percent of the images it maps within fifteen feet against 14 percent for that paper** — ⚠️ **with the repository adding the caveat verbatim that it is unsure which maps they tested on and that they have other criteria, so it may not be a fair comparison**, ⭐ **which this entry takes as the second most copyable item here**; **a section lists alternatives considered**, such as a compass rose or a scale bar, **with the reasons each was not used**; **a three-question section anticipates what readers most likely ask**, including whether it works on other map types and whether it uses artificial intelligence; **and the artificial-intelligence coding tools used in building it are stated**. **⑥ ⭐⭐ Readable with** [[oldinsurancemaps]], [[asgs]], [[pyincore]], [[duckdb-fema-nfip]] and [[openquake-engine]].

⚠️ **Stated plainly**: **① ⭐ The licence is Apache-2.0** — **a licence file is measurably present, answering 200 to a raw probe, and the GitHub field agrees**, ⚠️ **with its contents and the rights in its test data and map imagery not verified**, ⭐ **those including scans from public institutions, so rights in the code and rights in the material are two different things**. **② ⚠️⚠️⚠️ Nothing in it was run** — **the command-line tool was not installed, no manifest or imagery was downloaded, the tool was not run, no viewer link was opened and no image was opened**; **so this entry does not claim its georeferencing, its evaluation figures or its annotation output works as described**, ⭐ **what it verified being the verbatim README, including its performance table, its method argument, its failure cases and its development history, and the directory structure measured through the trees endpoint**. **③ ⚠️⚠️ Neither its source nor the documentation under its docs directory was read**, ⭐ **so whether the placement rates are attainable, how the robust fitting and its thresholds are implemented, and whether the four-parameter model is as described were not checked** — ⭐ **the single most important thing to verify next for this entry**. **④ ⚠️ The figures in its performance table were not verified**, ⭐ **no row re-checked and none of the viewer links opened**. **⑤ ⭐ ⚠️ No claim is made that the method works for any particular city or era**, ⭐ **its own failure cases being reported here rather than endorsed**. **⑥ ⚠️ At 10 stars with no forks the author’s background was not verified**. **⑦ ⚠️ Creation and push both fall inside the thaw window**. **⑧ ⚠️ This entry records what was seen on 2026-09-11**. **Verification note**: the repository was read on 2026-09-11 through the repository search endpoint and the GitHub API for stars, licence, language, size, dates and default branch; the 33,514-byte readme was read via `raw.githubusercontent.com` and checked verbatim, **including its performance table, its how-it-works section, its model notes, its prior-art section and its questions**; a licence probe against the root returned 200; **the file listing was read through the trees endpoint, 387 files and 30 directories with truncation false**; **nothing was cloned, no dependency was installed, no command was run, no manifest or imagery was downloaded, no viewer or image was opened, no source or documentation content was read, and no other network observation was made**.

entries.title: **把精算映射接到一个风险评分 API 上**：英国司法部监狱与缓刑服务（HMPPS）的一套 **Kotlin/Spring Boot 风险评分服务**，README 只有 **3,656 字节**却把**先决条件写成一条能跑的命令****——**调 `risk-scores` 之前必须先往 Redis 里初始化罪名代码精算映射**；**同一步骤在生产是一条公开可读的 Kubernetes 定时任务**；**并明说两条本地运行路线哪条推荐****（**Docker「不推荐」／**IntelliJ「推荐」**）
entries.title_en: Wiring actuarial mappings into a risk-scoring API: a Kotlin and Spring Boot risk-scoring service from the UK Ministry of Justice prison and probation service, whose 3,656-byte README states its prerequisite as a command you can actually run, shows the same step automated in production by a public Kubernetes CronJob, and takes a side on which local run route to use, marking the Docker route as not recommended and the IntelliJ route as recommended.
entries.title_hk: **把精算映射接到一個風險評分 API 上**：英國司法部監獄與緩刑服務（HMPPS）的一套 **Kotlin/Spring Boot 風險評分服務**，README 只有 **3,656 位元組**卻把**先決條件寫成一條能跑的命令****——**呼叫 `risk-scores` 之前必須先往 Redis 裡初始化罪名代碼精算映射**；**同一步驟在生產是一條公開可讀的 Kubernetes 定時任務**；**並明說兩條本機運行路線哪條推薦****（**Docker「不推薦」／**IntelliJ「推薦」**）
entries.summary: **arns-risk-actuarial-api**（仓库 `ministryofjustice/hmpps-arns-risk-actuarial-api`）**是英国司法部（Ministry of Justice）监狱与缓刑服务 HMPPS 的一套精算风险评分 API**（Kotlin／Spring Boot，**许可 MIT**，**实测 ★1**、**3,897 KB**、**创建 2025-07-04**、**推送 2026-09-07**）。**它在本轮主题里的价值不在算法，而在「接线」被写得多清楚**：**⭐⭐⭐ ①** `risk-scores` 这个端点**依赖另一份状态**（Redis 里的罪名代码精算映射），**README 把这件事写成一条可直接复制的命令**（**逐字**：**先**「**you must first initialise the offence-code actuarial mappings in Redis**」、**再**「**call the `/admin/update-offence-mapping` endpoint (no authentication required)**」）；**而同一动作在生产就是** `helm_deploy` 下的 **Kubernetes CronJob** `get-offence-actuarial-mapping`（**每天 07:00**，用 `alpine/curl` 发一条 POST）**——**那个「无需认证」的设计决定**正是**让集群内一条裸 curl 能成立的前提**；**⭐⭐⭐ ②** **它把「已铺好」与「已通电」分开写**：`helm_deploy` 下 dev／preprod／prod 三个 values 都在、CI 也对三个环境都跑 helm lint，**但 `deploy_preprod` 与 `deploy_prod` 两个 job 在 `pipeline.yml` 里是被注释掉的**，**实际部署只有 dev 一条通路**；**⭐⭐ ③** **它对自己测试里的硬编码陷阱点名**（**逐字**「**you will need to change the hardcoded service URL in the test file**」）；**⭐⭐ ④** **覆盖率是一个数字加一条查缺口的命令**（**逐字**「**We do impose a minimum test coverage of 85%**」＋ `./gradlew koverHtmlReport`）；**⭐⭐ ⑤** **三枚徽章都接在可核查的外部对象上**（**本次实测**：**合规徽章地址本身返回 JSON 且当前为「**MoJ Compliant**」／**「**Pass**」**、**GHCR 镜像地址 200**、**dev 环境的 Swagger UI 返回 403**）。**⚠️ 本次未运行该服务任何一步、未读任何 Kotlin 源码**，故**不主张**任何端点按所述工作，**也不对其评分口径与公平性作任何评价**；**⚠️ ARNS 这个缩写本词条未能展开**（**不猜**）。
entries.summary_hk: **arns-risk-actuarial-api**（倉庫 `ministryofjustice/hmpps-arns-risk-actuarial-api`）**是英國司法部（Ministry of Justice）監獄與緩刑服務 HMPPS 的一套精算風險評分 API**（Kotlin／Spring Boot，**許可 MIT**，**實測 ★1**、**3,897 KB**、**建立 2025-07-04**、**推送 2026-09-07**）。**它在本輪主題裡的價值不在演算法，而在「接線」被寫得多清楚**：**⭐⭐⭐ ①** `risk-scores` 這個端點**依賴另一份狀態**（Redis 裡的罪名代碼精算映射），**README 把這件事寫成一條可直接複製的命令**（**逐字**：**先**「**you must first initialise the offence-code actuarial mappings in Redis**」、**再**「**call the `/admin/update-offence-mapping` endpoint (no authentication required)**」）；**而同一動作在生產就是** `helm_deploy` 下的 **Kubernetes CronJob** `get-offence-actuarial-mapping`（**每天 07:00**，用 `alpine/curl` 發一條 POST）**——**那個「無需認證」的設計決定**正是**讓叢集內一條裸 curl 能成立的前提**；**⭐⭐⭐ ②** **它把「已鋪好」與「已通電」分開寫**：`helm_deploy` 下 dev／preprod／prod 三個 values 都在、CI 也對三個環境都跑 helm lint，**但 `deploy_preprod` 與 `deploy_prod` 兩個 job 在 `pipeline.yml` 裡是被註解掉的**，**實際部署只有 dev 一條通路**；**⭐⭐ ③** **它對自己測試裡的硬編碼陷阱點名**（**逐字**「**you will need to change the hardcoded service URL in the test file**」）；**⭐⭐ ④** **覆蓋率是一個數字加一條查缺口的命令**（**逐字**「**We do impose a minimum test coverage of 85%**」＋ `./gradlew koverHtmlReport`）；**⭐⭐ ⑤** **三枚徽章都接在可核查的外部對象上**（**本次實測**：**合規徽章地址本身回傳 JSON 且目前為「**MoJ Compliant**」／**「**Pass**」**、**GHCR 映像地址 200**、**dev 環境的 Swagger UI 回傳 403**）。**⚠️ 本次未運行該服務任何一步、未讀任何 Kotlin 原始碼**，故**不主張**任何端點按所述工作，**也不對其評分口徑與公平性作任何評價**；**⚠️ ARNS 這個縮寫本詞條未能展開**（**不猜**）。
entries.summary_en: **arns-risk-actuarial-api** (repository `ministryofjustice/hmpps-arns-risk-actuarial-api`) **is an actuarial risk-scoring API from HMPPS, the prison and probation service of the UK Ministry of Justice** (Kotlin and Spring Boot, **licence MIT**, **measured 1 star**, **3,897 KB**, **created 2025-07-04**, **pushed 2026-09-07**). **Its value for this round is not the algorithm but how clearly the wiring is written down**: **1, top** the `risk-scores` endpoint **depends on a separate piece of state**, the offence-code actuarial mappings held in Redis, and **the README states this as a command you can copy**, verbatim: first, that you must first initialise the offence-code actuarial mappings in Redis, and then that you call the `/admin/update-offence-mapping` endpoint, which the README itself marks as requiring no authentication; **in production that same action is a Kubernetes CronJob** named `get-offence-actuarial-mapping` under `helm_deploy`, running daily at 07:00 and issuing one POST with `alpine/curl`, **so the no-authentication design decision is exactly what lets a bare in-cluster curl work**. **2, top** **it separates what is provisioned from what is live**: values files for dev, preprod and prod all exist and CI lints all three, **yet the `deploy_preprod` and `deploy_prod` jobs are commented out in `pipeline.yml`, so only the dev path actually deploys**. **3** **it names the hardcoded trap in its own tests**, verbatim: you will need to change the hardcoded service URL in the test file. **4** **coverage is one number plus one command to find the gap**, verbatim: We do impose a minimum test coverage of 85%, with `./gradlew koverHtmlReport`. **5** **all three badges point at checkable external objects**: measured this round, the compliance badge endpoint returns JSON and currently reads MoJ Compliant and Pass, the GHCR image URL answers 200, and the dev Swagger UI answers 403. **Not run at all this round and no Kotlin source read**, so this entry does not claim any endpoint works as described **and makes no judgement on its scoring methodology or fairness**; **the acronym ARNS is left unexpanded rather than guessed**.
entries.body:
**arns-risk-actuarial-api**（仓库 `ministryofjustice/hmpps-arns-risk-actuarial-api`）**是英国司法部（Ministry of Justice）监狱与缓刑服务 HMPPS 旗下的一套精算风险评分 API**，**语言 Kotlin**、**构建 Spring Boot／Gradle**、**许可 MIT**、**实测 ★1**、**fork 0**、**仓库体量 3,897 KB**、**创建 2025-07-04**、**最后推送 2026-09-07**、**默认分支 `main`**（**均 GitHub API 实测**；**推送在解冻窗口之内，创建在窗口之外**）。**README 实测 3,656 字节**；**仓库经 GitHub API tree 接口实测共 372 条条目（未截断），其中 290 个文件、82 个目录**。本条目属于本轮主题**「接线：把它接到另一套东西上能用为止」**；**本词条认为它是本轮四条里「接线文档」写得最省字的一篇**：**它不说自己多强，只说**先做什么、**少了会怎样、**哪些值是环境相关的**。

**可核实信息（均 README、tree 与 raw 实测）**：**⭐⭐⭐ ① 它把「先决条件」写成一条能跑的命令，而不是一句要求**——**逐字**：**「**Before calling the `risk-scores` endpoint, you must first initialise the offence-code actuarial mappings in Redis.**」**，**紧接着**「**To do this, call the `/admin/update-offence-mapping` endpoint (no authentication required).**」**，**并给出可复制的**「**curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/update-offence-mapping**」**（**小节标题本身就是** `Initialising Offence-Code Actuarial Mappings`**）。**⭐ 本词条认为这是本轮最值得抄的一处**：**它承认了自己有两个状态**（服务进程 + Redis 里的映射），**并把这个先后顺序摆在正文最前面**——**多数 README 会把它塞进「注意事项」或干脆不写，读者会看到 `risk-scores` 返回空结果而不知为何**。**⭐⭐⭐ ② 同一个手工步骤在生产里有一条公开可读的自动化对应物**——`helm_deploy/hmpps-arns-risk-actuarial-api/templates/cron.yaml`（**实测 578 字节**）是一个 **Kubernetes CronJob**：`metadata.name` 为 `get-offence-actuarial-mapping`、`spec.schedule` 为 `0 7 * * *`（**每天 07:00**）、**容器** `name: curl`、**镜像** `image: alpine/curl`、**命令**为 `/bin/sh -c` 执行 `curl -v -f -X POST http://hmpps-arns-risk-actuarial-api/admin/update-offence-mapping`、`restartPolicy: Never`、`concurrencyPolicy: Forbid`、`securityContext.runAsUser: 1000`。**⭐ 四处值得记**：**① ⭐⭐⭐ README 里那一步「手动初始化」与生产里这条定时任务是同一件事**——**读者因此能看出**「本地要手动做的那件事，线上不会忘」**；**② ⭐⭐⭐ 那个「**no authentication required**」不是随手写的**：**它正是**让集群内一条**裸 curl**（**而且 URL 写的是 `http://` 而不是 `https://`**）**能成立的前提**——**认证决定、手工步骤、定时任务三样东西是同一根线上的接头**；**③ ⭐⭐ `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid` 说明它想过重复执行**（**不让两次初始化重叠**）；**④ ⭐⭐ 以 `runAsUser: 1000` 明写非 root**。**⭐⭐ ③ 它把「已铺好」与「已通电」分开写**：`helm_deploy/` 下 **同时存在** `values-dev.yaml`、`values-preprod.yaml`、`values-prod.yaml`，`.github/workflows/pipeline.yml`（**实测 3,616 字节**）的 `helm_lint` job **用 matrix 对 dev／preprod／prod 三个环境都跑 lint**——**但 `build` 之后只接了 `deploy_dev`，紧随其后的 `deploy_preprod`（注释写 **Deploy to pre-production environment**）与 `deploy_prod`（注释写 **Deploy to production environment**）两个 job 整段是被 `#` 前置注释掉的**。**⭐ 本词条认为这是本轮第二条最值得抄的写法**：**它没有把「支持三个环境」写成能力，而是让读者一眼看到**三个模板都在、三个都被 lint、**而只有 dev 通着电**。**⭐⭐ ④ 它点出自己测试脚本里的硬编码陷阱**——**逐字**：**「**If you wish to run the k6 performance tests against a different env you will need to change the hardcoded service URL in the test file.**」**，**且前一段先给出用环境变量的正规形式**「**k6 run -e AUTH_URL=http://localhost:8090/auth/oauth/token -e CLIENT_ID=REPLACE_ME -e CLIENT_SECRET=REPLACE_ME ./k6/performance-test.js**」**并提醒**「**Replace CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET with their actual values!**」**（**⭐ 即**它没有把「可换环境」讲成能力，**而是把「换环境要改哪一行」讲成已知限制**）。**⭐⭐ ⑤ 覆盖率是一个数字加一条查缺口的命令**——**逐字**：**「**We do impose a minimum test coverage of **85%**.**」**，**并给出**「**To generate a report to identify missing coverage, please run: `./gradlew koverHtmlReport`**」**（**⭐ 即**门槛与查缺口的手段成对出现，**而不是只写一个百分比**）。**⭐⭐ ⑥ 三枚徽章都接在可核查的外部对象上**（**本次实测**）：**① 政府 repo-standards 合规徽章**——**它的徽章地址本身就是一个 API**，**返回**「**{"color":"005ea5","label":"MoJ Compliant","labelColor":"0b0c0c","message":"Pass","schemaVersion":1,"style":"for-the-badge"}**」**（**即当前为** Pass**）**；**② GHCR 容器镜像** `https://ghcr.io/ministryofjustice/hmpps-arns-risk-actuarial-api` **返回 200**；**③ Swagger API 文档徽章指向 dev 主机** `https://arns-risk-actuarial-api-dev.hmpps.service.justice.gov.uk/swagger-ui/index.html`，**本次实测返回 403**。**⭐ 即**徽章不是装饰图，**而是接在报告、镜像与在线文档三个外部对象上的指针**——**同时它也暴露了一个常见错觉**：**「**API docs**」这枚徽章看着像公开文档，**实际指向的 dev 主机本次并不对外可读**。**⭐⭐ ⑦ CI 并发里留了一句诚实的因果说明**：`concurrency.group` 写作 `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref == ‘refs/heads/main’ && github.sha || github.ref }}`、`cancel-in-progress` 为 `${{ github.ref != ‘refs/heads/main’ }}`，**而配置文件里逐字写着理由**：「**Note that two pipelines running within a few minutes of each other will cause issues with helm deploying to a namespace, as the second one will not be able to get a lock as a deploy will be in progress.**」**（**⭐ 即**把「为什么这样写」留在配置旁边，**而不是留在某人的记忆里**；**本次逐字引用 YAML 表达式时把原文的 ASCII 直引号写作弓形引号以维持本词条的引号约定，表达式内容未改**）。**⭐ ⑧ 安全扫描是分开的、可数的工作流**：`.github/workflows/` 实测共 7 条，**其中 5 条是安全类**（`security_codeql_actions_scan.yml`、`security_owasp.yml`、`security_snyk_scan.yml`、`security_veracode_pipeline_scan.yml`、`security_veracode_policy_scan.yml`），**另两条是** `pipeline.yml` 与 `deploy_to_env.yml`。**⭐ ⑨ 应用配置本身就是一张接线图**：`src/main/resources/application.yml`（**实测 1,760 字节**）写明 **JWT 用** `jwk-set-uri: ${hmpps-auth.url}/.well-known/jwks.json` **验签**、**注册了一个下游客户端** `manage-offences-api`（`authorization-grant-type: client_credentials`、**token 端点** `${hmpps-auth.url}/oauth/token`）、**Redis `ssl.enabled: true`**、`server.forward-headers-strategy: native` **并给出 tomcat `remoteip` 的**内部代理 CIDR 清单（10/8、192.168/16、169.254/16、127/8、172.16–172.31、::1 等）**以便在反向代理后取到真实客户端 IP**、**`shutdown: graceful`**、**actuator 只暴露** `info, health`（`include: ‘info, health’`）**且健康检查缓存 2000ms、`show-components` 与 `show-details` 都开、`probes.enabled: true`**、**`springdoc.swagger-ui.version` 钉在 `5.32.11`**、**Jackson 日期格式** `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss`、**`spring.http.codecs.max-in-memory-size: 10MB`**。**⭐ ⑩ 本地栈是可读的，并且承认其中一块是替身**：`docker-compose.yml`（**实测 1,530 字节**）里那个名为 `manage-offences-api` 的服务**用的镜像其实是** `rodolpheche/wiremock`，**把仓库内** `./wiremock-manage-offences-api` **挂到** `/home/wiremock`、**以** `-verbose -global-response-templating` **启动**——**即下游在本地是个桩**；**Redis 用** `redis:8-alpine` **且** `ALLOW_EMPTY_PASSWORD=yes`；**三个服务各自的 healthcheck 都是** `bash -c echo > /dev/tcp/localhost/8080`；**HMPPS Auth 挂** `./auth_db` **卷并用 Flyway 位置清单**（**含** `filesystem:/auth_db`），**另把** `APPLICATION_AUTHENTICATION_UI_ALLOWLIST` **设为** `0.0.0.0/0`。**⭐ 即**「本地能跑」不等于「下游真的在那儿」，**它把替身留在明处**。**⭐ ⑪ 部署模板本身不在这个仓库里**：`helm_deploy/README.md`（**实测仅 203 字节**）逐字说 **「**This helm deployment makes use of the generic-service chart**」**并指向外部** `ministryofjustice/hmpps-helm-charts` 的 `charts/generic-service`（**本次实测该 Chart.yaml 返回 200，其 `version` 为 `3.17.5`**）——**⭐ 即**这个仓库只留 values，**接线接到一套组织级共享 chart 上**。**⭐ ⑫ 开发凭据是公开写出来的，用途也写明了**：README 里的 Basic 头 `aG1wcHMtYXJucy1yaXNrLWFjdHVhcmlhbC1hcGktZGV2OnRlc3Qtc2VjcmV0` **本次解码为** `hmpps-arns-risk-actuarial-api-dev:test-secret`，**Postman 授权设置也逐条列出**（OAuth 2.0／**Client Credentials**／**Token URL** `http://localhost:8090/auth/oauth/token`／**Client ID** `hmpps-arns-risk-actuarial-api-dev`／**Secret** `test-secret`／**Send as Basic Auth header**）——**这是一对本地 HMPPS Auth 容器里的开发凭据，不是生产秘密**。

**对 RIAA**：**本条与 [[insurance-governance]]**（**保险治理**）、**[[osfi-ai-risk-controls]]**（**监管机构对 AI 风险控制的要求**）**与 [[continuous-monitoring-ai-risk]]**（**持续监控**）**可并读**——**它给的是一个受监管环境里「评分服务长什么样」的工程样本**；**其公共部门个案评分场景与 [[insurance-fairness]] 讨论的公平性议题相邻，但本词条未作任何对照**；**而「先决条件必须先接线」的写法与 [[underwriting-decision-safety]] 的决策安全主题属同一类顾虑**。

**arns-risk-actuarial-api** (repository `ministryofjustice/hmpps-arns-risk-actuarial-api`) **is an actuarial risk-scoring API belonging to HMPPS, the prison and probation service of the UK Ministry of Justice**, written in **Kotlin** and built on **Spring Boot and Gradle**, **licence MIT**, **measured 1 star**, **0 forks**, **3,897 KB**, **created 2025-07-04**, **last pushed 2026-09-07**, **default branch `main`** (all GitHub API measurements; **the push is inside the thaw window, the creation is outside it**). **The README measures 3,656 bytes**; **the repository measures 372 entries through the GitHub API tree endpoint, untruncated, being 290 files and 82 directories**. This entry belongs to this round theme, **wiring something up until another system can use it**; **this entry considers it the most economical piece of wiring documentation of the round four**: **it does not say how strong it is, only what to do first, what breaks if you skip that, and which values depend on the environment**.

**Verified information, all measured from the README, the tree endpoint and raw fetches**: **1, top: it states its prerequisite as a command you can run rather than as a request** — verbatim, that before calling the `risk-scores` endpoint you must first initialise the offence-code actuarial mappings in Redis, followed by the instruction to call the `/admin/update-offence-mapping` endpoint, which the README itself marks as requiring no authentication, with the copyable line `curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/update-offence-mapping`; the section heading is itself `Initialising Offence-Code Actuarial Mappings`. **This entry considers this the single most copyable thing of the round**: **it admits that it has two states**, the service process and the mappings held in Redis, **and puts that ordering at the very front of the document**, where most READMEs would bury it under caveats or omit it so that a reader sees `risk-scores` return empty results without knowing why. **2, top: the same manual step has a publicly readable automation counterpart in production** — `helm_deploy/hmpps-arns-risk-actuarial-api/templates/cron.yaml`, measured at 578 bytes, is a **Kubernetes CronJob** named `get-offence-actuarial-mapping` whose `spec.schedule` is `0 7 * * *`, daily at 07:00, whose single container is named `curl`, uses the image `alpine/curl`, and runs `/bin/sh -c` with `curl -v -f -X POST http://hmpps-arns-risk-actuarial-api/admin/update-offence-mapping`, with `restartPolicy: Never`, `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid` and `securityContext.runAsUser: 1000`. **Two things worth recording**: first, **the step the README has you do by hand and this production CronJob are the same action**, so a reader can see that what is manual locally will not be forgotten online; second, **the no-authentication line is not incidental** — it is exactly what lets a bare in-cluster curl work, and the URL it calls is plain `http://`, so the authentication decision, the manual step and the scheduled job are connectors on one wire. **3: it separates what is provisioned from what is live** — `helm_deploy/` carries `values-dev.yaml`, `values-preprod.yaml` and `values-prod.yaml` side by side, and the `helm_lint` job in `.github/workflows/pipeline.yml`, measured at 3,616 bytes, lints all three environments through a matrix, **yet after `build` only `deploy_dev` is connected: the `deploy_preprod` and `deploy_prod` jobs, commented as the pre-production and production deployment jobs, are commented out with leading `#` characters**. So all three templates exist, all three are linted, and only dev has power running through it. **4: it names the hardcoded trap in its own tests** — verbatim, that if you wish to run the k6 performance tests against a different env you will need to change the hardcoded service URL in the test file, preceded by the proper environment-variable form of the k6 command and the reminder to replace CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET with their actual values; **rather than presenting environment-portability as a feature, it presents the exact line you must edit for another environment as a known limitation**. **5: coverage is one number plus one command to find the gap** — verbatim, that a minimum test coverage of **85%** is imposed, with the instruction to run `./gradlew koverHtmlReport` to generate a report identifying missing coverage. **6: all three badges point at checkable external objects**, as measured this round: **the repo-standards compliance badge endpoint is itself an API returning `{"color":"005ea5","label":"MoJ Compliant","labelColor":"0b0c0c","message":"Pass","schemaVersion":1,"style":"for-the-badge"}`, currently reading Pass**; **the GHCR image URL `https://ghcr.io/ministryofjustice/hmpps-arns-risk-actuarial-api` answers 200**; **and the Swagger API docs badge points at the dev host `https://arns-risk-actuarial-api-dev.hmpps.service.justice.gov.uk/swagger-ui/index.html`, which answered 403 this round**. So a badge is not decoration but a pointer wired to a report, an image and live documentation, **and it also exposes a common illusion: a badge labelled API docs looks like public documentation while the dev host behind it was not publicly readable this round**. **7: the CI concurrency block keeps an honest causal note next to the configuration**, verbatim: that two pipelines running within a few minutes of each other will cause issues with helm deploying to a namespace, as the second one will not be able to get a lock as a deploy will be in progress; the group expression uses the commit SHA on main and cancels in progress elsewhere. **This round the ASCII quotation marks of the original YAML expressions were rendered as curved quotation marks to keep this entry quote convention, with the expressions themselves unchanged.** **8: the security scans are separate, countable workflows** — `.github/workflows/` holds seven, five of them security-related: a CodeQL actions scan, OWASP, Snyk, a Veracode pipeline scan and a Veracode policy scan, alongside `pipeline.yml` and `deploy_to_env.yml`. **9: the application configuration is itself a wiring diagram** — `src/main/resources/application.yml`, measured at 1,760 bytes, verifies JWTs against `${hmpps-auth.url}/.well-known/jwks.json`, registers a downstream client named `manage-offences-api` with `authorization-grant-type: client_credentials` and a token endpoint at `${hmpps-auth.url}/oauth/token`, enables Redis SSL, sets `server.forward-headers-strategy: native` with an explicit tomcat `remoteip` list of internal proxy ranges so the real client address survives a reverse proxy, enables graceful shutdown, exposes only `info` and `health` on actuator with a 2000 ms health cache, `show-components` and `show-details` both on and probes enabled, pins `springdoc.swagger-ui.version` at `5.32.11`, sets the Jackson date format and allows ten megabytes in memory per codec. **10: the local stack is readable, and admits that one piece of it is a stand-in** — in `docker-compose.yml`, measured at 1,530 bytes, the service named `manage-offences-api` actually runs the image `rodolpheche/wiremock`, mounting the in-repo `wiremock-manage-offences-api` directory at `/home/wiremock` and starting with `-verbose -global-response-templating`, so the downstream dependency is a stub locally; Redis is `redis:8-alpine` with empty passwords allowed; each healthcheck is a bash probe of the TCP port; and HMPPS Auth mounts an `auth_db` volume with a Flyway locations list. **Being runnable locally does not mean the downstream service is really there, and it keeps the stand-in in plain sight.** **11: the deployment templates are not in this repository** — `helm_deploy/README.md`, measured at only 203 bytes, says verbatim that this helm deployment makes use of the generic-service chart and points to `charts/generic-service` in the external `ministryofjustice/hmpps-helm-charts` repository, whose `Chart.yaml` answered 200 with `version` `3.17.5` this round; **this repository keeps only the values and wires into an organisation-wide shared chart**. **12: the development credentials are published, and their purpose is stated** — the Basic header in the README decodes this round to `hmpps-arns-risk-actuarial-api-dev:test-secret`, with the Postman authorization settings listed field by field: **these are development credentials for a local HMPPS Auth container, not a production secret**.

**For RIAA**: **this entry reads alongside [[insurance-governance]]**, **[[osfi-ai-risk-controls]]** and **[[continuous-monitoring-ai-risk]]**, since **it is an engineering sample of what a scoring service looks like inside a regulated environment**; **its public-sector individual-level scoring context sits next to the fairness questions discussed under [[insurance-fairness]], but no comparison was made here**; **and its insistence that the prerequisite be wired first belongs to the same family of concerns as the decision-safety theme of [[underwriting-decision-safety]]**.

**Marked honestly by this entry**: **first, no part of it was run this round** — no JDK or Gradle installed, no compose stack started, no token obtained, no call to `risk-scores` or `/admin/update-offence-mapping`, no k6 run and no coverage report, **so this entry does not claim that any endpoint works as described, nor that the 85% coverage figure currently holds**, since that number is the README own statement and was not reproduced. **Second, no Kotlin source was read** — of the 372 tree entries this round only `README.md`, `src/main/resources/application.yml`, `docker-compose.yml`, the CronJob template, `helm_deploy/README.md` and `.github/workflows/pipeline.yml` were fetched, together with a directory listing, **so this entry does not claim anything about the inputs and outputs of `risk-scores`, its scoring methodology, algorithms, data sources or how the offence mapping is built**. **This is the item most in need of later verification: this is a real judicial and probation risk-scoring service, and its scoring methodology, contributing factors and fairness impact were not examined at all — nothing here should be used to judge its conclusions, its uses or its social impact; this entry records engineering wiring only and does not endorse its application.** **Third, the acronym ARNS is left unexpanded**: `application.yml` names the application `HMPPS Arns Risk Actuarial Api` and neither the README, nor `helm_deploy/README.md`, nor the directory listing spells ARNS out, and since no source was read the possibility of an expansion inside the code cannot be excluded, **so it is not guessed**. **Fourth, two badge targets did not answer this round**: the dev Swagger host answered 403, and the human-readable page for the compliance report answered 400, with only the badge API answering 200 and Pass, **so this entry claims only that the badge API path was readable, not that the report page is**. **Fifth, regarding the admin endpoint that needs no authentication**, this entry only relays the two verbatim statements and points out that they depend on each other; **no request was ever sent to any address this round and no cluster network policy was examined, so no security judgement is offered**. **Sixth, the licence file contents were not checked** (the GitHub field says MIT but the `LICENSE` text was not read), the current maintenance state of the `rodolpheche/wiremock` image was not checked, and neither `build.gradle.kts`, which was not read, nor the Java version setting was reconciled against the rest of the build. **Seventh, one star and zero forks: its production reach, the number of people affected and whether it informs real individual decisions were not verified, nor was the background of its authors.** **Eighth, this entry records what was visible on 2026-09-11**; **the creation date is outside the thaw window while the push is inside it, and the named gap that justifies the exception is that a government-published actuarial risk-scoring API in a judicial and probation setting had no counterpart in the pool** — the pooled `insurerisk`, `paco-uw` and `underwriting-decision-safety` entries all belong to insurance or underwriting rather than to public-sector individual risk scoring.

entries.title: **精算包的「接线层」本身**：JuliaActuary 的 **FinanceCore.jl**——**它明说「你不该直接用我」**，**并列出「谁再导出我、再导出什么」**；**实测只有两个依赖**、**用 Julia 的 `ext/` 扩展机制把 LoopVectorization 接成可选加速**、**CI 里另有一条 `downgrade` 任务专门把 `[compat]` 里声明的最低版本真的装起来跑一遍**
entries.title_en: The wiring layer of an actuarial package family: FinanceCore.jl from JuliaActuary, which states plainly that users should generally not use it directly, lists exactly which packages re-export which of its types and functions, carries only two hard dependencies, wires LoopVectorization in as optional acceleration through the Julia package extension mechanism, and runs a dedicated downgrade CI job that actually installs and tests the lower version bounds declared in its compat section.
entries.title_hk: **精算包的「接線層」本身**：JuliaActuary 的 **FinanceCore.jl**——**它明說「你不該直接用我」**，**並列出「誰再導出我、再導出什麼」**；**實測只有兩個依賴**、**用 Julia 的 `ext/` 擴展機制把 LoopVectorization 接成可選加速**、**CI 裡另有一條 `downgrade` 任務專門把 `[compat]` 裡聲明的最低版本真的裝起來跑一遍**
entries.summary: **FinanceCore.jl**（仓库 `JuliaActuary/FinanceCore.jl`）**是 JuliaActuary 精算包家族的最底层包**，**版本 2.7.0**、**许可 MIT**、**实测 ★3**、**998 KB**、**创建 2022-06-14**、**推送 2026-09-08**。**它在本轮主题里的价值是「接线」的**另一种样子**：**它自己不面向终端用户，而是被别人再导出**。**⭐⭐⭐ ①** 它逐字写出**「**Users should generally prefer to use other JuliaActuary packages which will re-export the FinanceCore data/methods as necessary.**」**，**并只留两个例外**（**逐字**「**If you are extending a function or type as a user or developer, then it would be a good idea to import/use this package directly.**」）**——**⭐ 即**它把「什么时候该直接依赖我」写成一条判据**；**⭐⭐⭐ ②** **它把「谁拿走了什么」分成三节列清**（**Reexported by ActuaryUtilities.jl**：`irr`、`internal_rate_of_return`；**Reexported by FinanceModels.jl**：`Rate`／`Frequency`、`discount`／`accumulation`／`forward`；**Used by multiple packages**：`Cashflow`／`Quote`、`amount`／`timepoint`、`present_value`／`pv`）**——**⭐ 即**一个底层包的 README 最该回答的是「**别人从我这里拿走了什么**」，**而不是「我有什么」**；**⭐⭐⭐ ③** **它用 Julia 的扩展机制接可选依赖**：`[weakdeps] LoopVectorization`、`[extensions] FinanceCoreLoopVectorizationExt = "LoopVectorization"`、`ext/FinanceCoreLoopVectorizationExt.jl` **实测存在**，**并通过包内私有函数** `FinanceCore._vectorization_backend(...)` **挂上去**——**⭐ 并逐字写明两条数值限制**（「**Reassociation and LoopVectorization’s exp may differ from the SIMD result by approximately one ulp.**」／「**The public IRR solver currently seeds Newton iteration with a Float64, so its Float32 cashflow path falls back to SIMD.**」）；**⭐⭐⭐ ④** **CI 里有一条任务专门跑 `[compat]` 的最低版本**（`downgrade` job，**逐字注释**「**Tests the lower bounds declared in [compat] by pinning dependencies to their oldest allowed versions before building.**」）**——**声明的兼容范围不是口号，**而是被一条会失败的测试接住了**；**⭐⭐ ⑤** **格式检查与 `git blame` 是一对**（CI 有 `runic` job，仓库根 `.git-blame-ignore-revs` 里逐字是注释 `# Adding Runic formatting` 加三个 40 位提交号）。**⚠️ 本次未安装 Julia、未运行或测试该包、未读 `src/` 任何文件**，故**不主张**任何函数或类型的签名与数值行为；**⚠️ `[deps]` 实测只有 `Dates` 与 `Roots` 两个**。

entries.summary_en: **FinanceCore.jl** (repository `JuliaActuary/FinanceCore.jl`) **is the lowest layer of the JuliaActuary actuarial package family**, at **version 2.7.0**, **licence MIT**, **measured 3 stars**, **998 KB**, **created 2022-06-14**, **pushed 2026-09-08**. **Its value for this round is a different shape of wiring: it does not face end users at all, it is re-exported by others.** **First, top** it says verbatim that users should generally prefer to use other JuliaActuary packages which will re-export the FinanceCore data and methods as necessary, **and leaves exactly two exceptions**, verbatim: if you are extending a function or type as a user or developer, then it would be a good idea to import or use this package directly, **so it states when you should depend on it directly as a criterion rather than a preference**. **Second, top** **it lists who took what, in three sections**: `irr` and `internal_rate_of_return` re-exported by ActuaryUtilities.jl; `Rate` and `Frequency`, plus `discount`, `accumulation` and `forward`, re-exported by FinanceModels.jl; and `Cashflow` and `Quote`, the `amount` and `timepoint` accessors, and `present_value` and `pv` used by multiple packages, **which means the README of a low-level package answers who takes what from it rather than what it contains**. **Third, top** **it wires an optional dependency through the Julia package extension mechanism**: `[weakdeps] LoopVectorization`, an `[extensions]` entry naming `FinanceCoreLoopVectorizationExt`, and a measurably present `ext/FinanceCoreLoopVectorizationExt.jl`, **hooked in through a package-private function** named `FinanceCore._vectorization_backend`, with two numerical limits stated verbatim: that reassociation and the LoopVectorization exponential may differ from the SIMD result by approximately one ulp, and that the public IRR solver currently seeds Newton iteration with a Float64 so its Float32 cashflow path falls back to SIMD. **Fourth, top** **a CI job exists purely to run the lowest versions declared in the compat section**, the `downgrade` job, with the verbatim comment that it tests the lower bounds declared in the compat section by pinning dependencies to their oldest allowed versions before building, **so a declared compatibility range is not a claim but something a failing test is wired to**. **Fifth** **formatting and blame form a pair**: CI runs a `runic` job and the repository root carries a blame-ignore file whose contents are, verbatim, the comment about adding Runic formatting followed by three full forty-character commit hashes. **Julia was not installed this round, the package was neither run nor tested, and no file under `src/` was read**, so this entry makes no claim about the signature or numerical behaviour of any function or type; **the measured hard dependencies are exactly two, `Dates` and `Roots`**.
entries.body:
**FinanceCore.jl**（仓库 `JuliaActuary/FinanceCore.jl`）**是 JuliaActuary 精算包家族的最底层包**，**版本 2.7.0**（`Project.toml` 实测 `version = "2.7.0"`，**注册身份** `uuid = "b9b1ffdd-6612-4b69-8227-7663be06e089"`）、**语言 Julia**、**许可 MIT**、**实测 ★3**、**仓库体量 998 KB**、**创建 2022-06-14**、**最后推送 2026-09-08**、**默认分支 `main`**；**README 实测 1,457 字节**。**文件清单本次经 `codeload.github.com` 的 tarball 枚举**（**本轮 GitHub 核心 API 配额已用尽**），**实测 30 条路径，其中 7 个目录、23 个文件**：`src/` 下 `FinanceCore.jl`、`Contracts.jl`、`irr.jl`、`pv.jl`、`Rates.jl`；`test/` 下 `runtests.jl`、`contracts.jl`、`irr.jl`、`present_value.jl`、`Rates.jl` 与 `Project.toml`；`docs/` 下 `make.jl`、`Project.toml`、`src/index.md`；`ext/FinanceCoreLoopVectorizationExt.jl`；`.github/workflows/` 下 `CI.yml`、`CompatHelper.yml`、`TagBot.yml`；**另有** `Project.toml`、`LICENSE`、`README.md`、`.gitignore`、`.git-blame-ignore-revs`。本条目属于本轮主题**「接线：把它接到另一套东西上能用为止」**；**本词条认为它是本轮四条里唯一一条**把「接线」讲在**依赖关系层面**的**：**它自己就是那条被接的线**。

**可核实信息（均 README、`Project.toml`、`ext/` 文件、`CI.yml`、`.git-blame-ignore-revs` 与文件清单实测）**：**⭐⭐⭐ ① 它明说「你不该直接用我」，并只留两个例外**——**正文逐字**：**「**This repository contains foundational types and routines that are used in other packages.**」**，**紧接**「**Users should generally prefer to use other JuliaActuary packages which will re-export the FinanceCore data/methods as necessary.**」**，**再给出例外**：**「**If you are extending a function or type as a user or developer, then it would be a good idea to import/use this package directly.**」**。**⭐ 本词条认为这是本轮值得抄的一处**：**一个底层包最好的文档不是「我能做什么」，而是**「你应该用哪一层、以及什么情况下才该下到我这一层」**——**它把读者往上游推，而不是把使用者留在自己这里**。**⭐⭐⭐ ② 它把「谁拿走了什么」分成三节列清**——**逐字三个小节标题与条目**：**「**Reexported by ActuaryUtilities.jl**」**：`irr` 与 `internal_rate_of_return`；**「**Reexported by FinanceModels.jl**」**：`Rate`s 与 `Frequency`s，以及 `discount`、`accumulation`、`forward` 三个函数；**「**Used by multiple packages**」**：`Cashflow` 与 `Quote` 两个类型、`amount` 与 `timepoint` 两个访问器、`present_value` 与 `pv` 两个函数。**⭐ 即**这份清单回答的是**别人从我这里拿走了什么、又从哪条路径拿**——**这正是「接线图」在包管理层面的样子**：**它不描述自己，它描述自己与上层的关系**。**⭐⭐⭐ ③ 它用 Julia 的扩展机制把可选依赖接成加速后端**——`Project.toml` 实测：`[weakdeps]` 下 `LoopVectorization = "bdcacae8-1622-11e9-2a5c-532679323890"`，`[extensions]` 下 `FinanceCoreLoopVectorizationExt = "LoopVectorization"`，**对应文件** `ext/FinanceCoreLoopVectorizationExt.jl` **实测存在**。**⭐ 四处值得记**：**① ⭐⭐⭐ 扩展是用一条「私有函数」挂上去的**——**文件里逐字为** `FinanceCore._vectorization_backend(r::T, cashflows::StridedVector{T}, times::TurboTimes{T})`，**即**函数名带**前导下划线**（**Julia 社区用下划线表示内部实现**），**并重定义了** `FinanceCore.__pv_div_pv′`（**名字末尾是一个 U+2032 PRIME 字符，不是撇号**）；**⭐ 本词条如实指出**这是一种**约定式接线**：**扩展点没有写进公开 API，而是靠包内私有名字**——**本词条不评价其优劣**，**但把它记下来**，**因为下划线名字在语义上并没有稳定性承诺**。**② ⭐⭐⭐ 它把两个后端的数值差异量化了**——**文件内注释逐字**：**「**Reassociation and LoopVectorization’s exp may differ from the SIMD result by approximately one ulp.**」**——**即**「**快的那条路算出来的结果与慢的那条不完全相同，差多少也写明了**」**；**⭐ 本词条认为这比「我们会自动加速」有用得多**：**加速是有代价的，代价写在旁边**。**③ ⭐⭐⭐ 同一文件还写明一条能力边界**——**逐字**：**「**The public IRR solver currently seeds Newton iteration with a Float64, so its Float32 cashflow path falls back to SIMD. Float32 remains valid for direct and future type-preserving solver calls.**」**——**即**它承认 **Float32 路径目前回落到 SIMD**，**同时又说明 Float32 在直接调用与未来类型保持的求解器调用里仍然有效**：**一处限制 + 一处仍然成立的范围**。**④ ⭐⭐ 它还留了一条「为什么这么写」的注释**——**逐字**：**「**The public IRR solver currently seeds Newton iteration with a Float64**」**里的 **currently** 一词**即**「这是当下的实现状态，不是设计约束」**。**⭐⭐⭐ ④ CI 里有一条任务专门跑 `[compat]` 里声明的最低版本**——`CI.yml`（**实测 3,616 字节级别以外的另一份文件，本次从 tarball 直读**）的 `downgrade` job 用 `julia-actions/julia-downgrade-compat@v1`、**参数** `skip: Dates` 与 `strict: ‘true’`，**并逐字注释两处理由**：**「**Tests the lower bounds declared in [compat] by pinning dependencies to their oldest allowed versions before building.**」**与**「**exact "=floor" pins for every entry, incl. >=1.0 (default v0 tilde-pins those)**」。**⭐ 本词条认为这是本轮最硬的一处**：**`[compat]` 里写的 `Roots = "1.0.12, 2"`、`LoopVectorization = "0.12.166"`、`julia = "1.10"` 通常只是声明**，**而这个仓库把「下界仍然可用」接到了一条会失败的测试上**——**声明的兼容范围因此变成可核查的东西**（**本次逐字引用该注释时把原文的 ASCII 直引号写作弓形引号以维持本词条的引号约定，注释内容未改**）。**⭐⭐ ⑤ 格式检查与 `git blame` 是一对**：CI 有 `runic` job（`uses: fredrikekre/runic-action@v1`，`with: version: ‘1’`），**而仓库根有** `.git-blame-ignore-revs`，**内容逐字是一行注释加三个提交号**——**注释为** `# Adding Runic formatting`，**三个提交号为** `288af3220d7e8e4506eda62d26091c97dec58102`、`0ce7dc006ac89a7184da17267fc17d530e5e3c7a`、`def34a8b2dcc09ffcd17ebcdd5a65c43bd034e2f`。**⭐ 即**「**格式检查**」与「**让 `git This entry belongs to this round theme, **wiring something up until another system can use it**; **this entry considers it the only one of the round four that discusses wiring at the level of dependency relationships, since it is itself the wire being plugged into**.

**Verified information, all measured from the README, `Project.toml`, the extension file, `CI.yml`, the blame-ignore file and the file listing**: **first, top: it states that you should generally not use it directly, and leaves exactly two exceptions** — verbatim, that the repository contains foundational types and routines used in other packages, followed by the statement that users should generally prefer to use other JuliaActuary packages which will re-export the FinanceCore data and methods as necessary, and then the exception, that if you are extending a function or type as a user or developer, then it would be a good idea to import or use this package directly. **The best documentation a low-level package can offer is not what it can do but which layer you should be using and when you should come down to this one**, and it pushes readers upstream rather than keeping users for itself. **Second, top: it lists who took what, in three sections** — the verbatim headings being that `irr` and `internal_rate_of_return` are re-exported by ActuaryUtilities.jl; that `Rate`s and `Frequency`s together with `discount`, `accumulation` and `forward` are re-exported by FinanceModels.jl; and that `Cashflow` and `Quote`, the `amount` and `timepoint` accessors, and `present_value` and `pv` are used by multiple packages. **So the listing answers who takes what from it and by which path, which is what a wiring diagram looks like at the package-management level: it does not describe itself, it describes its relationships upward.** **Third, top: it wires an optional dependency in as an acceleration backend through the Julia extension mechanism** — measured in `Project.toml`: `[weakdeps]` carries `LoopVectorization`, `[extensions]` maps `FinanceCoreLoopVectorizationExt` to `LoopVectorization`, and the corresponding file is measurably present under `ext/`. **Four things worth recording**: first, **the extension hooks in through a package-private function**, verbatim `FinanceCore._vectorization_backend(...)`, whose name carries a leading underscore, and it also redefines `FinanceCore.__pv_div_pv′`, whose name ends in a U+2032 prime character rather than an apostrophe; **this entry records honestly that this is a conventional rather than contractual attachment, since the extension point is not part of the public API but an in-package private name, and no judgement of its merits is offered here, though an underscore name carries no semantic stability promise and that is worth writing down**. Second, **it quantifies the numerical difference between the two backends**, verbatim: that reassociation and the LoopVectorization exponential may differ from the SIMD result by approximately one ulp, **which is far more useful than a promise of automatic acceleration, because the cost of going faster is written next to it**. Third, **the same file states a capability boundary**, verbatim: that the public IRR solver currently seeds Newton iteration with a Float64 so its Float32 cashflow path falls back to SIMD, and that Float32 remains valid for direct and future type-preserving solver calls, **one limitation plus one range that still holds**. Fourth, **it keeps a note about why the code looks like this**: the word currently in that sentence means the state of the implementation today rather than a design constraint. **Fourth, top: a CI job exists purely to run the lowest versions declared in the compat section** — the `downgrade` job uses `julia-actions/julia-downgrade-compat@v1` with `skip: Dates` and `strict: ‘true’`, and carries two verbatim comments: that it tests the lower bounds declared in the compat section by pinning dependencies to their oldest allowed versions before building, and that the exact equality-to-floor pins apply to every entry including those declared with a greater-or-equal bound, which the default version-zero behaviour would tilde-pin instead. **Lower bounds in a compat section are usually only a claim, and this repository wires the claim that the lower bound still works to a test that can fail, which makes the declared compatibility range checkable.** **This round the ASCII quotation marks of the original comments were rendered as curved quotation marks to keep this entry quote convention, with the comments themselves unchanged.** **Fifth: formatting and blame form a pair** — CI runs a `runic` job through `fredrikekre/runic-action@v1`, and the repository root carries a blame-ignore file whose contents are, verbatim, the comment about adding Runic formatting followed by three commit hashes: `288af3220d7e8e4506eda62d26091c97dec58102`, `0ce7dc006ac89a7184da17267fc17d530e5e3c7a` and `def34a8b2dcc09ffcd17ebcdd5a65c43bd034e2f`. **A formatting check and a blame ignore list are two halves of the same thing: adding a formatter pollutes the history, and this wires that pollution back out of blame.** **This round all three hashes were checked to be complete forty-character hexadecimal values.** **Sixth: the dependency surface is minimal** — `[deps]` measures exactly two entries, `Dates` and `Roots`, while `[compat]` additionally pins `Dates` to major version one, `Roots` to `1.0.12, 2`, `LoopVectorization` to `0.12.166` and Julia itself to `1.10`; **a package that many others depend on keeps two hard dependencies and puts acceleration behind a weak one, because the thinner the wiring layer the more packages can attach to it**. **Seventh: the test matrix spans three operating systems and four version labels** — ubuntu with the minimum supported version, ubuntu with version one, macOS, Windows and ubuntu with the pre-release version, **where the pre-release cell allows failure without turning the main status red** and fail-fast is disabled; coverage is produced into an lcov file and handed to Codecov with a token from secrets. **The minimum-supported cell and the pre-release cell each get their own slot with a different consequence for failure: one must pass and the other may not.** **Eighth: it also wires in two pieces of Julia ecosystem automation** — the three measured workflows are CI, CompatHelper, which opens pull requests when dependency compatibility bounds need raising, and TagBot, which tags releases after registration. **Ninth: five badges, all pointing at checkable objects** — stable and dev documentation, CI restricted to the main branch, Codecov, and an Aqua QA badge pointing at `JuliaTesting/Aqua.jl`. **Aqua is a tool in the Julia ecosystem for automated package quality consistency checks, but its checklist was not examined this round, so this entry does not describe what it checks.** **Tenth: the wiring to pooled entries** — this entry supplies the layer that `[[actuaryutilities-jl]]` and `[[financemodels-jl]]` both depend on, and adds a family dependency edge to `[[experienceanalysis-jl]]`, `[[mortalitytables-jl]]`, `[[lifecontingencies-jl]]`, `[[economicscenariogenerators-jl]]`, `[[hmd-jl]]`, `[[copulas-jl]]` and `[[conformalprediction-jl]]`; against libraries such as `[[quantlib]]`, `[[financepy]]` and `[[yieldcurves]]`, which ship complete implementations, this entry records the opposite design choice of lifting shared types to the bottom and letting the upper layers re-export them.

**For RIAA**: **this entry reads alongside [[actuaryutilities-jl]] and [[financemodels-jl]]**, because **it is the smallest available sample of how an open actuarial family is layered**: types and shared arithmetic at the bottom, re-export upward, acceleration behind a weak dependency, and a CI job that actually installs the declared minimum versions.

**Marked honestly by this entry**: **first, Julia was not installed, and the package was neither run nor tested** — nothing was instantiated, no test file was executed and no function was called — **so this entry does not claim that any function or type works as described, nor any performance or numerical conclusion**. **Second, no file under `src/` was read**: only the README, `Project.toml`, the extension file, `CI.yml`, the blame-ignore file and a complete file listing were read, **so this entry claims nothing about the signatures, return types, numerical behaviour, precision or convergence properties of `irr`, `pv`, `Rate`, `Cashflow` or any other API — this is the item most in need of later verification**. **Third, the Aqua checklist, the current Codecov percentage and whether CompatHelper and TagBot are still running were not verified, and the documentation site was not opened.** **Fourth, the risk this entry points out is not a conclusion**: the extension attaches through a private function with a leading underscore, and whether that name survives later versions was not verified; **this entry records the fact only and makes no judgement about its stability**. **Fifth, the file listing came from a tarball rather than the GitHub tree endpoint**, since the core API quota was exhausted, **so the counts of 23 files and 7 directories are tarball figures**; whether documentation outside the README exists but was not read was not established. **Sixth, three stars: forks, download counts and whether the registry copy is current were not checked**, nor was the maintainer background or activity. **Seventh, the creation date of 2022-06-14 is outside the thaw window while the push of 2026-09-08 is inside it**, and following the project convention that a window exception must name a gap, **the gap here is that the layer of packages which exist to be re-exported upward had no entry of its own in the pool**, even though `[[actuaryutilities-jl]]` and `[[financemodels-jl]]` were both already there. **Eighth, this entry records what was visible on 2026-09-11, and version 2.7.0 is the value of `Project.toml` on that date.** **9, quotation convention**: **when quoting that comment verbatim this entry renders the ASCII apostrophe in `LoopVectorization’s exp` as a curved apostrophe to keep the convention that this entry contains no ASCII single quote; the comment text is otherwise unchanged.**
