entries.title: **同一门课的两种形态，以及「答案在到期前不出来」的机制**：索邦大学 **M2 Actuariat** 气候风险课程材料——**五讲 × 两小时**，**每讲同时提供**学生版**（`SessionX_compact.pdf`）**与**演示版**（`SessionX_extended.pdf`，**逐条揭示、**新出现的那条高亮**）；**⭐⭐⭐ 而它的作业答案被**加密后提交进仓库**，**由一条每 5 分钟运行的 GitHub Action **到期自动解密发布**；**⭐ 参考文献里有**IAIS 的 AI 与气候监管文件**与**NGFS 情景****
entries.title_en: One course in two forms, plus a mechanism for keeping answers out of sight until they are due: climate risk materials for a Master 2 Actuarial Science programme at Sorbonne University, five two-hour sessions each published in a student version and a presentation version whose bullets are revealed one at a time with the newest highlighted, and coursework answers stored encrypted in the repository and decrypted and published automatically at their due time by a GitHub Action that runs every five minutes, with a reading list that includes the insurance supervisors climate guidance and the central banks climate scenarios.
entries.title_hk: **同一門課的兩種形態，以及「答案在到期前不出來」的機制**：索邦大學 **M2 Actuariat** 氣候風險課程材料——**五講 × 兩小時**，**每講同時提供**學生版**與**演示版**；**⭐⭐⭐ 而它的作業答案被**加密後提交進倉庫**，**由一條每 5 分鐘運行的 GitHub Action **到期自動解密發布**；**⭐ 參考文獻裡有**IAIS 的氣候監管文件**與**NGFS 情景****
entries.summary: **sorbonne-climate-risks**（`Vermandel/sorbonne-climate-risks`）**是索邦大学 **M2 Actuariat（精算硕士）**「气候风险」课程的**转型风险**部分材料**（**逐字为**「**cinq séances de deux heures**」**，**作者** Gauthier Vermandel**）**，**逐字说明它讲的是**「**la chaîne qui relie les politiques climatiques et l’activité économique aux émissions, à la température, aux entreprises, aux actifs financiers et aux décisions d’assurance**」。**本条目属于本轮主题**「同源多形」**，**它在两端都给样本**：**⭐⭐⭐ ① 同一门课、两种形态**——**每讲逐字提供两种**同步**格式**：`SessionX_compact.pdf` **为**« la version de référence destinée aux étudiant·es »**，`SessionX_extended.pdf` **为演示版并逐字说明**「**Ses puces sont révélées une à une et la puce nouvellement révélée est mise en évidence**」**；**⭐⭐⭐ ② 答案在到期前不出现在仓库里**——**这套机制逐字叫**「**Publication synchronisée des corrigés（PSC）**」：**每个未来的答案以**加密形式**保存**（`publication/encrypted/*.ipynb.gpg`**）**，**由一条 GitHub Action 在**`publication/releases.json` 里指定的时刻**解密并发布**；**⭐ 工作流实测**每 5 分钟跑一次**（`cron: "*/5 * * * *"`**）**，**清单里逐字给出时区** `Europe/Paris` **与** `lead_minutes: 15`**；**⭐⭐ ③ 教学材料里点名了**读情景的正确姿势**——**逐字**「**Interpréter les scénarios comme des trajectoires conditionnelles plutôt que comme des prévisions ou des probabilités**」**；**⭐⭐ ④ 参考文献是一份**精算监管向书单****（**含** GIEC AR6、**NGFS 2024、**TCFD 2017、**IAIS 2021 关于气候相关风险监管的应用文件、**Nordhaus 2017 社会碳成本、**McNeil／Frey／Embrechts 2015**）**。**⚠️ 本次未运行任何 notebook、**未读任何 PDF、**未解密任何答案**（**私钥只在 GitHub secret 里**）**。
entries.summary_hk: **sorbonne-climate-risks**（`Vermandel/sorbonne-climate-risks`）**是索邦大學 **M2 Actuariat（精算碩士）**「氣候風險」課程的**轉型風險**部分材料**（**逐字為**「**cinq séances de deux heures**」**）**，**逐字說明它講的是**「**la chaîne qui relie les politiques climatiques et l’activité économique aux émissions, à la température, aux entreprises, aux actifs financiers et aux décisions d’assurance**」。**本條目屬於本輪主題**「同源多形」**：**⭐⭐⭐ ① 同一門課、兩種形態**——**每講逐字提供兩種**同步**格式**（`SessionX_compact.pdf` **為學生版參考**；`SessionX_extended.pdf` **為演示版**，**逐字**「**Ses puces sont révélées une à une et la puce nouvellement révélée est mise en évidence**」**）**；**⭐⭐⭐ ② 答案在到期前不出現在倉庫裡**——**機制逐字叫**「**Publication synchronisée des corrigés（PSC）**」：**答案以**加密形式**保存**（`publication/encrypted/*.ipynb.gpg`**）**，**由 GitHub Action 在**`publication/releases.json` 指定的時刻**解密並發布**；**工作流每 5 分鐘跑一次**（`cron: "*/5 * * * *"`**）**，**清單逐字給出時區** `Europe/Paris` **與** `lead_minutes: 15`**；**⭐⭐ ③ 逐字教讀情景的正確姿勢**（**「**Interpréter les scénarios comme des trajectoires conditionnelles plutôt que comme des prévisions ou des probabilités**」**）**；**⭐⭐ ④ 參考文獻是一份**精算監管向書單****（**GIEC AR6、NGFS 2024、TCFD 2017、IAIS 2021、Nordhaus 2017、McNeil／Frey／Embrechts 2015**）**。**⚠️ 本次未運行任何 notebook、未讀任何 PDF、未解密任何答案**。
entries.summary_en: The repository `Vermandel/sorbonne-climate-risks` **holds the transition risk materials for a climate risk course in a Master 2 actuarial programme at Sorbonne University**, five two-hour sessions taught and written by Gauthier Vermandel, and described verbatim as developing the chain that links climate policy and economic activity to emissions, temperature, firms, financial assets and insurance decisions. **This entry belongs to the round theme of one source taking several forms, and it provides a sample at both ends**: **every session ships in two synchronised formats**, a compact reference version for students and a presentation version whose bullets are revealed one at a time with the newly revealed bullet highlighted; **and coursework answers do not exist in plaintext in the repository before they are due**, since each future correction is stored encrypted and a GitHub Action decrypts and publishes it at the time named in a manifest, a mechanism the README calls synchronised publication of corrections, running on a schedule every five minutes with the timezone and a fifteen-minute lead recorded in the manifest. **The materials also state the correct way to read scenarios**, verbatim, as conditional trajectories rather than forecasts or probabilities, **and the reading list is an actuarial supervision list**, including the latest IPCC report, the central banks climate scenarios, the task force on climate-related financial disclosures, the international association of insurance supervisors application paper on the supervision of climate-related risks, the social cost of carbon, and a standard quantitative risk management textbook. **No notebook was run, no PDF was read and no correction was decrypted this round.**
entries.body:
**sorbonne-climate-risks**（仓库 `Vermandel/sorbonne-climate-risks`）**是索邦大学 **M2 Actuariat**（**精算硕士**）「**Risques climatiques**（**气候风险**）」课程中**转型风险**部分的材料**，**逐字自述为**「**Ce dépôt contient le volet consacré au risque de transition de Gauthier Vermandel : cinq séances de deux heures.**」**，**并逐字说明这条链**：**「**Il développe la chaîne qui relie les politiques climatiques et l’activité économique aux émissions, à la température, aux entreprises, aux actifs financiers et aux décisions d’assurance.**」**。**本次实测**：**★1**、**创建 2026-08-21**、**最后推送 2026-09-09**、**主语言标注为 Jupyter Notebook**、**README 实测 5,532 字节**、**文件清单实测 61 条**（**15 个目录、46 个文件**）；**⚠️ 仓库内未见 `LICENSE`**。**本条目属于本轮主题**「**同源多形：一份内容、好几种形态，且必须对得上**」**；**本词条认为它是四条里唯一一条把**时间**也当成一种形态的**——**同一份答案，在到期前与到期后是两种状态**。

**可核实信息（均 README、文件清单、工作流、清单 JSON 与依赖文件实测）**：**⭐⭐⭐ ① 同一门课，每讲两种形态，且说明了两者的分工**——**README 逐字**：**「**Chaque séance est disponible dans deux formats synchronisés : `SessionX_compact.pdf` est la version de référence destinée aux étudiant·es. La page du cours renvoie directement vers ce format. `SessionX_extended.pdf` est la version de présentation. Ses puces sont révélées une à une et la puce nouvellement révélée est mise en évidence.**」**，**并逐讲给出两组链接**（**Séance 1 到 Séance 5**）**。**⭐ 即**同一份内容**有两种**同步**呈现**（**一为阅读、一为讲授**），**且哪一种是**给学生**的**被明确写出来**——**⭐ 而这也解释了为什么需要**两个 PDF**：**演示版的逐条揭示**在静态阅读里反而是缺点**。**⭐⭐⭐ ② 作业答案以**加密态**存在，**到期才变成明文****——README 有专节，**标题逐字为**「**Publication synchronisée des corrigés (PSC)**」**，**并逐字说明**：**「**La procédure PSC conserve chaque futur corrigé sous forme chiffrée, puis une GitHub Action le déchiffre et le publie à la date indiquée dans `publication/releases.json`. Elle s’exécute toutes les cinq minutes et peut aussi être lancée manuellement depuis l’onglet Actions.**」**。**⭐⭐⭐ 本次实测到该机制的**四处细节**：**① **清单文件**`publication/releases.json`（**1,266 字节**）**逐字给出** `"timezone": "Europe/Paris"` **与** `"lead_minutes": 15`，**并列出 6 条发布项**，**每条含** `id`、**ISO-8601 带时区的** `release_at`、**加密源路径** `encrypted` **与**目标路径 `target`（**如** `2026-09-02T10:15:00+02:00` **对应** `publication/encrypted/TP1_corrige.ipynb.gpg` **→** `Session1/correction/TP1_corrige.ipynb`**）**；**② **工作流**`.github/workflows/publish-corrections.yml`（**1,149 字节**）**逐字含** `cron: "*/5 * * * *"` **与** `workflow_dispatch`、**权限** `permissions: contents: write`、**并发组** `group: publish-corrections` **且** `cancel-in-progress: false`；**③ 步骤逐字为**：**检出 → 从 GitHub secret `PSC_PRIVATE_KEY` 导入私钥（**并在导入前先跑一条** `test -n "$PSC_PRIVATE_KEY"` **确认非空**）→ 运行** `python3 scripts/publish_due_corrections.py` **→ 若输出** `published == ‘true’` **则由机器人身份** `github-actions[bot]` **提交并推送**；**④ 仓库里只放**公钥**（`publication/psc-public-key.asc`）**，**README 逐字**「**La clé privée n’est présente que dans le secret GitHub `PSC_PRIVATE_KEY`.**」**。**⭐ 本词条认为这是本轮最值得抄的一处工程做法**：**「**答案在到期前不许出现**」如果只靠约定，**迟早会有人手滑推上去**；**它把这个约定**变成了一条可执行的检查**——**答案在仓库里**存在但不可读**，**发布是一条**定时任务**，**而**明文只在到期后出现**。**⭐⭐⭐ ③ README 还给出**准备一份新答案的四步**，**且第二步要求时间写成**带时区的 ISO-8601****——**逐字**：「**1. le chiffrer avec `scripts/prepare_correction.sh path/to/solution.ipynb publication/encrypted/solution.ipynb.gpg`；2. ajouter au manifeste son identifiant, son heure ISO-8601 avec fuseau, le chemin chiffré et le chemin public cible；3. versionner uniquement l’archive `.gpg`, le manifeste et la page du cours — jamais le corrigé en clair avant l’échéance；4. donner au bouton du site la classe `psc-correction` et un attribut `data-release-at` contenant exactement la même heure.**」**。**⭐ 即**第 4 步把**网页按钮**也绑到同一个时间上**（**属性值与清单里的时间必须完全相同**）——**⭐ 即**「**同一个时刻**」在**三个地方**出现：**清单、**按钮属性、**实际发布**；**⭐ 本词条如实标注**：**本次**未核实这三处实际是否一致**（**未读网页端代码**）**。**⭐⭐ ④ 材料本身对「情景」这个词给了正确的读法**——**课程目标逐字含**：**「**Interpréter les scénarios comme des trajectoires conditionnelles plutôt que comme des prévisions ou des probabilités**」**，**另一条逐字为**「**Discuter les implications et les limites des scénarios de transition issus de modèles pour l’analyse des risques actuariels et financiers**」**——**⭐ 即**它明确要求学生**不要把情景当成预测**——**⭐ 这与本站 [[ngfs]]、[[climate-conditioned-cat]]、[[soa-cc230-climate-mortality]] 等条目里反复出现的同一类提醒同向**：**情景是条件路径，不是概率分布**。**⭐⭐ ⑤ 教学内容是可数的、且自带数据与代码**——**五讲逐字为**：**① 一体化评估模型的经济学基础；② 排放、浓度与温度；③ 气候情景与 DICE；④ 参数不确定性；⑤ 最优气候政策与社会碳成本**；**文件清单实测含**12 个 notebook**（**每讲的 `TPx_sujet.ipynb` 与 `correction/TPx_corrige.ipynb`，**第 3／5 讲另有** `TP3_basics` **与** `TP5_bonus`**）**、**11 个 PDF**（**每讲两份**＋**syllabus**）**、**4 个 CSV**（**含** `data/SSP_scenarios.csv`、`data/ngfs_scenarios.csv`、`data/temperature_historique.csv` **与一份 SSP 数据**）**、**代码文件** `OptimalGrowth.py`、`climate_models.py`、**各讲的** `DICE.py`**、**6 个加密答案** `.gpg`**、**以及** `requirements.txt`（**逐字含** `numpy>=1.24`、`pandas>=1.5`、`matplotlib>=3.6`、`scipy>=1.10`、`jupyter>=1.0`、`nbconvert>=7.0`、`tqdm>=4.64`、`numba>=0.58`、`requests>=2.28`**）**。**⭐ 即**DICE 与简化的气候模型**是**在这个仓库里可运行的东西**，**而不是只出现在幻灯片上**。**⭐⭐ ⑥ 参考文献是一份「精算监管向」书单**——README 的 Références 一节逐字列出：**GIEC (2021) AR6 Working Group I**、**GIEC (2023) AR6 Synthesis Report**、**NGFS (2024) Climate Scenarios for Central Banks and Supervisors**、**O’Neill et al. (2017) The roads ahead: Narratives for shared socioeconomic pathways**、**Nordhaus (2017) Revisiting the social cost of carbon**、**TCFD (2017) Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures**、**IAIS (2021) Application Paper on the Supervision of Climate-related Risks**、**McNeil, Frey et Embrechts (2015) Quantitative Risk Management**。**⭐ 即**一门**精算硕士**课程的阅读清单里同时有**气候科学（IPCC）、**央行与监管情景（NGFS、TCFD、IAIS）**与**精算标准教材**（**McNeil 等**）**。**⭐⭐ ⑦ 还有一条容易被忽略的教学纪律**——**README 逐字**：**「**Ne créez, ne versionnez et ne synchronisez jamais d’environnement virtuel dans ce dépôt pédagogique : `.venv/`, `venv/` et `env/` sont exclus par `.gitignore`.**」**，**并要求把环境建在**Dropbox 目录之外**。**⭐ 即**「**不要把虚拟环境提交进教学仓库**」**也被写成一条明文要求**。**⚠️ 本次实测两处**缺失**（**只记录、不推测原因**）**：**① **仓库内未见 `LICENSE`**（**故本词条不主张许可状态，按惯例记作**权利不明****）；**② **本次未在清单里看到课程网站的源码**，**而 README 第 4 步提到**「**la page du cours**」**的按钮与属性**（**即**网页端可能不在此仓库**）。**⭐ ⑧ 与池内条目的关系**：**本站 [[ngfs]]、[[climate-conditioned-cat]]、[[dfa-climate-datasets]]、[[soa-cc230-climate-mortality]]、[[catmodeling]] 覆盖气候情景数据的来源与建模**，**[[insurance-pricing-course]]、[[cas-python-workshop]]、[[ldacourse1]]、[[juliaactuary-learn]] 覆盖**精算教学材料**这一形态**，**而本条补上的是**「**一门硕士课程如何把**练习、答案与数据**放在同一个仓库里，并让答案在到期前不可读**」这一组合**；**其转型风险链条与** [[open-source-economic-model]] **的资产负债建模取向相邻，但用途不同**。

**对 RIAA**：**本条与 [[ngfs]]、[[soa-cc230-climate-mortality]] 应当并读**——**它给的是一份**可直接对照的精算硕士气候风险课程样本**（**五讲大纲、**每讲的 notebook 与数据、**DICE 实现、**以及一份监管向阅读清单**）；**⭐ 而它对本词条项目自身最有借鉴的一点是**：**把「**什么时候可以公开**」做成机制**，**而不是靠自觉**。

**⚠️ 本词条如实标注**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次没有运行任何 notebook、没有安装任何依赖、没有解密任何答案**（**未执行 `prepare_correction.sh` 或 `publish_due_corrections.py`、**未触碰任何 `.gpg`、**未访问任何 PDF 或幻灯片**）**，**故不主张**课程内容、模型实现、情景数据或教学效果**按所述成立**。**② ⚠️⚠️ 未读任何 PDF 与任何 notebook 正文**——**本次只读了** `README.md`（5,532 字节）、**文件清单**、`.github/workflows/publish-corrections.yml`（1,149 字节）、`publication/releases.json`（1,266 字节）、`requirements.txt`（118 字节）**与** `scripts/publish_due_corrections.py` **的文件大小**，**故不主张** DICE 与 `climate_models.py` 的实现方式、notebook 的练习内容、**以及** `publish_due_corrections.py` **判定到期的具体逻辑**。**⚠️ 本条目最需后续核实的一处**。**③ ⚠️ 未核实发布机制是否真的按时间触发过**：**本次未查该仓库的 Actions 运行历史、**未核实那 6 条发布项的实际状态、**也未核实「**第 4 步**」要求的**按钮属性**是否与清单一致**（**未读网页端代码**）。**④ ⚠️ 未核实** `lead_minutes: 15` **这个提前量的用途**（**本次只读到该字段存在**）**。**⑤ ⚠️ 未核实课程的实际开课情况**（**未访问课程页、**未核实该 volet 是否为完整课程的一部分**——**README 逐字称它是**「**le volet consacré au risque de transition**」**，**即**完整课程中的一个部分**）**。**⑥ ⚠️ 未核实作者身份与院系关系**（**本次只读到 README 自述的姓名与单位**）；**★1 不构成质量证据**。**⑦ ⚠️ 许可未主张**：**仓库内未见 `LICENSE`**——**按惯例记作**权利不明**，**不是「无版权」**；**⚠️ 故其中的 PDF 与 notebook **不宜再分发**，**本词条只作描述与链接**。**⑧ ⚠️ 创建 2026-08-21 在解冻窗口之外、推送 2026-09-09 在窗口之内**——**本次按惯例把这一处写在这里**：**本条的缺口是「**把定时解密发布用于教学答案、并把同一门课做成同步的两种形态**」这一形态此前池内没有对应物**。**⑨ ⚠️ 本条目所记为 2026-09-11 所见**。 **⑩ ⚠️ 引号约定**：**本条目逐字引用法文原文时，把原文里的 ASCII 撇号（如 `l’activité`、`d’assurance`、`O’Neill`）写作 ’**——**以维持本词条不出现 ASCII 单引号的约定（引文内容未改）**。

pédagogique**」**，**並要求把環境建在**Dropbox 目錄之外**。**⚠️ 本次實測兩處**缺失**（**只記錄、不推測原因**）**：**① **未見 `LICENSE`**（**按慣例記作**權利不明****）；**② **清單裡未見課程網站原始碼**，**而第 4 步提到網頁按鈕**。

**對 RIAA**：**本條與 [[ngfs]]、[[soa-cc230-climate-mortality]] 應當並讀**——**它給的是一份**可直接對照的精算碩士氣候風險課程樣本**；**⭐ 而它對本詞條專案最有借鑑的一點是**：**把「**什麼時候可以公開**」做成機制**，**而不是靠自覺**。

**⚠️ 本詞條如實標註**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次沒有運行任何 notebook、沒有安裝任何依賴、沒有解密任何答案**，**故不主張**課程內容、模型實作、情景資料或教學效果**按所述成立**。**② ⚠️⚠️ 未讀任何 PDF 與任何 notebook 正文**——**只讀了** `README.md`、**文件清單**、`.github/workflows/publish-corrections.yml`、`publication/releases.json`、`requirements.txt` **與** `scripts/publish_due_corrections.py` **的檔案大小**。**⚠️ 本條目最需後續核實的一處**。**③ ⚠️ 未核實發布機制是否真的按時間觸發過**（**未查 Actions 執行歷史、未核實 6 條發布項狀態、未核實按鈕屬性是否與清單一致**）。**④ ⚠️ 未核實** `lead_minutes: 15` **的用途**。**⑤ ⚠️ 未核實課程的實際開課情況**（**README 逐字稱它是**「**le volet consacré au risque de transition**」**，**即**完整課程中的一部分**）**。**⑥ ⚠️ 未核實作者身份與院系關係**；**★1 不構成品質證據**。**⑦ ⚠️ 許可未主張**：**未見 `LICENSE`**——**記作**權利不明**，**不是「無版權」**；**其中 PDF 與 notebook 不宜再分發，本詞條只作描述與連結**。**⑧ ⚠️ 建立 2026-08-21 在解凍窗口之外、推送 2026-09-09 在窗口之內**——**本條的缺口是「把定時解密發布用於教學答案、並把同一門課做成同步的兩種形態」這一形態此前池內沒有對應物**。**⑨ ⚠️ 本條目所記為 2026-09-11 所見**。 **⑩ ⚠️ 引號約定**：**本條目逐字引用法文原文時，把原文裡的 ASCII 撇號（`l’activité`、`d’assurance`、`O’Neill`）寫作 ’**——**以維持本詞條不出現 ASCII 單引號的約定（引文內容未改）**。
entries.body_en:
The repository `Vermandel/sorbonne-climate-risks` **holds the transition risk portion of a climate risk course in the Master 2 actuarial programme at Sorbonne University**, described verbatim as five two-hour sessions that develop the chain linking climate policy and economic activity to emissions, temperature, firms, financial assets and insurance decisions. **Measured this round**: **one star**, **created 2026-08-21**, **last pushed 2026-09-09**, **primary language recorded as Jupyter Notebook**, **the README measuring 5,532 bytes**, **the file listing measuring sixty-one entries across fifteen directories and forty-six files**, and **no licence file present**. **This entry belongs to the round theme of one source taking several forms and of those forms having to agree, and it is the only one of the four that treats time itself as one of the forms.**

**Verified information, all measured from the README, the file listing, the workflow, the release manifest and the dependency file**: **first, each session ships in two synchronised forms, and which one is for whom is stated.** The README says verbatim that each session is available in two synchronised formats, that the compact file is the reference version for students and is the format the course page links to directly, and that the extended file is the presentation version whose bullets are revealed one at a time with the newly revealed bullet highlighted, followed by two links per session. **The same content therefore has two synchronised presentations, one for reading and one for teaching, and which one students should use is written out** — which also explains why two files are needed at all, since progressive reveal is a defect in static reading. **Second, coursework answers exist in encrypted form and only become plaintext when due.** A dedicated section, titled synchronised publication of corrections, states verbatim that the procedure keeps each future correction in encrypted form and that a GitHub Action decrypts and publishes it at the date given in the release manifest, running every five minutes and also launchable manually. **Four details of that mechanism were measured**: the manifest, measuring 1,266 bytes, names the timezone and a fifteen-minute lead, and lists six releases each carrying an identifier, an ISO-8601 timestamp with an offset, an encrypted source path and a target path; the workflow, measuring 1,149 bytes, runs on a five-minute cron and on manual dispatch, declares write permission for contents, and uses a concurrency group that does not cancel in progress; the steps import the private key from a repository secret after first asserting that the secret is non-empty, run the publishing script, and if the script reports that something was published, commit and push as the automation bot; and only the public key is committed, with the README stating verbatim that the private key exists only in the repository secret. **Enforcing that answers must not appear before they are due by convention alone eventually fails when somebody pushes the wrong file; here the convention becomes an executable check, because the answers exist in the repository but are unreadable, publication is a scheduled job, and plaintext appears only after the due time.** **Third, the README gives four steps for preparing a future correction and requires the time to be written as ISO-8601 with a timezone**: encrypt the notebook with the provided script; add to the manifest its identifier, its ISO-8601 time with offset, the encrypted path and the target public path; commit only the encrypted archive, the manifest and the course page, never the cleartext correction before the deadline; and give the site button a specific class and a release attribute containing exactly the same time. **The same instant therefore appears in three places: the manifest, the button attribute and the actual publication, although whether those three agree in practice was not verified, since the page code was not read.** **Fourth, the materials state the correct way to read a scenario**, verbatim, as interpreting scenarios as conditional trajectories rather than forecasts or probabilities, with a second objective about discussing the implications and limits of model-derived transition scenarios for actuarial and financial risk analysis, **which aligns with the same reminder that recurs across the pooled climate scenario and catastrophe entries: a scenario is a conditional path, not a probability distribution.** **Fifth, the teaching content is countable and comes with its own data and code**: five sessions on the economics of integrated assessment models, emissions and temperature, climate scenarios and DICE, parameter uncertainty, and optimal climate policy and the social cost of carbon; and the file listing holds twelve notebooks, eleven PDFs, four CSV files including shared socio-economic pathway scenarios, central bank climate scenarios and historical temperature data, three Python modules including the DICE implementation and a climate model per session, six encrypted corrections, and a requirements file pinning numpy, pandas, matplotlib, scipy, jupyter, nbconvert, tqdm, numba and requests. **DICE and the simplified climate models are therefore runnable artefacts in this repository rather than slides alone.** **Sixth, the reading list is an actuarial supervision list**: the latest IPCC working group one report and its synthesis report, the central banks climate scenarios, the task force on climate-related financial disclosures recommendations, the international association of insurance supervisors application paper on the supervision of climate-related risks, the social cost of carbon, the shared socio-economic pathway narratives and a standard quantitative risk management textbook. **Seventh, an easily missed teaching rule is also written down**: never create, version or synchronise a virtual environment in this teaching repository, with the environment directories excluded by the ignore file and the environment instructed to be created outside a cloud-synced folder. **Two absences were measured and are recorded without speculation about cause**: there is no licence file, so no licence status is claimed and the rights are recorded as unclear rather than as absent copyright; and the course page source does not appear in the listing although the fourth preparation step refers to a site button, so the page may live elsewhere. **Eighth, relative to existing entries**: the pooled climate scenario, catastrophe and data entries cover where climate data comes from and how it is modelled, and the pooled teaching entries cover actuarial teaching materials, while this entry supplies the combination of exercises, answers and data in one repository with the answers unreadable until due; its transition risk chain is adjacent to the pooled open-source economic model entry in spirit but serves a different purpose.

**For RIAA**: **this entry reads alongside [[ngfs]] and [[soa-cc230-climate-mortality]]**, because **it is a directly comparable sample of an actuarial master course on climate risk**, with a five-session outline, notebooks and data per session, a DICE implementation and a supervision-oriented reading list; **and the practice most transferable to this wiki is turning when something may be published into a mechanism rather than relying on discipline**.

**Marked honestly by this entry**: **first, no notebook was run, no dependency was installed and no correction was decrypted** — no preparation or publishing script was executed, no encrypted archive was touched and no PDF or slide deck was opened — **so the course content, the model implementations, the scenario data and the teaching outcome are not claimed to hold as described**. **Second, no PDF and no notebook body was read**: only the README, the file listing, the workflow, the release manifest, the requirements file and the size of the publishing script were read, **so nothing is claimed about how DICE and the climate model are implemented, what the exercises contain, or the exact logic by which the publishing script decides something is due; this is the item most in need of later verification**. **Third, whether the publication mechanism has actually fired on schedule was not verified**: the repository action history was not checked, the status of those six releases was not checked, and whether the site button attribute matches the manifest was not checked because the page code was not read. **Fourth, the purpose of the fifteen-minute lead was not established**, only that the field exists. **Fifth, whether the course actually runs was not verified**, the course page was not visited, and the README says verbatim that this is the transition risk portion of a larger course. **Sixth, the author identity and departmental affiliation were not verified beyond the README own account**, and one star is not evidence of quality. **Seventh, no licence status is claimed**: no licence file was seen, so the rights are recorded as unclear rather than as absent copyright, **which also means the PDFs and notebooks should not be redistributed and this entry only describes and links to them**. **Eighth, the creation date of 2026-08-21 is outside the thaw window while the push of 2026-09-09 is inside it**, and following the project convention of naming the gap, **the gap here is that using timed decryption and release for teaching answers, together with publishing one course in two synchronised forms, had no counterpart in the pool. Ninth, this entry records what was visible on 2026-09-11. Tenth, quotation convention: ASCII apostrophes in quoted French were rendered as curved apostrophes so that this entry contains no ASCII single quote, with the quoted text otherwise unchanged.**

entries.title: **「这批数据卖点不是量，而是出处」**：Zenodo 上的美国房贷常量表 **US Mortgage Financing Constants**（DOI `10.5281/zenodo.22676275`）——**四张表、三十行**，**每一行都写明**发布机构、生效年份、**来源网址**与一个「能否被取消」的布尔位**；**⭐ 它逐字说明为什么要这样做**（**逐字**「**The point of the collection is provenance rather than volume.**」）**；**⭐ 并逐字写明它**故意不收**什么**（**房主保险费因逐家而异，**故排除**）
entries.title_en: The selling point of this collection is provenance rather than volume: the US Mortgage Financing Constants tables on Zenodo, under a DOI, hold four tables and thirty rows, and every row names the agency that published it, the year it takes effect, the source URL and a boolean for whether the value can be cancelled; the description states verbatim why that matters, that figures of this kind are widely republished without a date or a source which makes them impossible to check and dangerous to reuse once they change, and it states verbatim what it deliberately excludes, namely homeowners insurance premiums because they vary by carrier.
entries.title_hk: **「這批資料賣點不是量，而是出處」**：Zenodo 上的美國房貸常量表 **US Mortgage Financing Constants**（DOI `10.5281/zenodo.22676275`）——**四張表、三十行**，**每一行都寫明**發布機構、生效年份、**來源網址**與一個「能否被取消」的布林位**；**⭐ 它逐字說明為什麼要這樣做**（**逐字**「**The point of the collection is provenance rather than volume.**」）**；**⭐ 並逐字寫明它**故意不收**什麼**（**房主保險費因逐家而異，**故排除**）
entries.summary: **US Mortgage Financing Constants**（Zenodo 记录 `22676275`，**DOI 逐字为** `10.5281/zenodo.22676275`，**概念 DOI 为** `10.5281/zenodo.22676274`）**是一组美国房贷成本常量表**：**四张表、三十行**，**逐字自述覆盖**「**conforming loan limits**」（**FHFA**）、「**FHA loan limits and premiums**」（**HUD**）、「**mortgage insurance assumptions**」（**PMI／FHA MIP／VA funding fee／USDA guarantee fee**）、**以及**「**ownership cost and qualifying assumptions**」（**CFPB**）**。**本条目属于本轮主题**「存证」**，**它是四条里把**出处**写成表结构的一条**：**⭐⭐⭐ ① 每个值自带来源**——**本次实测** `mortgage-insurance.csv` 的表头逐字为** `"program","key","description","value","unit","cancels","as_of","source","source_url"`，**即**每一行**都带**发布机构、**来源网址、**生效年份（`as_of`）**与一个**能否被取消**的布尔位（`cancels`**）**；**⭐⭐⭐ ② 它逐字说明为什么这样做**——**「**The point of the collection is provenance rather than volume. Figures of this kind are widely republished without a date or a source, which makes them impossible to check and dangerous to reuse once they change. Every value here states which agency published it and which year it applies to, so a reader can verify the arithmetic instead of trusting it.**」**——**⭐ 本词条认为这是本轮最值得抄的一句**；**⭐⭐ ③ 它逐字写明**故意排除**了什么**——**「**Homeowners insurance premiums are deliberately excluded: they vary by carrier, construction, claims history and coverage level**」**，**并逐字交代另一处限制**（**PMI 费率为**representative**而非报价**）**；**⭐⭐ ④ 登记层面**：**版本** `1.1.0`、**许可** CC-BY-4.0、**创建 2026-09-09**、**8 个文件**（**CSV 与 JSON 各一套**）、**两个 `isDocumentedBy` 链接指向方法与数据集页**。**⚠️ 本次未核对任何一行数字与其所列来源是否一致**（**未访问 FHFA／HUD／VA／CFPB 任何页面**）**。

entries.summary_en: The Zenodo record for US Mortgage Financing Constants, under a version DOI and a concept DOI, **holds reference tables of the constants that determine what a US mortgage costs**: four tables and thirty rows covering conforming loan limits from the housing finance agency, FHA limits and premiums from the housing department, mortgage insurance assumptions including private mortgage insurance, FHA premiums, VA funding fees and USDA guarantee fees, and ownership cost and qualifying assumptions from the consumer financial protection bureau. **This entry belongs to the round theme of evidence and citability, and of the four it is the one that writes provenance into the table structure**: the measured header of its mortgage insurance file carries programme, key, description, value, unit, a cancellation flag, an as-of year, a source name and a source URL, so **every single row names the agency that published it, the year it applies to and where to check it, plus whether the value can be cancelled**. **The description states the purpose verbatim**: the point of the collection is provenance rather than volume, since figures of this kind are widely republished without a date or a source, which makes them impossible to check and dangerous to reuse once they change, and every value here states which agency published it and which year it applies to so a reader can verify the arithmetic instead of trusting it. **It also states verbatim what it deliberately leaves out**, namely homeowners insurance premiums, because they vary by carrier, construction and claims, and it flags that private mortgage insurance rates are representative rather than quoted. **Registration details measured**: version 1.1.0, licence CC-BY-4.0, created 2026-09-09, eight files supplied as both CSV and JSON, and two documented-by links pointing at a methodology page. **No row was checked against the agency it cites, and no agency page was visited.**

**US Mortgage Financing Constants: Loan Limits, Insurance Premiums and Underwriting Assumptions (2026)**（Zenodo 记录 `22676275`）**是一组美国房贷成本常量表**，**本次实测**：**DOI 逐字为** `10.5281/zenodo.22676275`**、概念 DOI 为** `10.5281/zenodo.22676274`**、**版本** `1.1.0`**、**类型** Dataset**、**许可** CC-BY-4.0**、**创建与更新均为 2026-09-09**、**访问权限为** open**、**共 8 个文件**（**四张表各有 CSV 与 JSON 两种形式**）**；**作者** `Mane, Chetan`（**逐字附 ORCID** `0009-0001-8032-6101`）**；**关键字逐字含** `conforming loan limit`、`FHA loan limits`、`mortgage insurance premium`、`private mortgage insurance`、`VA funding fee`、`debt-to-income ratio`、`mortgage underwriting`、`United States`**；**关联标识两个**，**逐字为** `https://www.usmortgagecalc.com/datasets` **与** `.../methodology`，**关系均为** `isDocumentedBy`**。**本条目属于本轮主题**「**存证：编号、版本、许可，以及把每个数追回它的来源**」**。

**可核实信息（均 Zenodo 元数据与文件实测）**：**⭐⭐⭐ ① 表结构本身就是出处声明**——**本次实读** `mortgage-insurance.csv`，**表头逐字为** `"program","key","description","value","unit","cancels","as_of","source","source_url"`**；**每一行实测形如**：`conventional` / `pmi_annual_percent` / **说明逐字为**「**Private mortgage insurance, percent of the original loan amount per year**」/ `0.6` / `percent` / `cancels` 为 `true` / `as_of` 为 `2025` / **来源** `Consumer Financial Protection Bureau` / **来源网址** `https://www.consumerfinance.gov/`；**另有** FHA 的 `fha_upfront_mip_percent`（`1.75`**，**来源 HUD**）**、**`fha_annual_mip_percent`（`0.55`**，**说明逐字含**「**Lasts the life of the loan below a 10% down payment**」**）**、**VA 的 `va_funding_fee_first_use_zero_down`（`2.15`**，**说明逐字含**「**Replaces monthly mortgage insurance**」**）**。**⭐ 即**「**这个数是谁发的、**哪一年生效、**能在哪一页核对、**以及它会不会被取消**」**四件事**被放在同一行里**——**⭐ 本词条认为这是本轮最值得抄的一处**。`conforming-loan-limits.csv` **表头逐字为** `"limit_type","description","amount_usd","as_of","source","source_url","changes_annually"`**，**实测一行逐字为** `baseline_conforming` / **说明**「**Baseline conforming loan limit for a one-unit property in most counties**」/ `806500` / `2025` / **FHFA** / `https://www.fhfa.gov/` / **`changes_annually` 为 `true`**——**⭐ 即**它还标注了**这个数会不会每年变**。**⭐⭐⭐ ② 它逐字说明为什么这批数据的重点是出处**——**Zenodo 描述逐字**：**「**Four reference tables covering the constants that determine what a US mortgage costs, each figure published with a named source and the year it takes effect.**」**，**随后**：**「**The point of the collection is provenance rather than volume. Figures of this kind are widely republished without a date or a source, which makes them impossible to check and dangerous to reuse once they change. Every value here states which agency published it and which year it applies to, so a reader can verify the arithmetic instead of trusting it.**」**。**⭐ 三处值得记**：**① ⭐⭐⭐ 它把**「**这类数字被广泛转贴时不带日期与来源**」**点名为一个**具体危害**（**无法核对、且一旦变化就危险**）**；**② ⭐⭐⭐ 它给出的解法不是「我们更权威」，而是**「**让读者能自己核对**」（**verify the arithmetic instead of trusting it**）；**③ ⭐⭐ 它把**数据的时间点**写清**（**逐字**「**Data as of 2025 programme year; last reviewed August 2026.**」**）**——**⭐ 即**「**数据是哪一年的**」与「**我什么时候复核过**」**是两件事、两句话**。**⭐⭐⭐ ③ 它逐字写明**故意不收**什么，以及另一处限制**——**逐字**：**「**Limitations: conventional PMI rates are representative rather than quoted — actual pricing varies by insurer, credit score and loan-to-value. Homeowners insurance premiums are deliberately excluded: they vary by carrier, construction, claims history and coverage level**」**。**⭐ 即**它区分了**两种「不确定」**：**一种是**我这行数只是代表值**（**仍给一个数并标明性质**），**另一种是**这个量根本不该被列成单值**（**因逐家而异，**故整类不收**）**——**⭐ 本词条认为这个区分很值得抄**：**不确切的仍然列出并标明，**而本质上无法统一的**直接排除并说明理由**。**⭐⭐ ④ 交付形式是可核对的两种**——**8 个文件**：`ownership-cost-assumptions.csv`／`.json`、`mortgage-insurance.csv`／`.json`、`conforming-loan-limits.csv`／`.json`、`fha-limits.csv`／`.json`；**描述逐字**「**Thirty rows across four tables, supplied as CSV (RFC 4180) and JSON.**」**——**⭐ 即**它连 CSV 遵循的规范（**RFC 4180**）都写出来了**；**⭐ 本词条如实标注**：**JSON 那四份本次**未打开**（**只读了两份 CSV**）**。**⭐⭐ ⑤ 登记机制值得记录**：**该记录有**概念 DOI**（`10.5281/zenodo.22676274`）与**版本 DOI**（`10.5281/zenodo.22676275`）**两层**，**故**引用时可以选「**永久指向这个概念**」或「**指向这一版**」；**⭐ 并与本站池内已有的**8 条 Zenodo 来源条目**同一形态**（**如 [[inflation-aware-xol-reserving]]、[[claims-inflation-motor-my]]、[[scelo]]、[[climate-conditioned-cat]]、[[dfa-climate-datasets]]**）**。**⭐⭐ ⑥ 与池内条目的关系**：**本站 [[fanniemae-underwriting-rules]] 记录的是**房贷承保规则的代码化**，**[[tpa-transparency-data]]、[[cms-open-data]] 记录的是**监管与公开数据源**，**而本条补上的是**「**把一批散落在不同机构的常量**逐行标注出处**之后放进一个带 DOI 的表里**」这一做法**——**⭐ 其领域（**美国房贷与房贷保险**）与我们的精算主线相邻但不同**（**本词条如实指出这一点**）**，**故本条的价值主要在**出处写法**而不在题材**。

**对 RIAA**：**本条与 [[fanniemae-underwriting-rules]]、[[tpa-transparency-data]] 应当并读**——**它给的是一个**可以直接照抄的表设计**：**把「**发布机构、**来源网址、**生效年份、**是否会定期变、**是否可取消**」**作为列**，**而不是写进附注**；**⭐ 对本词条项目自身**，**它那句「**provenance rather than volume**」**与本站**「**每个数都要能回到来源**」**是同一条纪律的另一种说法**。

**⚠️ 本词条如实标注**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次没有核对任何一行数字与其所列来源是否一致**（**未访问** FHFA、HUD、VA、CFPB **或** usmortgagecalc.com **的任何页面**）**，**故不主张**任何常量的数值、`as_of` 年份或来源归属正确**——**本词条只主张「**表里写了这些列、这些行**」**。**⚠️ 本条目最需后续核实的一处**。**② ⚠️⚠️ 未读 JSON 四份**（**只读了两份 CSV 的表头与若干行**），**故不主张 JSON 的结构与 CSV 是否一一对应**。**③ ⚠️ 未核实 30 行**这个数的构成**（**描述逐字称三十行**，**而本次**只逐行读了其中两份文件的若干行，**未逐行计数四张表**）**。**④ ⚠️ 未核实作者身份**（**只读到姓名与一个 ORCID**）**与** usmortgagecalc.com **的性质**（**未访问该站**）**；**⚠️ Zenodo 的下载量与引用数本次未记录**。**⑤ ⚠️ 未核实许可适用范围**：**记录字段为** CC-BY-4.0**，**本次**未读任何附带的许可说明文件**（**该记录只有 8 个数据文件，**本次未见独立许可文本**）**。**⑥ ⚠️ 该记录**创建 2026-09-09 在解冻窗口之内**，**故本条不需要窗口例外**；**⭐ 但本词条如实指出**：**「**把监管常量逐行标注机构与生效年份、并明确排除无法统一列值的那一类**」这一形态，此前池内没有对应物**。**⑦ ⚠️ 本条目所记为 2026-09-11 所见**；**⭐ 并如实指出**：**本条的领域是**美国住房金融**，**与本站以**保险与精算**为主线的定位**相邻而不重合****。

**US Mortgage Financing Constants: Loan Limits, Insurance Premiums and Underwriting Assumptions (2026)**（Zenodo 記錄 `22676275`）**是一組美國房貸成本常量表**。**本次實測**：**DOI 逐字為** `10.5281/zenodo.22676275`**、概念 DOI 為** `10.5281/zenodo.22676274`**、**版本** `1.1.0`**、**類型** Dataset**、**許可** CC-BY-4.0**、**建立與更新均為 2026-09-09**、**共 8 個檔案**（**四張表各有 CSV 與 JSON**）**；**作者** `Mane, Chetan`（**附 ORCID**）**；**關鍵字逐字含** `mortgage insurance premium`、`private mortgage insurance`、`VA funding fee`、`debt-to-income ratio`**；**關聯標識兩個**，**關係均為** `isDocumentedBy`**。**本條目屬於本輪主題**「**存證：編號、版本、許可，以及把每個數追回它的來源**」**。

**可核實資訊（均 Zenodo 元數據與檔案實測）**：**⭐⭐⭐ ① 表結構本身就是出處聲明**——**實讀** `mortgage-insurance.csv`，**表頭逐字為** `"program","key","description","value","unit","cancels","as_of","source","source_url"`**；**每一行實測形如**：`conventional` / `pmi_annual_percent` / `0.6` / `percent` / `cancels` **為** `true` / `as_of` **為** `2025` / **來源** `Consumer Financial Protection Bureau` / **來源網址** `https://www.consumerfinance.gov/`；**另有** FHA `fha_upfront_mip_percent`（`1.75`，HUD）、`fha_annual_mip_percent`（`0.55`，**說明逐字含**「**Lasts the life of the loan below a 10% down payment**」）、VA `va_funding_fee_first_use_zero_down`（`2.15`）。**⭐ 即**「**這個數是誰發的、**哪一年生效、**能在哪一頁核對、**以及它會不會被取消**」**四件事**放在同一行**。`conforming-loan-limits.csv` **表頭逐字為** `"limit_type","description","amount_usd","as_of","source","source_url","changes_annually"`，**實測一行** `baseline_conforming`／`806500`／`2025`／FHFA／`https://www.fhfa.gov/`／**`changes_annually` 為 `true`**。**⭐⭐⭐ ② 它逐字說明為什麼重點是出處**——**逐字**：**「**The point of the collection is provenance rather than volume. Figures of this kind are widely republished without a date or a source, which makes them impossible to check and dangerous to reuse once they change. Every value here states which agency published it and which year it applies to, so a reader can verify the arithmetic instead of trusting it.**」**。**⭐ 三處值得記**：**① 它把「**這類數字被廣泛轉貼時不帶日期與來源**」**點名為具體危害**；**② 它給的解法不是「我們更權威」，而是**「讓讀者能自己核對」**；**③ 它把數據時間點與複核時間分成兩句話**（**逐字**「**Data as of 2025 programme year; last reviewed August 2026.**」**）**。**⭐⭐⭐ ③ 它逐字寫明**故意不收**什麼**——**逐字**：**「**conventional PMI rates are representative rather than quoted — actual pricing varies by insurer, credit score and loan-to-value. Homeowners insurance premiums are deliberately excluded: they vary by carrier, construction, claims history and coverage level**」**——**⭐ 即**它區分了**「**只是代表值**」（**仍列出並標明**）與「**本質上無法列單值**」（**整類不收並說明理由**）**。**⭐⭐ ④ 交付形式是可核對的兩種**——**8 個檔案**（**CSV 與 JSON 各四**）**；**描述逐字**「**Thirty rows across four tables, supplied as CSV (RFC 4180) and JSON.**」**；**⭐ 本詞條如實標註**：**JSON 四份本次未打開**。**⭐⭐ ⑤ 登記機制**：**該記錄有**概念 DOI**與**版本 DOI**兩層**；**⭐ 與池內已有的 8 條 Zenodo 來源條目同一形態**。

**對 RIAA**：**本條與 [[fanniemae-underwriting-rules]]、[[tpa-transparency-data]] 應當並讀**——**它給的是一個可直接照抄的表設計**：**把「**發布機構、**來源網址、**生效年份、**是否定期變、**是否可取消**」**作為欄位**；**⭐ 它那句「**provenance rather than volume**」與本站「**每個數都要能回到來源**」是同一條紀律**。

**⚠️ 本詞條如實標註**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次沒有核對任何一行數字與其來源是否一致**（**未訪問** FHFA／HUD／VA／CFPB 或 usmortgagecalc.com**），**故不主張**任何常量數值、`as_of` 年份或來源歸屬正確**。**⚠️ 本條目最需後續核實的一處**。**② ⚠️⚠️ 未讀 JSON 四份**。**③ ⚠️ 未核實「**三十行**」的構成**（**未逐行計數四張表**）**。**④ ⚠️ 未核實作者身份與** usmortgagecalc.com **的性質**；**未記錄下載量與引用數**。**⑤ ⚠️ 未核實許可適用範圍**（**未見獨立許可文本**）**。**⑥ ⚠️ 建立 2026-09-09 在解凍窗口之內**，**故本條不需要窗口例外**；**但「把監管常量逐行標註機構與生效年份、並明確排除無法統一列值的那一類」此前池內沒有對應物**。**⑦ ⚠️ 本條目所記為 2026-09-11 所見**；**⭐ 並如實指出本條領域為**美國住房金融**，**與本站以**保險與精算**為主線的定位**相鄰而不重合****。
entries.body_en:
The Zenodo record for US Mortgage Financing Constants, published in 2026, **is a set of reference tables for the constants that determine what a US mortgage costs**. **Measured this round**: a version DOI and a concept DOI, **version 1.1.0**, resource type Dataset, **licence CC-BY-4.0**, **created and updated on 2026-09-09**, open access, **eight files** in total, meaning each of four tables is supplied in both CSV and JSON; the creator carries an ORCID; the keywords name conforming loan limits, FHA loan limits, mortgage insurance premiums, private mortgage insurance, VA funding fees, debt-to-income ratios and mortgage underwriting; and two related identifiers, both marked as documented by, point at a datasets page and a methodology page. **This entry belongs to the round theme of evidence and citability: a number, a version, a licence, and tracing every value back to its source.**

**Verified information, all measured from the Zenodo metadata and the files themselves**: **first, the table structure is itself a provenance claim.** The measured header of the mortgage insurance file carries columns for programme, key, description, value, unit, a cancellation flag, an as-of year, a source name and a source URL. **Measured rows read as follows**: conventional private mortgage insurance at six tenths of a percent per year, cancellable, as of 2025, sourced to the consumer financial protection bureau with its URL; FHA upfront premium at 1.75 percent and annual premium at 0.55 percent sourced to the housing department, the latter annotated verbatim as lasting the life of the loan below a ten percent down payment; and a VA funding fee of 2.15 percent for first use with no down payment, annotated verbatim as replacing monthly mortgage insurance. **Four facts therefore sit on the same row: who issued the number, which year it takes effect, where it can be checked, and whether it can be cancelled.** The loan limits file adds columns for amount, as-of year, source and whether the value changes annually, with a measured row giving 806,500 dollars as the baseline conforming limit for a one-unit property in most counties as of 2025, sourced to the federal housing finance agency, and flagged as changing annually. **Second, the description states why the point of the collection is provenance.** Verbatim, these are four reference tables covering the constants that determine what a US mortgage costs, each figure published with a named source and the year it takes effect; the point of the collection is provenance rather than volume, because figures of this kind are widely republished without a date or a source, which makes them impossible to check and dangerous to reuse once they change; and every value here states which agency published it and which year it applies to, so a reader can verify the arithmetic instead of trusting it. **Three things are worth recording**: it names a concrete harm, that such figures circulate undated and unsourced; its remedy is not a claim of greater authority but making verification possible for the reader; and it separates two statements in two sentences, that the data is as of a given programme year and that it was last reviewed in a given month. **Third, it states verbatim what it deliberately leaves out and where else it is limited**, noting that conventional private mortgage insurance rates are representative rather than quoted because actual pricing varies by insurer, credit score and loan-to-value, and that homeowners insurance premiums are deliberately excluded because they vary by carrier, construction and claims. **It therefore distinguishes two kinds of uncertainty: a value that is merely representative, which is still listed with its character stated, and a quantity that cannot be stated as a single value at all, which is excluded as a class with the reason given.** **Fourth, delivery is two machine-readable forms**: eight files, four tables each in CSV and JSON, with the description stating verbatim that thirty rows across four tables are supplied as CSV following RFC 4180 and as JSON. **The JSON files were not opened this round. Fifth, the registration mechanism is worth recording**: the record carries both a concept DOI and a version DOI, so a citation can point either at the idea or at this particular version, **which matches the shape of the eight Zenodo-sourced entries already in the pool. Sixth, relative to existing entries**: the pooled mortgage underwriting rules entry records the codification of underwriting rules and the pooled transparency and open data entries record regulator-side sources, while this entry supplies the practice of taking constants scattered across agencies, annotating each row with its source, and publishing them as a DOI-bearing table. **This entry states plainly that the subject matter is US housing finance, adjacent to but not overlapping the insurance and actuarial focus of this wiki, so its value here lies in the sourcing practice rather than the topic.**

**For RIAA**: **this entry reads alongside [[fanniemae-underwriting-rules]] and [[tpa-transparency-data]]**, because **it is a table design that can be copied directly**: make the issuing agency, the source URL, the effective year, whether it changes periodically and whether it can be cancelled into columns rather than footnotes; **and its phrase about provenance rather than volume is another way of stating this wiki own rule that every number must trace back to a source**.

**Marked honestly by this entry**: **first, no row was checked against the source it cites and no agency page was visited** — neither the housing finance agency, the housing department, the veterans affairs department, the consumer financial protection bureau nor the site named as documentation — **so no constant value, as-of year or source attribution is claimed correct; this entry claims only that the table contains these columns and these rows. This is the item most in need of later verification.** **Second, the four JSON files were not read**, so nothing is claimed about their structure or whether they correspond one-to-one with the CSVs. **Third, the composition of the claimed thirty rows was not verified**, only several rows of two files were read and the four tables were not counted row by row. **Fourth, the creator identity and the nature of the site named as documentation were not verified**, only a name and an ORCID were read, and download and citation counts were not recorded. **Fifth, the scope of the licence was not verified**: the metadata field reads CC-BY-4.0 and no separate licence text was seen among the eight data files. **Sixth, the record was created on 2026-09-09, inside the thaw window, so no window exception is needed; however, the shape of annotating regulatory constants row by row with their issuing agency and effective year, and of explicitly excluding a class of quantities that cannot be stated as single values, had no counterpart in the pool. Seventh, this entry records what was visible on 2026-09-11, and states plainly that its subject matter is US housing finance, adjacent to but not overlapping this wiki main focus.**

Every value here states which agency published it and which year it applies to, so a reader can verify the arithmetic instead of trusting it.」、「Thirty rows across four tables, supplied as CSV (RFC 4180) and JSON.」、「Data as of 2025 programme year; last reviewed August 2026.」以及 Limitations（PMI 为 representative 而非报价；房主保险费 deliberately excluded）｜⚠️未核对任何一行数字与其所列来源是否一致（未访问 FHFA／HUD／VA／CFPB／usmortgagecalc.com 任何页面），不主张任何数值、as_of 年份或来源归属正确——本条目最需后续核实的一处｜⚠️未读四份 JSON（只读两份 CSV 的表头与若干行），不主张 JSON 结构与 CSV 一一对应｜⚠️未逐行计数四张表，未核实「三十行」的构成｜⚠️未核实作者身份与该站性质，未记录下载量与引用数｜⚠️未读独立许可文本，只记录元数据字段为 CC-BY-4.0｜⚠️创建 2026-09-09 在解冻窗口之内，无需窗口例外；但「监管常量逐行标注机构与生效年份＋明确排除无法统一列值的那一类」此前池内无对应物｜⚠️本条的领域为美国住房金融，与本站以保险与精算为主线的定位相邻而不重合，本词条如实指出｜⚠️本条目所记为 2026-09-11 所见

entries.title: **把「谁在什么情况下可以写这一格」写成四列四条规则**：一个美国死亡率分解项目（Zenodo DOI `10.5281/zenodo.22650711`，v0.1.4）——**它把**引用**、**出处**、**人工核签**、**他方佐证**拆成**四件不同的事****；**⭐ 逐字**「**A number carrying a citation looks verified whether or not anyone verified it. An automated fetch does not solve that; it changes the costume.**」**；**⭐ 自动化抓取**永远不能**写 `verified_by`**，**故一次成功的抓取之后**`UnverifiedDataError` 仍然会抛**；**⭐ 并逐字写明**空白不等于失败****
entries.title_en: Writing who may fill which cell, and under what claim, as four columns and four rules: a US mortality decomposition project archived on Zenodo at version 0.1.4 separates citation, provenance, human attestation and third-party corroboration into four different things, states verbatim that a number carrying a citation looks verified whether or not anyone verified it and that an automated fetch does not solve that but changes the costume, guarantees that no machine path can write the attestation column so that an unverified-data error still fires after a successful fetch, and states verbatim that a blank corroboration field means not corroborated rather than failed.
entries.title_hk: **把「誰在什麼情況下可以寫這一格」寫成四欄四條規則**：一個美國死亡率分解專案（Zenodo DOI `10.5281/zenodo.22650711`，v0.1.4）——**它把**引用**、**出處**、**人工核簽**、**他方佐證**拆成**四件不同的事****；**⭐ 逐字**「**A number carrying a citation looks verified whether or not anyone verified it. An automated fetch does not solve that; it changes the costume.**」**；**⭐ 自動化抓取**永遠不能**寫 `verified_by`**，**故一次成功的抓取之後**`UnverifiedDataError` 仍然會拋**；**⭐ 並逐字寫明**空白不等於失敗****
entries.summary: **mortality-analysis**（`terryfinberg/mortality-analysis`；**Zenodo 记录** `22650711`，**DOI 逐字为** `10.5281/zenodo.22650711`）**是一个美国 2010–2024 年死亡率分解项目**：**用** Kitagawa 方法**把粗死亡率的变化拆成**年龄别死亡率**与**人口年龄结构**两部分**，**并测量这十五年间**四个口径边界**（**CDC WONDER 逐年口径、**2023 年的 Vintage 2024 重述、**2010 年 4 月 1 日基准、**2017／2018 的 bridged-race 到 single-race 接缝**）**。**本条目属于本轮主题**「存证」**，**它是四条里把**证据等级**写得最细的一条**：**⭐⭐⭐ ① 它把四件事拆成四列、四种「谁可以写」**——**按** `source_citation`（**引用**，**由导出文件页脚派生**）／`fetched_from`（**出处**，**由抓取脚本写**）／`verified_by`（**人工核签**，**逐字**「**a human, only**」）／`corroborated_against`（**他方佐证**，**同样只允许人写**）**；**⭐⭐⭐ ② 它逐字说明为什么必须拆**——**「**A number carrying a citation looks verified whether or not anyone verified it. An automated fetch does not solve that; it changes the costume. A run against the wrong dataset, or the right dataset with a wrong filter, writes an impeccably precise `fetched_from` string onto a wrong number, and does so more convincingly than a hand transcription would.**」**；**⭐⭐⭐ ③ 它保证机器**写不了**核签那一格**——**逐字**「**no machine path in this repository can write `verified_by`, and a test asserts it against a temporary directory rather than against the current CSVs**」**，**且**一次成功抓取之后**`UnverifiedDataError` 仍会抛**；**⭐⭐ ④ 它也规定**改了就要撤销签名****（**改引用或覆写数值都会清空 `verified_by`**，**理由逐字为**「**a signature was made against what the old citation claimed**」**）**；**⭐⭐⭐ ⑤ **空白 = 未佐证，不等于失败****（**逐字**「**A blank `corroborated_against` means not corroborated. It does not mean corroboration failed**」**）**，**并要求**部分佐证就写成部分**（**逐字**「**Partial corroboration stated as partial is worth more than complete attestation to a standard met on a sample.**」**）**；**⚠️ 本次未运行、未读任何数据行**。
entries.summary_hk: **mortality-analysis**（`terryfinberg/mortality-analysis`；**Zenodo 記錄** `22650711`）**是一個美國 2010–2024 年死亡率分解專案**：**用** Kitagawa 方法**把粗死亡率變化拆成**年齡別死亡率**與**人口年齡結構**，**並測量四個口徑邊界**。**本條目屬於本輪主題**「存證」**：**⭐⭐⭐ ① 它把四件事拆成四欄、四種「誰可以寫」**（`source_citation`／`fetched_from`／`verified_by`／`corroborated_against`，**後兩者逐字**「**a human, only**」**）**；**⭐⭐⭐ ② 它逐字說明為什麼必須拆**——**「**A number carrying a citation looks verified whether or not anyone verified it. An automated fetch does not solve that; it changes the costume.**」**；**⭐⭐⭐ ③ 它保證機器**寫不了**核簽那一格**（**逐字**「**no machine path in this repository can write `verified_by`, and a test asserts it against a temporary directory rather than against the current CSVs**」**）**；**⭐⭐ ④ 改了引用或覆寫數值就會清空 `verified_by`**（**逐字理由**「**a signature was made against what the old citation claimed**」**）**；**⭐⭐⭐ ⑤ **空白＝未佐證，不等於失敗****。**⚠️ 本次未運行、未讀任何資料列**。
entries.summary_en: The project at `terryfinberg/mortality-analysis`, archived on Zenodo under a version DOI, **decomposes United States mortality between 2010 and 2024**: it splits the change in the crude death rate into an age-specific mortality component and a population age-structure component using the Kitagawa method, and it measures rather than assumes four denominator boundaries inside that single fifteen-year series, namely the per-year vintage chain carried by one national data product, a restatement of one year under a later vintage, an earlier measurement basis, and a race-bridging seam. **This entry belongs to the round theme of evidence and citability, and of the four it writes evidence levels in the most detail**: it splits four things into four columns with four different rules about who may write them, covering citation derived from the export footer, provenance written by the fetch script, human attestation which verbatim only a human may write, and third-party corroboration which likewise only a human may write; it states verbatim why the split is necessary, that a number carrying a citation looks verified whether or not anyone verified it, that an automated fetch does not solve that but changes the costume, and that a run against the wrong dataset or the right dataset with a wrong filter writes an impeccably precise provenance string onto a wrong number more convincingly than a hand transcription would; it guarantees that no machine path in the repository can write the attestation column and that a test asserts this against a temporary directory rather than against the current data, so an unverified-data error still fires after a successful fetch; it clears the attestation whenever the citation or the value changes, on the reasoning that a signature was made against what the old citation claimed; and it states verbatim that a blank corroboration field means not corroborated rather than failed, and that partial corroboration stated as partial is worth more than complete attestation to a standard met on a sample. **Nothing was run and no data row was read this round.**
entries.body:
**mortality-analysis**（GitHub 仓库 `terryfinberg/mortality-analysis`；**Zenodo 记录** `22650711`）**是一个美国死亡率分解项目**，**标题逐字为**「**Decomposing U.S. Crude Death Rates, 2010-2024: Population Aging Dominates, and the Denominator Is Not Stable**」。**本次实测**：**Zenodo 记录** —— **DOI 逐字为** `10.5281/zenodo.22650711`**、概念 DOI 为** `10.5281/zenodo.22263667`**、**版本** `v0.1.4`**、**类型** Software**、**许可** BSD-3-Clause**、**创建与更新均为 2026-09-07**、**1 个文件**（**逐字名为** `terryfinberg/mortality-analysis-v0.1.4.zip`**）**、**作者** `Finberg, Terry`（**附 ORCID** `0009-0006-1598-4200`**）**、**关联标识逐字为** `https://github.com/terryfinberg/mortality-analysis/tree/v0.1.4`（**关系** `isSupplementTo`，**即**指向**打上版本标签**的那一次提交**）**；**GitHub 仓库** —— **创建 2026-09-01、最后推送 2026-09-07**、**★0**、**语言 Python**；**文件实测**：`README.md` 31,176 字节、`STATUS.md` **53,244 字节**、`UAT_CHECKLIST.md` 19,073 字节、`docs/denominator-methods.md` 31,398 字节、`LICENSE` 2,202 字节（**BSD-3-Clause**）**。**本条目属于本轮主题**「**存证：编号、版本、许可，以及把每个数追回它的来源**」**；**本词条认为它是本会话迄今为止**把「**证据等级**」写得最细的一条**——**⭐ 其做法与本词条项目自身的纪律**高度同构**。

**可核实信息（均 README、`STATUS.md` 与文件清单实测）**：**⭐⭐⭐ ① 它把四件事拆成四列，并规定每列**谁可以写****——**README 有一节标题逐字为**「**Provenance, attestation and corroboration are three different columns**」（**⭐ 注意标题说 three，而表里是四列——本文照原文引用，并在下文如实列出四行**），**表头逐字为** `Column`／`The claim`／`Who may write it`，**四行逐字为**：**① **`source_citation`**——主张逐字**「**What this value is a copy of. The export’s footer `Dataset`, its query parameters, access date and sha256**」**，**写入者逐字**「**derived from the footer by `export_citation()`**」；**② **`fetched_from`**——主张逐字**「**Provenance. `wonder-export:<filename>@sha256:<hash>`**」**，**写入者逐字**「**`src.fetch.promote()`**」；**③ **`verified_by`**——主张逐字**「**Attestation. A person confirmed this value matches the cited export**」**，**写入者逐字**「**a human, only**」；**④ **`corroborated_against`**——主张逐字**「**Corroboration. A separate publication reports the same figure, e.g. an NVSR volume and table. Not independent: see the note below**」**，**写入者同样逐字**「**a human, only**」**。**⭐ 本词条认为这是本轮最值得抄的一处**：**「**这一格是谁写的**」**被写成表的一列**，**而不是靠约定——**⭐ 而四列的**四种主张**分别是：**我抄的是哪一份文件**、**这份数据是怎么来的**、**有人核过它与该文件一致**、**另有出版物报了同一个数**。**⭐⭐⭐ ② 它逐字说明为什么必须拆开**——**逐字**：**「**This split is the point, not bookkeeping. A number carrying a citation looks verified whether or not anyone verified it. An automated fetch does not solve that; it changes the costume. A run against the wrong dataset, or the right dataset with a wrong filter, writes an impeccably precise `fetched_from` string onto a wrong number, and does so more convincingly than a hand transcription would.**」**。**⭐ 三处值得记**：**① ⭐⭐⭐ 「**带着引用的数字看起来就像被核过**」**——**这是本词条见过的对「**引用的暗示力**」最准确的一句描述**；**② ⭐⭐⭐ 「**自动抓取并没有解决问题，它只是换了一身衣服**」（**changes the costume**）**——**⭐ 即**自动化提高了**可信的外观**，**而没有提高**可信度**；**③ ⭐⭐⭐ 「**跑错数据集、或对的数据集配错的筛选条件，会把一个精确到无可挑剔的出处字符串写在一个错的数字上，而且比手工转录更有说服力**」**——**⭐ 本词条认为这是本轮四条里**最重要的一句**：**它说的不是「人会出错」，而是「**机器出错时更像对的**」。**⭐⭐⭐ ③ 它保证机器**写不了**核签那一格，而且用测试把这个「**不可能**」钉住**——**逐字**：**「**So `verified_by` is never machine-written. `src.fetch.promote()` fills `source_type`, `fetched_from` and `source_citation`, and leaves `verified_by` blank, which means **`UnverifiedDataError` still fires after a successful fetch**. Promotion gets the numbers into place; it does not sign them off. You do that, row by row, and the loader will not run in strict mode until you have.**」**；**另一处逐字**：**「**no machine path in this repository can write `verified_by`, and a test asserts it against a temporary directory rather than against the current CSVs**」**。**⭐ 三处值得记**：**① ⭐⭐⭐ 抓取成功后仍然报「未核实」**——**即**「**数据到位**」与「**数据被核签**」**是两个状态**；**② ⭐⭐⭐ 严格模式在你逐行核签之前**跑不起来**——**⭐ 即**核签是**前置条件**，**而不是**事后补的文档**；**③ ⭐⭐⭐ 那条测试**针对临时目录**断言，**而不是针对当前那份 CSV**——**⭐ 即**它测的是「**机器写不了**」这条**规则本身**，**而不是「**这一份文件当前恰好没有被机器写**」。**⭐⭐ ④ 改动必须**撤销签名****——**逐字两处**：**「**If `promote()` rewrites a row’s `source_citation`, it clears `verified_by` too: **a signature was made against what the old citation claimed.**」**与**「**If `promote()` overwrites a value you had already signed off on, it clears your `verified_by` for that row. **Your attestation was about the old number.**」**。**⭐ 即**签名**绑定**在「**当时那个引用与那个数值**」上**——**⭐ 数值或引用一变，**签名自动作废**。**⭐⭐⭐ ⑤ 它把「**空**」的含义写死，并要求部分佐证就承认是部分**——**逐字**：**「**A blank `corroborated_against` means not corroborated. It does not mean corroboration failed, and the loader never requires it. Partial corroboration stated as partial is worth more than complete attestation to a standard met on a sample.**」**；**并逐字说明「**这不是独立确认**」**：**「**It is corroboration, not independent confirmation. NVSR and WONDER are both NCHS products drawing on the same mortality file and the same Census-derived denominators. Agreement rules out a real class of error, namely a query returning the wrong slice, and says nothing about whether the underlying NCHS data is right.**」**。**⭐ 即**它区分了**三件事**：**未佐证**（**空白**）、**佐证失败**（**不存在这种状态**）、**同源机构之间的一致**（**不构成独立确认**）——**⭐ 本词条认为这与本站第 337 轮「**没有任何东西能站在单一来源上**」是同一族纪律，**而这里更进一步**：**它连「**两个来源一致**」也要追问这两个来源**是不是同一只手**。**⭐⭐⭐ ⑥ 佐证的**实际程度被逐条写明**，且**弱主张保持弱**——**次节逐字给出**：**十五个年度总计中的**十三个（2010–2022）**与对应 NVSR《Deaths: Final Data》报告的 Table B **完全一致**，**且计算出的粗死亡率与 NVSR 公布的率在**一位小数**上一致**；**2023 年的**计数**经 NVSR 74-11 佐证，**但其**率**未获佐证**（**逐字理由**「**because that report computes rates on a different population basis, at a precision too coarse to discriminate ours**」**）**；**2024 年**没有任何已发表来源**（**逐字**「**2024 has no published source at all, and blank means not corroborated rather than failed**」**）**；**并逐字说明列的设计意图**「**`corroborated_measures` records which measures each row’s source actually confirmed, so the weaker claim stays visibly weaker.**」。**⭐ 即**「**计数被佐证**」与「**率被佐证**」**被分开记**，**故**弱的那一个不会看起来和强的一样**。**⭐⭐ ⑦ 两处「**这个项目当前到哪**」的自我交代**——**README 开头逐字**：**「**Repository status: populated, attested, and running. Corroboration against NCHS’s published reports is partial and deliberately labelled as such: 14 of 15 annual totals.**」**（**⭐ 注意此处写 14，而正文写「**十三个 2010–2022 一致，**2023 的计数亦被佐证**」——**本词条把两处都如实转述，不替它调和**）**；**并指向** `STATUS.md`（**实测 53,244 字节**）**逐字说明它写的是**「**where the project stands, what is still open and in what order, and the known limits stated plainly**」**；**另有** `UAT_CHECKLIST.md`（19,073 字节）**与** `docs/denominator-methods.md`（31,398 字节）**。**⭐⭐ ⑧ 可核对性是**字节级**的**——**README 逐字**：**「**Inputs are four committed CDC WONDER exports and three U.S. Census population vintages. Each export carries WONDER’s own query-parameter footer and a SHA-256 that the test suite recomputes, so a reviewer receives the exact bytes the results were computed from**」**；**并逐字说明原始导出文件是**故意提交**的**（**「**The raw CDC WONDER export files in `data/raw/wonder_exports/` are **committed deliberately**, not by accident. They are the reproducibility artifact**」**）**。**⭐ 即**「**可复现**」在这里的具体含义是：**评审者拿到的是**当时算过的那些字节**，**而测试套件会**重算 SHA-256**。**⭐⭐ ⑨ 抓取路径本身也被约束**——**逐字给出三个子命令**（`--discover`／`--reconcile`／`--check`**，**其中** `--check` **逐字为**「**as `--reconcile`, exit non-zero on >0.5% drift**」**）**，**并逐字说明**「**Nothing in the fetch path writes to `data/raw/*.csv`; parsed output lands in `data/raw/fetched/` and only the explicit, default-dry-run `promote()` copies it across.**」**；**另有两条**「**不变量**」**逐字**：**「**Both exact identities: `sum(bands) + not_stated == annual deaths`, and `sum(bands) == annual population`, for all 15 years, with no tolerance.**」**与**「**The external check: the crude rate computed from these CSVs reproduces WONDER’s own published Crude Rate column for all 15 years.**」**。**⭐⭐ ⑩ 与池内条目的关系**：**本站 [[rki-excess-mortality]]、[[human-mortality-db]]、[[cmi-mortality-projections]]、[[mortalitylaws]]、[[demography]]、[[mortcast]] 覆盖死亡率数据与方法**，**[[great-expectations]]、[[reproducible-actuarial-work]]、[[verified-reserving]] 覆盖数据校验与可复现性**，**[[reliability-harness]] 覆盖「**怎么知道它可靠**」**——**⭐ 而本条补上的是**证据等级的分栏**：**引用、出处、人工核签、他方佐证四件分开**，**且每件都规定**谁能写**。**⚠️ 本词条如实标注**：**其主题（**美国死亡率与分母口径**）与本站主线**直接相关**，**但本次**未读任何数据行、未运行任何命令**。

**对 RIAA**：**本条与 [[rki-excess-mortality]]、[[cmi-mortality-projections]] 应当并读**——**它给的是**结论**（**人口老化主导粗死亡率上升，**尽管年龄别死亡率在改善**）**与**方法论**（**Kitagawa 分解、**四个分母口径边界**）**；**⭐ 而它对本站最有价值的是那**四列**：**把「**谁可以写这一格**」写进表结构**，**并让机器**写不了**核签那一栏**。

**⚠️ 本词条如实标注**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次没有运行该项目任何一步**（**未跑 bootstrap、未跑测试、未跑 `src.fetch` 或 `src.report`、未读任何 CSV 行**），**故不主张**其分解结果、佐证比例或数据不变量**按所述成立**。**② ⚠️⚠️ 未读 `STATUS.md`、`UAT_CHECKLIST.md`、`docs/denominator-methods.md` 的正文**（**本次只读其存在与字节数**），**故不主张**其中列出的未决事项、检查单与分母方法论细节。**⚠️ 本条目最需后续核实的一处**。**③ ⚠️ 未核实那些**外部断言**：**未访问 NVSR 的任何报告或表格、**未访问 CDC WONDER、**未核对「**十三个年度总计一致**」与「**2023 计数被佐证**」这两处说法**，**也未核实它自己指出的**「**NCHS 曾在两份报告中给出两个不同的 2020 年粗死亡率**」**这一说法**。**④ ⚠️ README 内部有一处**数字不一致**（**开头写 14 of 15，正文写十三个完全一致＋2023 计数亦被佐证**）**——**⭐ 本词条如实记录，**不替它调和、**也不据此判定谁对**（**可能口径不同**）**。**⑤ ⚠️ 未核实那条「**测试断言机器写不了 `verified_by`**」是否真的存在**（**未读测试代码**）**——**⭐ 本词条只转述原文**。**⑥ ⚠️ 未核实作者身份与该项目是否与任何机构有关**；**★0 不构成质量证据**。**⑦ ⚠️ 许可为 BSD-3-Clause**（**Zenodo 字段与仓库 `LICENSE` 一致**），**本次**未读许可正文**。**⑧ ⚠️ Zenodo 记录创建 2026-09-07 与仓库推送 2026-09-07 都在解冻窗口之内**，**故本条不需要窗口例外**；**⭐ 但本词条如实指出**：**「**四列证据等级 ＋ 机器不能写核签 ＋ 改动即撤销签名 ＋ 空白不等于失败**」这一组合，此前池内没有对应物**。**⑨ ⚠️ 本条目所记为 2026-09-11 所见**。 **⑩ ⚠️ 引号约定**：**本条目逐字引用英文原文时，把原文里的 ASCII 撇号（如 `export’s`、`row’s`、`NCHS’s`）写作 ’**——**以维持本词条不出现 ASCII 单引号的约定（引文内容未改）**。

The project at `terryfinberg/mortality-analysis`, archived on Zenodo, **decomposes United States crude death rates between 2010 and 2024**, with the full title stating that population aging dominates and that the denominator is not stable. **Measured this round**: on the Zenodo side, a version DOI, a concept DOI, **version 0.1.4**, resource type Software, **licence BSD-3-Clause**, **created and updated on 2026-09-07**, **a single file**, a creator with an ORCID, and one related identifier marked as supplementing a version-tagged GitHub path; on the GitHub side, **created 2026-09-01**, **last pushed 2026-09-07**, zero stars, Python, with a README of 31,176 bytes, **a status file of 53,244 bytes**, a user acceptance checklist of 19,073 bytes, a denominator methods document of 31,398 bytes and a licence file of 2,202 bytes. **This entry belongs to the round theme of evidence and citability, and this project writes evidence levels in more detail than anything else encountered this session.**

**Verified information, all measured from the README, the status file and the file listing**: **first, it splits four things into four columns and states who may write each.** The table headers are column, the claim, and who may write it. Citation is the claim about what the value is a copy of, derived from the export footer including its dataset name, query parameters, access date and SHA-256 hash, written by a derivation function. Provenance is a string recording the source export filename and hash, written by the fetch promotion step. Attestation is the claim that a person confirmed the value matches the cited export, and corroboration is the claim that a separate publication reports the same figure, and **both of those two may be written by a human only**. **Who wrote this cell is a column of the table rather than a matter of convention**, and the four claims are distinct: what file I copied, how this datum came to be here, whether anyone checked it against that file, and whether another publication reports the same number. **Second, it states verbatim why the split is necessary**: the split is the point rather than bookkeeping, because a number carrying a citation looks verified whether or not anyone verified it; an automated fetch does not solve that but changes the costume; and a run against the wrong dataset, or the right dataset with a wrong filter, writes an impeccably precise provenance string onto a wrong number and does so more convincingly than a hand transcription would. **This entry considers those three sentences the most important of the round, because the point is not that people make mistakes but that machines make mistakes that look correct.** **Third, it guarantees that no machine path can write the attestation column, and pins that impossibility with a test.** Verbatim, the attestation column is never machine-written, the promotion step fills the source type, provenance and citation fields and leaves attestation blank, which means an unverified-data error still fires after a successful fetch, promotion gets the numbers into place but does not sign them off, the reader does so row by row, and the loader will not run in strict mode until then. A second passage states that no machine path in the repository can write the attestation column and that a test asserts this against a temporary directory rather than against the current data files, **so what is tested is the rule rather than the accident that the current file happens to be unmarked**. **Fourth, changing anything clears the signature**: if the promotion step rewrites a citation it also clears the attestation, because a signature was made against what the old citation claimed, and if it overwrites a value that had been signed off it clears that attestation too, because the attestation was about the old number. **Fifth, it defines what blank means and insists that partial corroboration be labelled partial.** Verbatim, a blank corroboration field means not corroborated, it does not mean corroboration failed, and the loader never requires it; partial corroboration stated as partial is worth more than complete attestation to a standard met on a sample. It also states verbatim that this is corroboration rather than independent confirmation, because the two national sources are products of the same agency drawing on the same mortality file and the same census-derived denominators, so agreement rules out a real class of error and says nothing about whether the underlying data is right. **Three states are therefore distinguished: not corroborated, corroboration failed, which does not exist as a state, and agreement between two sources that are not independent.** **Sixth, the actual extent of corroboration is written out claim by claim, and the weaker claim is kept visibly weaker**: thirteen of fifteen annual totals between 2010 and 2022 match a table in the corresponding published final-data report exactly, and the computed crude rate matches the published rate to one decimal in all thirteen; the 2023 count is corroborated but not its rate, because that report computes rates on a different population basis at a precision too coarse to discriminate; 2024 has no published source at all, and blank means not corroborated rather than failed; and a dedicated column records which measures each row source actually confirmed, **so that the weaker claim does not end up looking like the stronger one**. **Seventh, two statements about where the project stands**: the README opens by describing the repository as populated, attested and running, with corroboration against the published reports partial and deliberately labelled as such, and points at a status file described verbatim as covering where the project stands, what is still open and in what order, and the known limits stated plainly, alongside a user acceptance checklist and a denominator methods document. **Eighth, checkability is at the byte level**: the inputs are four committed data product exports and three census population vintages, each export carries the data product own query-parameter footer and a SHA-256 that the test suite recomputes, so a reviewer receives the exact bytes from which the results were computed, and the raw exports are committed deliberately rather than by accident, described as the reproducibility artefact. **Ninth, the fetch path is itself constrained**: three subcommands offer discovery, reconciliation, and a check that exits non-zero on more than half a percent drift; nothing in the fetch path writes to the raw data files, parsed output lands in a separate fetched directory, and only an explicit, default-dry-run promotion copies it across; and two invariants are stated with no tolerance, that summed age bands plus an unspecified remainder equal annual deaths and that summed bands equal annual population, across all fifteen years, together with an external check that the computed crude rate reproduces the published crude rate column for every year. **Tenth, relative to existing entries**: the pooled mortality data and method entries supply sources and techniques, the pooled validation and reproducibility entries supply data checking, and the pooled reliability entry discusses how to know something is trustworthy, while **this entry supplies the grading of evidence into columns, with a rule for who may write each and a guarantee that the machine cannot sign.** **The subject matter of US mortality and denominator definitions is directly relevant to this wiki main line, but no data row was read and no command was run this round.**

**For RIAA**: **this entry reads alongside [[rki-excess-mortality]] and [[cmi-mortality-projections]]**, because **it supplies both a conclusion and a method**, and because **the four columns are the most transferable part: make who may write this cell part of the table structure, and make it impossible for the machine to sign the attestation column**.

**Marked honestly by this entry**: **first, no step of the project was run** — no bootstrap, no test suite, no fetch and no report — **so its decomposition results, its corroboration fractions and its data invariants are not claimed to hold as described**. **Second, the bodies of the status file, the acceptance checklist and the denominator methods document were not read**, only their existence and byte counts, **so the open items, checkpoints and methodological detail they contain are not claimed; this is the item most in need of later verification**. **Third, no external assertion was verified**: no published final-data report was visited, the national data product was not visited, and neither the claim of thirteen matching annual totals nor the corroborated 2023 count nor the claim that the agency itself published two different crude death rates for one year was checked. **Fourth, the README contains one internal numerical inconsistency**, describing corroboration as covering fourteen of fifteen totals in one place and as thirteen matching totals plus a corroborated count in another, **which this entry records without reconciling or adjudicating, since the two may use different definitions**. **Fifth, whether a test really asserts that no machine path can write the attestation column was not verified**, because no test code was read; the passage is relayed only. **Sixth, the creator identity and any institutional affiliation were not verified**, and zero stars is not evidence of quality. **Seventh, the licence is BSD-3-Clause by both the archive metadata and the repository licence file, whose text was not read. Eighth, both the archive record and the repository push fall on 2026-09-07 inside the thaw window, so no window exception is needed; however, the combination of four graded evidence columns, a machine that cannot sign, signatures cleared on change, and a blank that means not corroborated rather than failed had no counterpart in the pool. Ninth, this entry records what was visible on 2026-09-11. Tenth, quotation convention: ASCII apostrophes appearing inside quoted English were rendered as curved apostrophes so that this entry contains no ASCII single quote, with the quoted text otherwise unchanged.**
