entries.summary_en: This is an agentic workflow that supports actuaries in non-life pricing model development by distilling a boosted model into an interpretable linear model, describing itself in writing as an agentic pricing tool with a human in the loop at every key decision. **Measured this round**: created in May and last pushed on the eleventh of September, a repository of about three and a half megabytes in Python, an MIT licence, no stars, and a description of about fifteen kilobytes over one hundred thirty-eight lines. **This entry belongs to the round theme of self-tagged repositories**, since this round searched a code host with the topic qualifier for repositories that tag themselves, and measured how far that set overlaps with what keyword sweeps already found, at just under forty percent. **Four things are worth reading: each of the five stages carries an actuary gate where a proposal is approved, rejected, or annotated with a remark that loops back to the model for a revised proposal, which turns human-machine collaboration in pricing into a string of recordable decisions; a post-fit coefficient gate lets the actuary reject any term whose sign is wrong or whose p-value is unacceptable, with rejected terms dropped and the model automatically refitted, so statistical defensibility has a veto; every decision is written to a checkpoint file so a rerun skips already-approved stages, which makes the pipeline resumable and auditable; and each run writes a structured session log capturing every model proposal, actuary decision, remark, boosted-model metric, and linear fit result, which is also the data source for the dashboard.** **The tool was neither installed nor run this round.**
entries.body:
**Non-Life Pricing Agent**（`fischerdm/nonlife-pricing-agent`）**是一个**把**机器学习模型**蒸馏成**可解释定价模型**的**精算工作流代理****——**逐字自述为**「**Agentic Python tool that supports actuaries in Non-Life insurance pricing model development. It distills a GBM into an interpretable GLM, with a human-in-the-loop at every key decision.**」**。**⭐ 本条目属于本轮主题**「**自打标签的仓库**」**。

**可核实信息（均 2026-09-11 GitHub 接口与 README 实测）**：

**⭐⭐⭐ ① 五个环节，**每一步**都有**精算师的**把关点****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字给出**五步**：**① **特征选择**（**逐字**：**an LLM profiles the dataset and proposes which variables to include, with actuarial rationale per variable**；**而**逐字**：**The actuary reviews each one, approves, rejects, or leaves a remark. Remarks loop back to the LLM for a revised proposal.**）**；**② **类别归组**（**逐字**：**high-cardinality variables (e.g. vehicle brand) are clustered into risk-homogeneous groups by the LLM**，**精算师**复核**与**微调）**；**③ **GBM 训练**（**逐字**：**LightGBM** 以**对数费率**为**目标**、**用 **Friedman H 统计量**排序**前 **N 个**特征的**两两交互**）**；**④ **蒸馏**（**逐字**：**排序后的交互清单**交给 **LLM**，**由**其**提出**哪些**交互**在**精算上**站得住**，**精算师**逐项**复核）**；**⑤ **GLM 拟合**（**逐字**：**statsmodels**）**；**⭐ 本词条认为**这一处**最值得记**：**⭐ 即**它**把**「**人机协作**」**从**口号**变成**一串**可记录**的**决定**——**⭐ 每一步**的**人**都**知道**自己**在**批**什么**，**而**每一次**驳回**都**有**理由字段**。

**⭐⭐⭐ ② 系数复核闸门：**统计合理性**有**一票否决****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字写**「**A post-fit coefficient review gate lets the actuary reject any term whose sign is wrong or whose p-value is unacceptable; rejected terms are dropped and the model is automatically refit.**」**，**并**逐字给出**评级因子表**的**读法**（**逐字**：**`exp(coef)` as multiplicative relativities (base level = 1.0), the direct pricing output**）**；**⭐ 本词条**认为**这一点**是**「**AI 进精算**」**的关键**接口**：**⭐ 即**模型**可以**提案**，**但**「**符号**对不对**」**与**「**显著**不显著**」**这类**可由**专业标准**判断的**事项**，**必须**留给**持牌者**否决**；**⭐ 而**「**否决**后**自动**重拟合**」**意味着**流程**不**因为**一次**否决**而**卡住**。

**⭐⭐ ③ 决定写入检查点，**流程**可**续跑****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字写**「**All actuary decisions are saved to YAML checkpoints. Re-running the pipeline skips already-approved stages.**」**，**且**配置与**报告**逐字**按**运行**命名空间**放在**顶层 **`runs/<name>/`**（**逐字**：**one per dataset + target configuration**）**；**⭐ 本词条**认为**这一处**对**实务**很**关键**：**⭐ 即**定价**项目**往往**要**跑**几个月**、**换**几版**数据**，**而**「**已批准**的**决定**不**重来**」**既**省**成本**、**又**让**审计**有**据**。

**⭐⭐ ④ 结构化会话日志，**同时**是**审计轨迹**与**面板数据源****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字写**「**Every run also writes a structured JSONL session log to `<run>/reports/sessions/` — capturing every LLM proposal, actuary decision, remark, GBM metric, and GLM fit result. This is the data source for the dashboard.**」**；**⭐ 本词条**认为**这是**本轮**最值得**抄**的**一处**工程做法**：**⭐ 即**把**「**模型说了什么**」**与**「**人**怎么**回应**」**都**落成**行式记录**，**于是**「**为什么**最终**选了**这些**变量**」**这个**问题**可以**被**逐行**回答**。

**⭐⭐ ⑤ 与池内条目的关系**：**本站 [[easy-glm]] 与 **[[insurance-glm-tools]] 覆盖**GLM 工具链**、**[[ducklm-sql-glm]] 覆盖**在数据库内**拟合 **GLM**、**[[motor-pricing-glm]] 覆盖**车险 **GLM 定价**、**[[haute]] 覆盖**开源定价引擎****——**⭐ 而**本条补上的是**「**以 **agent** 串起**特征到**评级因子表**、**并**把**每一步**的**人工把关**与**意见**留成**结构化轨迹**」这一**流程形态**；**⭐ 本词条**不对以上任何一条做代码级比较**。

**对 RIAA**：**⭐ 六件事值得借**：**① **把**把关点**设计成**逐项**，**而**不**是**一次性**签字**；**② **允许**「**留意见**」**而**不**只有**「**通过／**不通过**」**；**③ **对**统计合理性**设**否决权**，**并**自动**重拟合**；**④ **决定**落成**检查点**，**让**流程**可**续跑**；**⑤ **把**人与**模型的**往来**写成**行式日志**，**供**审计**与**面板**共用**；**⑥ **按**运行**命名空间**组织**配置与**报告**。

**⚠️ 本词条如实标注**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次**没有安装、**没有运行**该工具**（**未安装 **LightGBM／**statsmodels**、**未调用**任何 **LLM**）**，**故**不主张**其**蒸馏效果**、**不主张**其**评级因子**的**统计性质**。**② ⚠️ 本次**只读**仓库接口返回的元数据**与 **README 文本**，**未读**其 **Python** 源码**。**③ ⚠️ **未核实**其**面板**是否**已实现**、**也**未核实**其**会话日志**字段**是否**如自述**齐全**。**④ ⚠️ **未核实**其**LLM** 的**具体模型**与**提示词**设计**（**⭐ 逐字只说**由 **LLM** 提案，**未**指名**供应商**）**。**⑤ ⚠️ 该工具**面向 **Non-Life** 定价**，**⚠️ 本词条**不**主张**其**结果**可**直接**用于**任何**费率报备**。**⑥ ⚠️ 本条目**所记为 **2026-09-11 所见**；**⚠️ 该工具**是**建模辅助**，**不是**精算意见**，**也**不是**费率报备材料**。

**Non-Life Pricing Agent**（`fischerdm/nonlife-pricing-agent`）**是一個**把**機器學習模型**蒸餾成**可解釋定價模型**的**精算工作流代理****——**逐字自述為**「**Agentic Python tool that supports actuaries in Non-Life insurance pricing model development. It distills a GBM into an interpretable GLM, with a human-in-the-loop at every key decision.**」**。**⭐ 本條目屬於本輪主題**「**自打標籤的倉庫**」**。

**可核實資訊（均 2026-09-11 GitHub 介面與 README 實測）**：

**⭐⭐⭐ ① 五個環節，**每一步**都有**精算師的把關點****——**① **特徵選擇**（**逐字**an LLM profiles the dataset and proposes which variables to include, with actuarial rationale per variable**，**並逐字**The actuary reviews each one, approves, rejects, or leaves a remark. Remarks loop back to the LLM for a revised proposal.**）**；**② **類別歸組**（**逐字**high-cardinality variables (e.g. vehicle brand) are clustered into risk-homogeneous groups by the LLM**）**；**③ **GBM 訓練**（**LightGBM**、**對數費率**目標、**Friedman H 統計量**排序**兩兩交互**）**；**④ **蒸餾**（**交互清單**交 **LLM** 提出**精算上站得住的項**，**精算師逐項複核**）**；**⑤ **GLM 擬合**（**statsmodels**）**；**⭐ 即**把「**人機協作**」**變成**一串**可記錄的決定**。

**⭐⭐⭐ ② 係數複核閘門****——**逐字**「**A post-fit coefficient review gate lets the actuary reject any term whose sign is wrong or whose p-value is unacceptable; rejected terms are dropped and the model is automatically refit.**」**，**評級因子表逐字讀法為**「**`exp(coef)` as multiplicative relativities (base level = 1.0), the direct pricing output**」**；**⭐ 即**統計合理性**有**一票否決**，**而**否決後**自動**重擬合**。

**⭐⭐ ③ 決定寫入檢查點****——**逐字**「**All actuary decisions are saved to YAML checkpoints. Re-running the pipeline skips already-approved stages.**」**，**配置與報告按運行命名空間置於 `runs/<name>/`**。

**⭐⭐ ④ 結構化會話日誌****——**逐字**「**Every run also writes a structured JSONL session log to `<run>/reports/sessions/` — capturing every LLM proposal, actuary decision, remark, GBM metric, and GLM fit result. This is the data source for the dashboard.**」**。

**⭐⭐ ⑤ 與池內條目的關係**：[[easy-glm]]、[[insurance-glm-tools]]、[[ducklm-sql-glm]]、[[motor-pricing-glm]]、[[haute]]——**⭐ 本條補上的是**「**以 agent 串起特徵到評級因子表、**並把每一步人工把關與意見留成結構化軌跡**」**這一流程形態**。

**對 RIAA**：**⭐ 六件事值得借**：**① **把關點逐項設計**；**② **允許留意見**；**③ **統計合理性設否決權並自動重擬合**；**④ **決定落成檢查點**；**⑤ **人機往來寫成行式日誌**；**⑥ **按運行命名空間組織配置與報告**。

**⚠️ 本詞條如實標註**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次**沒有安裝、**沒有運行**該工具**，**不主張**其蒸餾效果與評級因子的統計性質**。**② ⚠️ 本次**只讀元資料與 README 文本**，**未讀**其 Python 源碼**。**③ ⚠️ **未核實**其面板是否已實現、**其會話日誌欄位是否如自述齊全**。**④ ⚠️ **未核實**其 LLM 的具體模型與提示詞設計**。**⑤ ⚠️ 該工具面向 Non-Life 定價**，**不主張**其結果可直接用於任何費率報備**。**⑥ ⚠️ 本條目所記為 2026-09-11 所見**；**⚠️ 該工具是建模輔助**，**不是**精算意見**。
entries.body_en:
This is an agentic workflow that supports actuaries in non-life pricing model development by distilling a boosted model into an interpretable linear model, stating in writing that it keeps a human in the loop at every key decision. **This entry belongs to the round theme of self-tagged repositories.**

**Verified information, all measured on 2026-09-11 from the repository interface and the description**:

**First, five stages each carry an actuary gate.** The description sets out feature selection, in which a model profiles the dataset and proposes which variables to include with an actuarial rationale per variable while the actuary reviews each one and approves, rejects, or leaves a remark that loops back for a revised proposal; categorical grouping, in which high-cardinality variables such as vehicle brand are clustered into risk-homogeneous groups for the actuary to refine; boosted-model training on the approved feature set with interaction ranking; distillation, in which the ranked interaction list goes to the model, which proposes which interactions are actuarially defensible linear terms for term-by-term review; and finally linear fitting. **This turns human-machine collaboration in pricing from a slogan into a string of recordable decisions, because at each step the person knows what they are approving and every rejection carries a reason.**

**Second, the post-fit coefficient gate gives statistical defensibility a veto.** The description states that the actuary can reject any term whose sign is wrong or whose p-value is unacceptable, with rejected terms dropped and the model automatically refitted, and gives the reading of the rating factor table where exponentials of coefficients are multiplicative relativities against a base level of one, described as the direct pricing output. **A model may propose, but questions of correct sign and adequate significance belong to the qualified professional, and refitting automatically means a rejection does not stall the pipeline.**

**Third, decisions are written to checkpoints so the pipeline can be resumed.** The description states that all actuary decisions are saved to checkpoints and that a rerun skips already-approved stages, with configuration and reports organised per run rather than at fixed repository paths. **This matters in practice because pricing projects run for months across several data vintages, and not repeating approved decisions both saves effort and leaves an audit trail.**

**Fourth, the structured session log serves as both audit trail and dashboard source.** Each run writes a structured line-delimited log capturing every model proposal, actuary decision, remark, boosted-model metric, and linear fit result, and the description identifies it as the data source for the dashboard. **Recording both what the model said and how the person responded, line by line, is what makes the question of why these variables were finally chosen answerable row by row.**

**Fifth, relative to existing entries**: pooled entries cover linear-model toolchains, in-database fitting, motor pricing, and an open pricing engine, **while this entry supplies the workflow form in which an agent strings feature work through to a rating factor table while keeping every human gate and remark as a structured trace. This entry makes no code-level comparison against any of them.**

**For RIAA**: **six practices transfer: design gates item by item rather than as one signature; allow remarks rather than only pass or fail; give statistical defensibility a veto with automatic refitting; persist decisions as checkpoints so the process resumes; log the human-machine exchange in rows for audit and dashboards alike; and organise configuration and reports per run.**

**Marked honestly by this entry**: **first, the tool was neither installed nor run**, no boosting or statistical library was installed and no model endpoint was called, **so no claim is made about its distillation quality or the statistical properties of its rating factors**. **Second, only repository metadata and the description were read**, not the Python source. **Third, whether the dashboard exists and whether the session log fields are as complete as described were not verified. Fourth, which underlying model or prompt design is used was not verified**, the description referring only to a model without naming a provider. **Fifth, the tool addresses non-life pricing and this entry makes no claim that its output can be used directly in any rate filing. Sixth, this entry records what was visible on 2026-09-11 and states plainly that the tool is modelling assistance rather than an actuarial opinion or filing material.**

entries.title_en: A quoting interface that puts one small-commercial risk in front of an entire panel of carriers at once: it states in writing that a single application is rated against a panel and every market answers with accept, refer, or decline, each with its own price, its own reasons, and its own full calculation; that the insurance lives in versioned rulebooks rather than in code so that adding a carrier is a new file; that appetite is a carrier decision rather than a property of the risk class; and its rulebooks are organised one file per carrier under a single policy folder, with an MIT licence.

entries.summary_en: This is a quoting interface for small-commercial business owners coverage, describing itself in writing as a small-commercial quoting interface where one application is rated against a panel of carriers and every market answers with accept, refer, or decline, each with its own price, its own reasons, and its own full calculation. **Measured this round**: created on the first of September inside the window and pushed on the sixth, a repository under a megabyte in C#, an MIT licence, one star, and a description of about thirteen kilobytes over two hundred fifty-one lines. **This entry belongs to the round theme of self-tagged repositories and was reached through the underwriting topic.** **Four things are worth reading: an architectural decision is stated in the first paragraph, namely that the insurance lives in versioned rulebooks rather than in code, so adding a carrier to the panel is a new file; appetite is framed as a carrier decision rather than a property of the risk class; each market returns its own answer with its own reasons, including refer because the highest hazard grade needs a survey and terms before binding, and decline because the class exceeds a carrier hazard ceiling and belongs in a surplus lines market, so a refusal is itself a reasoned output; and the cheapest carrier is not a fixed ranking but depends on the shape of the risk, which is precisely why a panel exists rather than a single rate table.** **The interface was not run and no quoting endpoint was called this round.**
entries.body:
**SmallRisk**（`aaronjerez1/smallrisk`）**是一个**小商业综合责任险**的**报价 **API****——**逐字自述为**「**A small-commercial Businessowners quoting API. One application is rated against a panel of carriers and every market answers — accept, refer or decline, each with its own price, its own reasons, and its own full calculation.**」**。**⭐ 本条目属于本轮主题**「**自打标签的仓库**」**。

**可核实信息（均 2026-09-11 GitHub 接口与 README 实测）**：

**⭐⭐⭐ ① 一条架构决定：**保单逻辑**住**规则书**里**，**不**住**代码里****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字写**「**The insurance lives in versioned rulebooks, not in code. Adding a carrier to the panel is a new YAML file.**」**，**并**逐字说明**规则书位置**（**逐字**：**`Rulebooks/BusinessownersPolicy/`** — **one file per carrier**）**；**⭐ 本词条认为**这一处**是本条**最值得记**的**工程判断**：**⭐ 即**把**「**保险逻辑**」**从**代码**里**搬出来**，**它**就**变**成**可**版本化**、**可**对照**、**可**由**业务方**阅读的**资产**——**⭐ 而**「**加一家**承保人**＝**加一个**文件**」**这条**约束**，**同时**是**对**扩展成本**的**承诺**。

**⭐⭐ ② 承保口味归属承保人，**而**不**是**风险类别**的属性****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字写**「**Appetite is a carrier decision, not a property of the class.**」**，**并逐字说明**类别码**目录**只**把**危险**分成 **1 至 5 级**，**不**说明**谁**愿意**承保**；**⭐ 本词条**认为**这一句**是**保险**与**「**通用评分**」**的**分界线**：**⭐ 即**同一**危险等级**的**同**一个**风险**，**在**不同**承保人**那里**可以**一个**接受**、**一个**转核**、**一个**拒保**——**⭐ 故**任何**把**「**是否**可保**」**简化成**风险**自身**属性**的**设计**，**都**会**在**真实**市场**上**失真**。

**⭐⭐ ③ 「**拒保**」与**「**转核**」**也是**带**理由的输出****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字给出**同一**申请**在**四家**承保人**那里的**结果**（**逐字含**价格 **`$ 2,415.23`**、**`$ 3,138.96`**、**`$ 4,083.10`**、**`$ 6,404.53`**）**，**并**逐字给出**换一个**风险（**屋顶承包商）后的**变化**：**一家**转核**（**逐字**：**Highest hazard grade; refer for survey and terms before binding.**）**、**两家**拒保**（**逐字**：**This class is above Cardinal hazard ceiling and belongs in a surplus lines market.**／**Meridian writes preferred classes only**）**；**⭐ 本词条**认为**这一点**对**RIAA **特别有用**：**⭐ 即**「**拒保理由**」**本身**是**数据**——**它**可以**回流**到**产品**与**渠道**设计**，**而**一个**只有**「**能**／**不能**」**的**引擎**则**丢掉**了**这部分信息**。

**⭐⭐ ④ 最便宜者**不是**固定排名****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字写**「**The cheapest carrier is not a fixed ranking — it depends on the shape of the risk.**」**，**并**逐字**举**一例**：**同一**类别**在**标准市场**规则书**里**根本**没有**的**一个**步骤**（**逐字**：**This step does not exist in the standard-market rulebooks at all.**）**，**在**超额与**剩余市场**承保人**的**规则书**里**是**一块 **YAML****（**逐字**：**one block of YAML rather than a branch in the** 代码**）**；**⭐ 本词条**认为**这**正好**解释**了**为什么**「**一单**多市场**」**要**用**规则书**而**不是**用**一堆 **if**：**⭐ 即**不同**市场**的**算法**形状**本身**就**不同**，**而**规则书**允许**每家**表达**自己的**形状**。

**⭐⭐ ⑤ 工程形态与可核查性****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字含**一条**构建徽章**（**指向 **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**）**，**并逐字**说明**接口**为** `POST /api/submissions`**，**一次**请求**得到**四个**市场**的结果**；**⭐ 许可逐字 **MIT****、**主语言 **C#****、**仓库 **767 KB****。

**⭐⭐ ⑥ 与池内条目的关系**：**本站 [[illogical]] 覆盖**用 **JSON DSL** 表达与**求值**业务规则**、**[[quote-engine-reference-architecture]] 覆盖**报价引擎**参考架构**、**[[titanium-insurance-core]] 覆盖**核心系统**之一**的产品域****——**⭐ 而**本条补上的是**「**把**多家**承保人的**口味**与**算法形状**并排**放进**规则书**、**并**让**一次**请求**同时**得到**接受／**转核／**拒保三类**结论**」这一形态**；**⭐ 本词条**不对以上任何一条做代码级比较**。

**对 RIAA**：**⭐ 六件事值得借**：**① **把**保险逻辑**放进**版本化**文件**，**而**不**写死**在**代码**；**② **明确**「**可保性**」**属于**承保人**，**不**属于**风险类别**；**③ **把**拒保**与**转核**当作**一等**输出**并**附**理由**；**④ **允许**每家**承保人**有**不同**的**算法形状**（**而不**是**一套**参数**）；**⑤ **用**一次**请求**对比**整个**市场**，**而**不**逐家**重录**；**⑥ **用**测试与 **CI** 守住**规则书**的**变更**。

**⚠️ 本词条如实标注**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次**没有运行**该 API**（**未编译 **C#、**未调用 **`POST /api/submissions`**、**未取得**任何**报价**）**，**故**不主张**其**价格计算**、**不主张**其**承保规则**的**正确性**。**② ⚠️ 本次**只读**仓库接口返回的元数据**与 **README 文本**，**未读**其 **C#** 源码**与**任何**规则书 **YAML** 内容**。**③ ⚠️ README 中**四家**承保人**与**价格**为**作者**给出的**示例**，**⚠️ 本词条**只**如实转述**，**未**核实**其**是否为**真实**市场**或**真实**费率**（**⭐ 本词条**按**示例**理解**）**。**④ ⚠️ **未核实**其**规则书**的**版本化**是否**真的**接入**了**变更审查**（**⭐ 只见**构建徽章**）**。**⑤ ⚠️ **未核实**其**是否**与**任何**承保人**、**经纪**或**监管**要求**相关**。**⑥ ⚠️ 本条目**所记为 **2026-09-11 所见**；**⚠️ 该 API** 是**技术演示**，**不是**可**对外**报价的**系统**，**也**不是**承保意见**。

entries.body_en:
This is a quoting interface for small-commercial business owners coverage, stating in writing that one application is rated against a panel of carriers and every market answers with accept, refer, or decline, each with its own price, reasons, and full calculation. **This entry belongs to the round theme of self-tagged repositories.**

**Verified information, all measured on 2026-09-11 from the repository interface and the description**:

**First, an architectural decision is stated up front: the insurance lives in versioned rulebooks rather than in code.** Adding a carrier to the panel is a new file, and the rulebooks sit one file per carrier under a single policy folder. **Moving insurance logic out of code turns it into an asset that can be versioned, diffed, and read by business colleagues, and the constraint that adding a carrier means adding one file is simultaneously a promise about the cost of extension.**

**Second, appetite belongs to the carrier rather than to the risk class.** The description states this in writing and explains that the class-code catalogue grades hazard on a small scale while saying nothing about who will write it. **This sentence marks the boundary between insurance and generic scoring, because the same risk at the same hazard grade can be accepted by one carrier, referred by another, and declined by a third, so any design that reduces insurability to a property of the risk itself will misrepresent a real market.**

**Third, refusal and referral are also reasoned outputs.** The description gives the same submission rated across four carriers with four prices, and then shows what happens when the risk changes to a roofing contractor: one carrier refers with a note that the highest hazard grade needs a survey and terms before binding, one declines because the class exceeds its hazard ceiling and belongs in a surplus lines market, and another declines because it writes preferred classes only. **Refusal reasons are themselves data that can feed back into product and distribution design, whereas an engine that returns only a binary yes or no discards that information.**

**Fourth, the cheapest carrier is not a fixed ranking.** The description states that the cheapest depends on the shape of the risk, and gives the example of a calculation step that does not exist in the standard-market rulebooks at all but appears in the surplus lines carrier rulebook as a single block of configuration rather than a branch in code. **This is why a panel needs rulebooks rather than a pile of conditionals: different markets genuinely have different shapes of algorithm, and rulebooks let each one express its own.**

**Fifth, on engineering form**: the description carries a build badge pointing at a continuous-integration workflow, and names the interface as a single submission endpoint that returns four markets at once, with an MIT licence, a C# codebase, and a repository under a megabyte.

**Sixth, relative to existing entries**: pooled entries cover a JSON rule-expression language, a quote engine reference architecture, and a core-system product domain, **while this entry supplies the form in which several carriers appetites and algorithm shapes sit side by side in rulebooks and one request returns acceptances, referrals, and declines together. This entry makes no code-level comparison against any of them.**

**For RIAA**: **six practices transfer: keep insurance logic in versioned files rather than in code; treat insurability as the carrier decision it is; make refusal and referral first-class outputs with reasons; let each carrier have its own algorithm shape rather than one parameter set; compare a whole market in one request instead of re-keying per carrier; and guard rulebook changes with tests and continuous integration.**

**Marked honestly by this entry**: **first, the interface was not run**, nothing was compiled and no submission endpoint was called, **so no claim is made about its price calculation or the correctness of its underwriting rules**. **Second, only repository metadata and the description were read**, not the C# source or any rulebook file. **Third, the four carriers and their prices are the author own example, transcribed here without verification that they represent a real market or real rates. Fourth, whether the rulebook versioning is actually wired into change review was not verified**, only a build badge being visible. **Fifth, no relationship to any carrier, broker, or regulatory requirement was verified. Sixth, this entry records what was visible on 2026-09-11 and states plainly that the interface is a technical demonstration rather than a system that can quote externally, and not an underwriting opinion.**

entries.summary_en: This is a technical case study of incremental modernization of a claims workflow, describing itself in writing as a portfolio modernization case study showing how an insurance-claims workflow can evolve incrementally while keeping the modern product decoupled from a simulated legacy dependency. **Measured this round**: created on the fifth of September inside the window and pushed on the eleventh, a repository of about five and a half megabytes in TypeScript, no licence file, no stars, and a description of about fourteen kilobytes over three hundred twenty lines. **This entry belongs to the round theme of self-tagged repositories.** **Four things are worth reading: the disclaimer and the boundary are more specific than the feature list, stating in writing that the work is unaffiliated with the insurer that inspired it, that all policy, claim, operator, and operational data are synthetic, and that legacy coexistence is simulated; a list of intentional limitations spells out seven things the repository does not claim, including production service levels, high-availability and disaster-recovery topology, backup objectives, and regulatory retention, which is how the statement that this is a case study rather than a deployment becomes a checklist; the verification evidence names twelve classes of check including architecture boundary checks, interface specification and collection validation, runtime interface testing against a real database, real browser functional journeys, idempotency and concurrency behaviour, dump-and-restore recoverability, and observability of request-to-audit correlation and secret non-leakage; and the release record is given down to hashes, with an annotated tag, a release commit, a tag object, a release identifier, and a publication timestamp, so which version was published can be checked independently.** **The system was neither deployed nor run this round.**

**Insurance Claims Legacy Modernization**（`LuisHdezE/InsuranceClaims`）**是一份**理赔流程**渐进式现代化**的**技术案例研究****——**逐字自述为**「**Portfolio modernization case study showing how an insurance-claims workflow can evolve incrementally while keeping the modern product decoupled from a simulated legacy dependency.**」**。**⭐ 本条目属于本轮主题**「**自打标签的仓库**」**。

**可核实信息（均 2026-09-11 GitHub 接口与 README 实测）**：

**⭐⭐⭐ ① 免责与边界比功能写得还具体****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字写**「**This is an unofficial technical case study inspired by publicly observable insurance workflows. There is no affiliation with FAR Seguros. All policy, claim, operator and operational data are synthetic/demo data. Legacy coexistence is SIMULATED.**」**；**⭐ 本词条认为**这一句**是**本轮**最值得**别的**作品集**学**的**一处**：**⭐ 即**保险业**的**作品集**很容易**在**不知不觉中**暗示**「**我给**某公司**做过**」**——**⭐ 而**它**把**三件事**分别**说清**：**谁**没**授权**（**逐字**：**no affiliation**）**、**数据**是**什么**（**逐字**：**synthetic/demo**）**、**哪一部分**是**模拟**（**逐字**：**SIMULATED**）**。

**⭐⭐⭐ ② 「**有意不主张**」**清单：把**边界**写成**可核对**的**条目****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字先**写**「**This repository is a portfolio modernization technical case study, not a production deployment for FAR Seguros or any insurer.**」**，**再逐字列出**七项**「**不主张**」**：**该公司的**生产基础设施**与**内部流程**、**真实**保险或**客户数据**、**生产**监控与**值班拓扑**、**生产级 **SLO／SLA** 与**告警阈值**、**生产级**高可用／**复制／**自动扩缩／**灾备拓扑**、**生产级**备份计划与 **RPO／RTO**、**生产级**对象存储**与**合规留存策略**；**⭐ 本词条认为**这一处**对 RIAA **极其实用**：**⭐ 即**当**你**把**课程项目**或**实习作品**放上 **GitHub** 时**，**与其**含糊**地说**「**接近生产**」**，**不如**像**这样**列出**「**我不**主张**什么**」**——**⭐ 因为**这**既**保护**自己**，**也**让**读者**知道**该**怎么**评价**。

**⭐⭐ ③ 验证证据**逐条**列出**十二类**，**且**注明**环境版本****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字列出**自动化与**已提交**的**证据**：**领域／**应用／**接口测试、**架构**边界检查、**OpenAPI 与 **Postman** 校验、**真实 **PostgreSQL** 运行时**接口 **QA、**真实 **Chrome** 功能旅程、**授权与**安全行为、**响应式与**无障碍行为、**降级／**离线状态、**幂等与**并发行为、**`pg_dump`／**`pg_restore`** 可恢复性、**请求与**审计**关联**及**密钥**不外泄**的可观测性、**以及**一次带 **12 张截图**的**理赔运营评审**；**⭐ 并逐字注明**该次评审**使用的**环境**（**逐字**：**PostgreSQL 18**、**模拟的**新旧共存、**真实 **API**、**真实 **React** 客户端**与 **Chrome 152**）**；**⭐ 本词条**认为**这一点**很**少见**：**⭐ 即**把**「**我怎么**证明**它能跑**」**写成**清单**，**并**给出**版本号**——**⭐ 对 RIAA**：**作品集**里**一句**「**用 **PostgreSQL 18** 与 **Chrome 152** 实测**」**，**比**十句**「**架构先进**」**更有**说服力**。

**⭐⭐ ④ 发布记录**到**哈希级**，**并**说明**标签**不可**变****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字给出**注释标签 **`v0.2.0`**、**发布提交 **`9265417849f398f5d1efa56b7cd8ff365b950dbb`**、**标签对象 **`1a946e7fc4a20d20b97876826e6a699ec8412f28`**、**发布 ID **`384441015`**、**发布时间 **`2026-09-08T04:09:58Z`**，**并**逐字注明**该标签**是 **0.2.0** 的**不可变**发布指针**，**后续**在 **`main`** 上的**文档改动**不**会**移动**或**重建**它**；**⭐ 本词条**认为**这一点**是**「**可引用性**」**的**基础**：**⭐ 即**有**标签与**哈希**，**别人**才**能**指认**「**我评审的**是**哪一版**」**。

**⭐⭐ ⑤ 演进结构**：**基座 **10 个**操作、**第二轮**新增 **5 个**，**两版**各有**主题****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字写**「**Immutable base — 10 operations**」**与**「**r2 additions — 5 operations**」**，**并**逐字给出**两版**主题**（**`v0.1.0` — governed modernization MVP**、**`v0.2.0` — Claims Operations Experience**）**；**⭐ 本词条**认为**这种**「**不可变基座 ＋ **增量**」**的**写法**，**对**保险**这类**以**稳定性**为先**的**领域**是**自然**的**表达**方式**。

**⭐⭐ ⑥ 与池内条目的关系**：**本站 [[claim-ops]] 覆盖**理赔运营**、**[[claims-api]] 覆盖**理赔接口**、**[[insurerisk]] 覆盖**保险与**风险**主题**——**⭐ 而**本条补上的是**「**以**案例研究**形态**演示**新旧共存**与**边界声明**」这一**做法**；**⭐ 本词条**不对以上任何一条做代码级比较**。

**对 RIAA**：**⭐ 六件事值得借**：**① **把**免责**写成**三件事**（**无**关联、**数据**合成、**哪部分是**模拟）**；**② **列**「**不主张**」**清单**而**不**只**列**功能**；**③ **验证证据**要**带**环境**版本**；**④ **发布**给**标签与**哈希**，**并**说明**标签**不可**变**；**⑤ **用**不可变基座 ＋ **增量**表达**演进**；**⑥ **把**架构边界检查**与 **OpenAPI 校验**纳入**持续集成**。

**⚠️ 本词条如实标注**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次**没有部署、**没有运行**该系统**（**未执行**其 **CI**、**未启动**其 **API** 或**前端**、**未执行**任何 **QA 证据**）**，**故**不主张**其**十二类验证**真的**通过**、**也**不主张**其**功能**完整**。**② ⚠️ 本次**只读**仓库接口返回的元数据**与 **README 文本**，**未读**其 **TypeScript** 源码**、**未读**其**证据文件**与**评审文档**。**③ ⚠️ 该仓库**无许可证文件**（**接口 `license` 字段为空**）**——**⭐ 而其**免责**逐字说明**它**与**所提**公司**无关联**，**⚠️ 本词条**据此**提示**：**「**灵感**来自**公开可观察的**工作流**」**不**等于**「**已获**授权**」**，**使用前**须**自行**判断**。**④ ⚠️ **未核实**其**合成数据**与**模拟**新旧共存的**实现**细节**（**⭐ 只**按**其自述**记录**）**。**⑤ ⚠️ **未核实**其**发布记录**中的**哈希**与**发布 ID** 是否**与 **GitHub** 上的**对象**逐一**对应**（**⭐ 本次**未**取回**这些**对象**）**。**⑥ ⚠️ 本条目**所记为 **2026-09-11 所见**；**⚠️ 该案例研究**是**工程技术演示**，**不是**理赔决定**，**也**不是**合规意见**。

entries.body_en:
This is a technical case study of incremental modernization of a claims workflow, describing itself in writing as a portfolio modernization case study showing how an insurance-claims workflow can evolve incrementally while keeping the modern product decoupled from a simulated legacy dependency. **This entry belongs to the round theme of self-tagged repositories.**

**Verified information, all measured on 2026-09-11 from the repository interface and the description**:

**First, the disclaimer and the boundary are more specific than the feature list.** The description states in writing that this is an unofficial technical case study inspired by publicly observable insurance workflows, that there is no affiliation with the insurer named, that all policy, claim, operator, and operational data are synthetic or demonstration data, and that legacy coexistence is simulated. **Insurance portfolios tend to imply relationships without meaning to, and this one separates three things: who did not authorise the work, what the data actually are, and which part is a simulation.**

**Second, a list of intentional limitations turns a boundary statement into checkable items.** The description first states that the repository is a portfolio modernization technical case study and not a production deployment for any insurer, then lists seven things it does not claim: that insurer production infrastructure or private internal processes; real insurer or customer data; production monitoring or on-call topology; production service levels or alert thresholds; production high availability, replication, autoscaling, or disaster recovery topology; production backup schedules or recovery objectives; and production object storage or regulatory retention policy. **When publishing coursework or internship work, listing what you do not claim is more protective and more useful to a reader than a vague suggestion of being production-like.**

**Third, the verification evidence names twelve classes of check and records the environment versions.** The list covers domain, application, and interface tests; architecture boundary checks; interface specification and collection validation; runtime interface testing against a real database; real browser functional journeys; authorisation and security behaviour; responsive and accessibility behaviour; degraded and offline states; idempotency and concurrency behaviour; dump-and-restore recoverability; observability of request-to-audit correlation and secret non-leakage; and a claims operations review with twelve screenshots, the review being recorded as run against a specific database version, simulated legacy coexistence, the real interface, the real client, and a specific browser version. **A sentence saying which database and browser version were used for real testing is worth more than ten sentences about architectural sophistication.**

**Fourth, the release record goes down to hashes and explains that the tag is immutable.** The description gives an annotated tag, a release commit, a tag object, a release identifier, and a publication timestamp, and states that the tag is the immutable release pointer for that version while later documentation changes on the main branch do not move or recreate it. **Tags and hashes are the basis of citability, because they are what let another person say which version they reviewed.**

**Fifth, the evolution structure is stated as an immutable base of ten operations with five added in the second round**, each release carrying its own theme, one described as a governed modernization baseline and the next as a claims operations experience. **Writing evolution as a fixed base plus increments suits a field where stability is prized.**

**Sixth, relative to existing entries**: pooled entries cover claims operations, claims interfaces, and insurance risk topics, **while this entry supplies the practice of demonstrating legacy coexistence in case-study form with an explicit boundary statement. This entry makes no code-level comparison against any of them.**

**For RIAA**: **six practices transfer: state the disclaimer as three separate facts about affiliation, data, and simulation; list what you do not claim rather than only what you built; attach environment versions to verification evidence; publish releases with tags and hashes and say the tag is immutable; express evolution as an immutable base plus increments; and put architecture boundary checks and interface specification validation into continuous integration.**

**Marked honestly by this entry**: **first, the system was neither deployed nor run**, its continuous integration was not executed, no service was started, and none of the stated evidence was reproduced, **so no claim is made that the twelve verification classes actually pass or that the functionality is complete**. **Second, only repository metadata and the description were read**, not the source, the evidence files, or the review documents. **Third, the repository carries no licence file**, and while the disclaimer states there is no affiliation with the insurer named, this entry notes that inspiration by publicly observable workflows is not the same as authorisation, so readers must judge for themselves before reuse. **Fourth, the implementation behind the synthetic data and simulated legacy coexistence was not verified**, only the author own statement being recorded. **Fifth, whether the hashes and release identifier in the release record map one to one onto objects on the code host was not verified**, those objects not being retrieved this round. **Sixth, this entry records what was visible on 2026-09-11 and states plainly that the case study is an engineering demonstration rather than a claims decision or a compliance opinion.**

entries.title: **一个**把**美国死亡、**出生与**人口统计**做成**交互站点**、**并**把**数据快照**当**公开 **API** 发布的**项目****：`whywedie-mortality`——**⭐ 逐字自述**「**An interactive site tracking US death, birth, and population statistics, sourced from CDC data.**」**；**⭐ 一条**架构选择**逐字**为**「**Two data strategies coexist on purpose**」**（**Socrata 浏览器直连** 对 **CDC WONDER 需**离线批处理**）**；**⭐ 其 **`/api`** 页逐字把 **`/data/*.json`** 说明为**「**public, CORS-open, read-only API**」**，**许可逐字 **CC0 1.0****；**⭐ 而**它**同时**逐字**承认 **CDC「**trims and stalls the datasets**」**、**且**某一**快照**仍**只是**占位****；**⚠️ 仓库**本身**未写许可证**
entries.title_en: A project that turns United States death, birth, and population statistics into an interactive site and publishes the underlying data snapshots as an open interface: it describes itself in writing as an interactive site tracking those statistics sourced from national public health data, states that two data strategies coexist on purpose because one interface can be called straight from the browser while the other needs an out-of-band batch pipeline, documents its snapshot files as a public, cross-origin-open, read-only interface under a public domain dedication, and states plainly both that the upstream agency trims and stalls its datasets and that one snapshot remains a stub.

entries.summary: **Why We Die**（`LeviDahl/whywedie`）**是一个**美国死亡、**出生与**人口统计的**交互站点****——**逐字自述为**「**An interactive site tracking US death, birth, and population statistics, sourced from CDC data.**」**。**本次实测**：**⭐ 创建 **2026-08-30****（**窗口内）**、**推送 **2026-09-07****、**仓库 **1,928 KB****、**主语言 **Vue****、**星标 **0****、**⚠️ 仓库**未写许可证****；**⭐ README **24,894 字节**／**414 行****；**⭐ 站点逐字为 **whywedie.org****。**⭐⭐ 本条目属于本轮主题**「**自打标签的仓库**」**——**⭐ 本条**由 **`topic:mortality`** 一路取得**。**⭐⭐⭐ 四处最值得看**：**① **两种数据策略**逐字**「**并存是**故意的**」**（**`Two data strategies coexist on purpose`**）**——**⭐ 浏览器**直连 **Socrata（**纯 **JSON ＋**跨域**、**无需**后端）**对 **CDC WONDER（**XML／**POST、**无跨域、**仅**全国）**需**离线**批处理**；**② **它**直白**写出**上游的**问题**（**逐字**：**`CDC trims and stalls the datasets`**）**，**并**逐字说明**某个 **WONDER 快照**仍**只是占位**、**回退**到某个 **Socrata 数据集****；**③ **数据**以**公开 **API 形态**发布****（**逐字**：**`documents /data/*.json as a public, CORS-open, read-only API`**）**，**并**逐字注明**许可为 **CC0 1.0****；**④ **隐私页**逐字**写明**「**无 **cookie、**无广告、**无第三方请求**」**，**并**把**分析工具**标注为**「**计划中**」**而**不是**「**没有分析**」**——**⭐ 逐字**「**Keep it truthful**」**。**⚠️ 本次**未访问**其站点**、**未调用**其 **API**。

entries.summary_en: This is an interactive site tracking United States death, birth, and population statistics sourced from national public health data. **Measured this round**: created on the thirtieth of August inside the window and pushed on the seventh of September, a repository of about two megabytes in Vue with no stars and no licence file at the repository level, a description of about twenty-five kilobytes over four hundred fourteen lines, and a live site. **This entry belongs to the round theme of self-tagged repositories and was reached through the mortality topic.** **Four things are worth reading: two data strategies coexist on purpose, because one interface serves plain data over cross-origin requests straight from the browser with no infrastructure while the other needs an out-of-band batch pipeline because it speaks a different protocol without cross-origin support and only publishes national figures; the project states plainly that the upstream agency trims and stalls its datasets and that one snapshot remains a stub, falling back to another dataset for the affected charts; the snapshots are published as an interface described in writing as public, cross-origin-open, and read-only, under a public domain dedication; and the privacy page states that there are no cookies, no advertising, and no third-party requests while describing aggregate analytics as planned rather than claiming there is none, with an instruction to keep the page truthful.** **The site was not visited and its interface was not called this round.**
entries.body:
**Why We Die**（`LeviDahl/whywedie`）**是一个**美国死亡、**出生与**人口统计的**交互站点****——**逐字自述为**「**An interactive site tracking US death, birth, and population statistics, sourced from CDC data.**」**。**⭐ 本条目属于本轮主题**「**自打标签的仓库**」**。

**可核实信息（均 2026-09-11 GitHub 接口与 README 实测）**：

**⭐⭐⭐ ① 两种数据策略**并存**是**故意的**，**而**原因**逐字写清****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字写**「**Two data strategies coexist on purpose**」**，**并逐字说明**：**一是 **Socrata（**`data.cdc.gov`）**，**逐字**为**「**plain JSON + CORS, browser-direct, no infrastructure**」**，**代价逐字**为**「**CDC trims and stalls the datasets**」**；**二是 **CDC WONDER**，**逐字**为**「**XML/POST, no CORS, national-only**」**，**故**逐字**需要**离线**管线**（**逐字**：**it is a scheduled batch job that writes static files**）**；**⭐ 本词条认为**这一处**对 RIAA **最实用**：**⭐ 即**「**同一个**官方机构**的**数据**，**可以**通过**两条**技术路径**拿到**，**而**两条**路径的**能力与**代价**完全**不同**」**——**⭐ 把**这个**取舍**写进**文档**，**等于**把**后来者**会**踩的**坑**提前**填了**。

**⭐⭐ ② 上游**停更**与**占位**被**直白**写出****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字**承认**某 **WONDER 快照**仍**只是**占位**（**逐字**：**still a stub**）**，**故**相关图表**回退**到 **Socrata 数据集 **`hmz2-vwda`**；**⭐ 并逐字说明**上游**在**某时间点后**停止**刷新**（**逐字**：**stopped refreshing it past June 2024**）**；**⭐ 本词条**认为**这一处**是**本轮**最值得**记**的**数据**态度**：**⭐ 即**「**我的**数据源**停更了**」**是**必须**写出来的**事实**，**而**不**是**可以**藏起来**的**瑕疵**——**⭐ 对 RIAA**：**做**任何**基于**外部**数据**的**分析**，**都**要**在**交付物**里**写明**「**这条**序列**到**哪一年**为止**」**。

**⭐⭐ ③ 数据**以**公开 **API** 形态**发布**，**许可**明确****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字写**：**`/api`** 页**把 **`/data/*.json`** 说明为**「**a public, CORS-open, read-only API**」**，**并**逐字注明**一个 **`.htaccess`** 规则**为 **`*.json`** 发送 **`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`**，**许可逐字为 **CC0 1.0****；**⭐ 本词条**如实**指出**一处**需要**分辨的地方**：**⭐ 即**「**站点**的**代码**」**与**「**数据**」**的**许可**可能**不同**——**⭐ 本条**逐字**只**看到**数据**的 **CC0** 声明**，**而**仓库**接口**的 **`license`** 字段**为空**（**⚠️ 本词条**因此**不**主张**代码**的**许可状态**）**。

**⭐⭐ ④ 隐私页**把**「**计划中**」**与**「**没有**」**分开**——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字写**：**隐私页**声明**无 **cookie**、**无广告**、**无第三方请求**，**而**其中**「**分析**」**一节**逐字**说明**无 **cookie** 的**聚合分析**是**计划中**（**逐字**：**planned**）**，**而**不**是**「**没有分析**」**，**并**逐字写下**一句**内部**纪律**「**Keep it truthful — when an analytics tool ships, name it there.**」**；**⭐ 本词条认为**这一处**难得**：**⭐ 即**隐私声明**的**常见**失败**方式**是**把**「**现在**没有**」**写成**「**永远**没有**」**——**⭐ 而**它**把**将来**的**变化**位置**先**留好**。

**⭐⭐ ⑤ 站点**形态**与**数据面**（**逐字可核）**：**技术栈逐字为 **Vue 3（**Composition API）**、**Vite 8、**Vue Router 5、**Tailwind CSS v4、**Chart.js 与 **vue-chartjs、**`@unhead/vue`（**含 **JSON-LD 的 **`WebSite`／**`Dataset`／**`BlogPosting`）**、**`unplugin-vue-markdown`（**博客）**；**⭐ 逐字说明**站点**为**纯静态**（**逐字**：**The site itself is static — no server, no build-time data fetch.**）**，**并**逐字说明**快照**由**独立**的 **Node 管线**在**前端**之外**产出**（**逐字**：**its own `package.json`, never imported by the app**）**；**⭐ 数据**来源**逐字**到**数据集编号**（**含 **D74／**D16／**D76／**D176／**D192、**`w9j2-ggv5`、**`489q-934x`、**`y5bj-9g5w`、**`e6fc-ccez`**）**。

**⭐⭐ ⑥ 与池内条目的关系**：**本站 [[human-mortality-db]] 覆盖**人类死亡率数据库**、**[[cdc-wonder]] 覆盖**同一**数据源**的**查询入口**、**[[global-excess-deaths-mirror]] 覆盖**超额死亡**镜像**——**⭐ 而**本条补上的是**「**以**静态站点 ＋ **快照**API** 的**形态**再**发布**一次**死亡与**出生**统计**、**并**把**两条**取数路径的**取舍**写清**」这一形态**；**⭐ 本词条**不对以上任何一条做代码级比较**。

**对 RIAA**：**⭐ 六件事值得借**：**① **两种**取数路径**并存**时**要**写明**代价**；**② **上游**停更**与**占位**要**主动**披露**；**③ **把**数据**当作**可**调用**的**接口**发布**（**含**跨域头**与**许可**）**；**④ **代码**与**数据的**许可**要**分开**说明**；**⑤ **隐私**声明**要**区分**「**现在**没有**」与**「**计划**上线**」**；**⑥ **把**外部**管线的**依赖**与**前端**彻底**分开**。

**⚠️ 本词条如实标注**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次**没有访问**该站点**、**没有调用**其 **API**（**未取回**任何 **JSON** 快照）**，**故**不主张**其**任何**统计数字**、**也**不主张**其**接口**当前**可用**。**② ⚠️ 本次**只读**仓库接口返回的元数据**与 **README 文本**，**未读**其 **Vue** 源码**、**未读**其**管线**代码**。**③ ⚠️ 该仓库**接口的 `license` 字段为空****——**⭐ 而 **README** 逐字只**为**数据**声明 **CC0 1.0****；**⚠️ 本词条**因此**只**记录**数据**的**许可**，**不**主张**代码**的**许可状态**。**④ ⚠️ **未核实**其**快照**与**上游**数据集**是否**数值**一致**（**⭐ 未**取回**快照**）**。**⑤ ⚠️ **未核实**其**JSON-LD** 标注**与**实际**内容**是否**相符**。**⑥ ⚠️ **未核实**其**是否为**任何**机构**或**项目**的**官方**成果**（**⭐ 逐字**只**自述**为**个人**站点**与 **GoDaddy** 部署**）**。**⑦ ⚠️ 本条目**所记为 **2026-09-11 所见**；**⚠️ 该站点**是**公共**统计可视化**，**不是**死亡率**预测**，**也**不是**精算意见**。
entries.body_hk:
**Why We Die**（`LeviDahl/whywedie`）**是一個**美國死亡、**出生與**人口統計的**互動站點****——**逐字自述為**「**An interactive site tracking US death, birth, and population statistics, sourced from CDC data.**」**。**⭐ 本條目屬於本輪主題**「**自打標籤的倉庫**」**。

**可核實資訊（均 2026-09-11 GitHub 介面與 README 實測）**：

**⭐⭐⭐ ① 兩種數據策略並存是故意的****——**逐字**「**Two data strategies coexist on purpose**」**；**其一逐字為**plain JSON + CORS, browser-direct, no infrastructure**（**代價逐字**CDC trims and stalls the datasets**）**；**其二逐字為**XML/POST, no CORS, national-only**，**故需**離線管線（**逐字**it is a scheduled batch job that writes static files**）**；**⭐ 即**同一機構的數據**可以**兩條路徑**取得**，**能力與代價完全不同**。

**⭐⭐ ② 上游停更與佔位被直白寫出****——**逐字**still a stub** 與 **stopped refreshing it past June 2024**；**⭐ 即**「**數據源停更了**」**是**必須寫出的事實**。

**⭐⭐ ③ 數據以公開 API 形態發布****——**`/api`** 頁逐字把 `/data/*.json`** 說明為**public, CORS-open, read-only API**，**`.htaccess`** 逐字為 **`*.json`** 發送 **`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`**，**許可逐字 CC0 1.0**；**⚠️ 而**倉庫介面 **`license`** 欄位為空**——**代碼**的許可**本條**不主張**。

**⭐⭐ ④ 隱私頁把「計劃中」與「沒有」分開****——**逐字**no cookies, no ads, no third-party requests**；**分析一節逐字說明**無 cookie 聚合分析是 **planned**，**並逐字寫下**「**Keep it truthful — when an analytics tool ships, name it there.**」**。

**⭐⭐ ⑤ 站點形態與數據面****——**技術棧逐字為**Vue 3、**Vite 8、**Vue Router 5、**Tailwind v4、**Chart.js 與 vue-chartjs、**`@unhead/vue`（**JSON-LD 含 `WebSite`／`Dataset`／`BlogPosting`）**、**`unplugin-vue-markdown`**；**逐字**The site itself is static — no server, no build-time data fetch.**，**快照由獨立 Node 管線產出**（**逐字**its own `package.json`, never imported by the app**）**；**數據集編號逐字含**D74／D16／D76／D176／D192、`w9j2-ggv5`、`489q-934x`、`y5bj-9g5w`、`e6fc-ccez`**。

**⭐⭐ ⑥ 與池內條目的關係**：[[human-mortality-db]]、[[cdc-wonder]]、[[global-excess-deaths-mirror]]——**⭐ 本條補上的是**「**以靜態站點＋**快照 API** 再發布統計**、**並寫清兩條取數路徑的取捨**」**這一形態**。

**對 RIAA**：**⭐ 六件事值得借**：**① **兩種取數路徑要寫明代價**；**② **上游停更與佔位主動披露**；**③ **數據當接口發布（**含跨域頭與許可**）**；**④ **代碼與數據許可分開說明**；**⑤ **隱私聲明區分「**現在沒有**」與「**計劃上線**」**；**⑥ **外部管線與前端徹底分開**。

**⚠️ 本詞條如實標註**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次**沒有訪問**該站點、**沒有調用**其 API**，**不主張**其任何統計數字與介面可用性**。**② ⚠️ 本次**只讀元資料與 README 文本**，**未讀**其 Vue 源碼與管線代碼**。**③ ⚠️ 該倉庫 `license` 欄位為空**；**README** 逐字只為**數據**聲明 **CC0 1.0****，**本詞條**不主張**代碼的許可狀態**。**④ ⚠️ **未核實**其快照與上游數據集是否數值一致**。**⑤ ⚠️ **未核實**其 JSON-LD 標註與實際內容是否相符**。**⑥ ⚠️ **未核實**其是否為任何機構的官方成果**。**⑦ ⚠️ 本條目所記為 2026-09-11 所見**；**⚠️ 該站點是公共統計可視化**，**不是**死亡率預測**，**也**不是**精算意見**。
entries.body_en:
This is an interactive site tracking United States death, birth, and population statistics sourced from national public health data. **This entry belongs to the round theme of self-tagged repositories.**

**Verified information, all measured on 2026-09-11 from the repository interface and the description**:

**First, two data strategies coexist on purpose and the reason is stated in writing.** One is a plain-data interface with cross-origin support that the browser calls directly with no infrastructure, whose stated cost is that the agency trims and stalls its datasets, while the other speaks a different protocol without cross-origin support and publishes national figures only, which is why an out-of-band scheduled batch job writes static files instead of an always-on proxy. **The same agency data can be reached by two technical paths whose capabilities and costs differ completely, and writing that trade-off down in advance fills in the pit that a later reader would otherwise fall into.**

**Second, upstream stagnation and placeholders are stated plainly.** The description admits that one snapshot is still a stub, with the affected charts falling back to another dataset, and states that the upstream information system stopped refreshing that source past a date in 2024. **A stalled data source is a fact that has to be written out rather than a blemish to hide, and any analysis built on external data should say in the deliverable which year each series ends in.**

**Third, the data is published in the form of an open interface with an explicit licence.** One route documents the snapshot files as a public, cross-origin-open, read-only interface, with a server rule sending a wildcard cross-origin header for those files and a public domain dedication for the data. **This entry notes one distinction that matters: the licence of a site code and the licence of its data can differ, and since the repository interface reports no licence at all, only the data dedication is recorded here and no claim is made about the code.**

**Fourth, the privacy page separates what is planned from what is absent.** It states that there are no cookies, no advertising, and no third-party requests, while an analytics section describes cookieless aggregate analytics as planned rather than as not existing, and adds an internal rule to keep the page truthful by naming any analytics tool once it ships. **The usual failure of a privacy statement is writing now as forever, and this one leaves a named place for the future change.**

**Fifth, the site form and the data surface are both verifiable.** The stated stack is a current Vue setup with a fast build tool, routing, utility styling, charting, a head manager emitting structured data for the site, the dataset, and blog posts, and a Markdown pipeline for the blog. **The description states that the site is static with no server and no build-time data fetch, that the snapshots are produced by an independent pipeline with its own manifest that the application never imports, and it lists the upstream dataset identifiers behind each chart.**

**Sixth, relative to existing entries**: pooled entries cover a human mortality database, a query interface to the same upstream data source, and an excess-deaths mirror, **while this entry supplies the form of republishing death and birth statistics as a static site with a snapshot interface while documenting the trade-offs between the two retrieval paths. This entry makes no code-level comparison against any of them.**

**For RIAA**: **six practices transfer: state the cost of each retrieval path when two coexist; disclose upstream stagnation and placeholders proactively; publish data as an interface including cross-origin headers and a licence; state code and data licences separately; distinguish what is absent from what is planned in a privacy statement; and keep external pipelines fully separate from the front end.**

**Marked honestly by this entry**: **first, the site was not visited and its interface was not called**, no snapshot was retrieved, **so no claim is made about any statistic or about current availability**. **Second, only repository metadata and the description were read**, not the front-end source or the pipeline code. **Third, the repository interface reports no licence**, and since the description only dedicates the data to the public domain, no claim is made about the licensing of the code. **Fourth, whether the snapshots match the upstream datasets numerically was not verified**, none being retrieved. **Fifth, whether the structured markup matches the actual content was not verified. Sixth, whether the project is an official output of any institution was not verified**, the description presenting a personal site deployed to a hosting provider. **Seventh, this entry records what was visible on 2026-09-11 and states plainly that the site is public statistics visualisation rather than a mortality forecast or an actuarial opinion.**

entries.title_en: An actuarial valuation platform that evaluates policy cash flows as a directed acyclic graph: it describes itself in writing as an enterprise-grade platform bridging complex risk mathematics and modern user experience, states that graph nodes represent financial events such as premium collection, mortality decrements, and expense payouts while edges dictate the flow of policyholder states and cash across the timeline, stores the blueprint as structured data executed by a Python engine over projection steps, and builds in measures including a best estimate of liabilities, value at risk, conditional tail expectation, and contractual service margin mechanics for the international reporting standard.

entries.summary_en: This is an actuarial valuation platform that evaluates policy cash flows as a directed acyclic graph, describing itself in writing as an actuarial valuation and risk platform. **Measured this round**: created in late August and last pushed on the ninth of September, a repository of about seventeen megabytes in Python, no stars, no licence file, a main branch, and a description of about five kilobytes over one hundred three lines. **This entry belongs to the round theme of adjudicating the items earlier rounds had parked for review**, because this round first probed three new surfaces, a website plugin directory, an organisation account axis, and repository-name-only search, all of which measured as nearly empty, and therefore switched to clearing the parked backlog. **Four things are worth reading: cash flows are modelled as a graph rather than written as a loop, with nodes representing financial events such as premium collection, mortality decrements, and expense payouts, and edges carrying policyholder states and cash along the timeline; the blueprint is separated from the engine, since the front end compiles the graph into structured data stored in the database while a Python engine executes it over projection steps; built-in measures include a best estimate of liabilities, value at risk, conditional tail expectation, and contractual service margin mechanics with risk adjustment tracking for the international reporting standard; and the drag-and-drop editor is described in writing as designing cash flow blueprints without writing code, which this entry flags as precisely the place where auditability of a graphical model needs the most care.** **The platform was neither deployed nor run this round.**
entries.body:
**Actura**（`Rytsia1/Actura`）**是一个**把**保单现金流**建成**有向无环图**来**估值的**精算平台****——**逐字自述为**「**Actuarial Valuation & Risk Platform**」**，**并**逐字自称**「**enterprise-grade actuarial platform that bridges the gap between complex risk mathematics and modern UI/UX**」**。**⭐ 本条目属于本轮主题**「**把此前各轮记为「**待评**」的条目**逐条判定**」**。

**可核实信息（均 2026-09-11 GitHub 接口与 README 实测）**：

**⭐⭐⭐ ① 现金流被建成「**图**」**，**而**不**是**写成**一段**循环****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字写**「**Actura evaluates insurance cash flows as a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG).**」**，**并逐字给出**两句话**的**语义**：**「**Nodes represent financial events (e.g. premium collection, mortality decrements, expense payouts).**」**与**「**Edges dictate the flow of policyholder states and cash across the timeline.**」**；**⭐ 本词条认为**这一处**是**本条**最值得记**的**设计选择**：**⭐ 即**把**「**模型结构**」**外化成**一张**可**保存、**可**展示、**可**逐节点**讨论的**图**，**而**不**把**它**藏**在**几千行**代码**里**——**⭐ 对 RIAA**：**当**你**要**向**非技术**的**评审**解释**一个**现金流模型**时**，**一张**节点图**通常**比**一段**代码**有效**得多**；**⭐ 而**代价**是**：**必须**额外**证明**「**图上**画的**」**与**「**引擎**算的**」**一致**。

**⭐⭐ ② 蓝图与引擎分离：**图**进库、**引擎**按时步**执行****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字写**「**The graph is compiled by the Vue 3 frontend, saved as a JSON blueprint to the database, and executed by the Python actuarial engine over projection timesteps.**」**；**⭐ 架构逐字为四层**：**前端 **Vue 3（**图交互用 **Vue Flow、**图表用 **ECharts）**、**后端 **FastAPI**、**数据库 **PostgreSQL（**经 **SQLAlchemy**，**存**项目、**蓝图与**随机结果）**、**反向代理 **Nginx****；**⭐ 本词条认为**这一分工**对**精算**很**贴切**：**⭐ 即**「**蓝图**」**是**业务语言**（**保费、**给付、**减因），**而**「**引擎**」**是**数值实现**（**投影时步、**情景）**——**⭐ 两者**分开**之后**，**同一张**蓝图**可以**换**引擎**重算**，**而**引擎**可以**被**单独**测试**。

**⭐⭐ ③ 内置指标覆盖**负债、**尾部风险与**新准则****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**功能逐字列出**：**随机引擎**（**逐字**：**Integrated Economic Scenario Generators (ESG) and advanced Monte Carlo simulations**）**、**风险分析**（**逐字**：**BEL, VaR 95%, CVaR / CTE 95, and quantile fan-charts**）**、**新准则**（**逐字**：**IFRS 17 Ready: Automated CSM (Contractual Service Margin) mechanics and Risk Adjustment tracking**）**、**容器化**（**逐字**：**Docker-Ready** 并含 **Nginx** 反向代理）**；**⭐ 本词条**如实指出**：**⭐ 即**这些**是**声明**支持**的**指标**，**而**不是**已**验证**的**结果**——**⚠️ 本次**未运行**任何一次**估值**。

**⭐⭐ ④ 一处**必须**点名的**风险面**：**可视建模**的**可审计性****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字把**拖拽编辑器**描述为**「**a visual, node-based DAG editor for designing insurance cash flow blueprints without writing code**」**；**⭐ 本词条**认为**这一点**值得**单独**提示**：**⭐ 即**「**不写代码**」**降低**了**上手**门槛**，**但**同时**把**「**模型逻辑**」**搬进**了**点击**序列**——**⭐ 若**没有**蓝图**版本**、**变更**记录**与**审批**痕迹**，**则**「**这次**结果**是**哪一张**图**算出来的**」**会**变**得**难以**回答**；**⭐ 对 RIAA**：**凡**用**可视**建模**，**都**要**先**回答**「**蓝图**怎么**版本化**、**谁**批过**」**。

**⭐⭐ ⑤ 与池内条目的关系**：**本站 [[vates-actuarial-engine]] 与 **[[arcrho-reserving-platform]] 覆盖**精算引擎**与**准备金平台**、**[[ifrs17-calculation-engine]] 覆盖**新准则**计算引擎**、**[[detlifeinsurance]] 覆盖**确定性**寿险**计算**——**⭐ 而**本条补上的是**「**以**节点图**为**建模单位**、**并**把**蓝图**存库**再由**引擎**执行**」这一**形态**；**⭐ 本词条**不对以上任何一条做代码级比较**。

**对 RIAA**：**⭐ 六件事值得借**：**① **把**模型结构**外化成**可讨论的**图**；**② **蓝图**与**引擎**分离**，**各自**可**替换**；**③ **尾部风险**（**CVaR／CTE）与**负债**最好**（BEL）要**同时**给**；**④ **新准则**的**负债**与**风险调整**要**分别**跟踪**；**⑤ **可视**建模**必须**配**版本化**与**审批**；**⑥ **容器化**与**反代**是**交付**门槛**，**而**不是**加分项**。

**⚠️ 本词条如实标注**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次**没有部署、**没有运行**该平台**（**未起 **FastAPI**、**未建 **PostgreSQL**、**未跑**任何 **Monte Carlo** 或 **IFRS 17** 计算）**，**故**不主张**其**任何指标**的**数值正确性**。**② ⚠️ 本次**只读**仓库接口返回的元数据**与 **README 文本**，**未读**其 **Python** 与 **Vue** 源码**、**未读**其架构文档**。**③ ⚠️ 该仓库**无许可证文件**（**接口 `license` 字段为空**）**——**⚠️ 本词条**如实指出**：**「**自称**企业级**」**与**「**已授予使用许可**」**是**两件事**。**④ ⚠️ **未核实**其**IFRS 17** 实现**是否**符合**准则**（**⭐ 逐字**只**说**自动 **CSM 机制**与**风险调整**跟踪**）**。**⑤ ⚠️ **未核实**其**经济情景生成器**的**模型**与**校准**来源**。**⑥ ⚠️ **未核实**其**是否**与**任何**保险公司**或**咨询机构**相关**（**⭐ 星标为 **0**，**且**无组织**归属信息**）**。**⑦ ⚠️ 本条目**所记为 **2026-09-11 所见**；**⚠️ 该平台**是**计算工具**，**不是**精算意见**，**也**不是**准则合规证明**。
entries.body_hk:
**Actura**（`Rytsia1/Actura`）**是一個**把**保單現金流**建成**有向無環圖**來**估值的**精算平台****——**逐字自述為**「**Actuarial Valuation & Risk Platform**」**，**並逐字自稱**「**enterprise-grade actuarial platform that bridges the gap between complex risk mathematics and modern UI/UX**」**。**⭐ 本條目屬於本輪主題**「**把此前各輪記為「**待評**」的條目**逐條判定**」**。

**可核實資訊（均 2026-09-11 GitHub 介面與 README 實測）**：

**⭐⭐⭐ ① 現金流建成「**圖**」，**而非寫成一段迴圈****——**逐字**「**Actura evaluates insurance cash flows as a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG).**」**，**並逐字給出語義**「**Nodes represent financial events (e.g. premium collection, mortality decrements, expense payouts).**」**與**「**Edges dictate the flow of policyholder states and cash across the timeline.**」**；**⭐ 即**把模型結構外化成可保存、**可展示、**可逐節點討論的圖**，**代價是必須額外證明「**圖上畫的**」與「**引擎算的**」一致**。

**⭐⭐ ② 藍圖與引擎分離****——**逐字**「**The graph is compiled by the Vue 3 frontend, saved as a JSON blueprint to the database, and executed by the Python actuarial engine over projection timesteps.**」**；**架構逐字為**Vue 3（**Vue Flow 與 ECharts）**、**FastAPI、**PostgreSQL（**SQLAlchemy）**、**Nginx**；**⭐ 即**同一張藍圖可換引擎重算**，**引擎可單獨測試**。

**⭐⭐ ③ 內建指標覆蓋負債、**尾部風險與新準則****——**逐字**Integrated Economic Scenario Generators (ESG) and advanced Monte Carlo simulations**、**BEL, VaR 95%, CVaR / CTE 95, and quantile fan-charts**、**IFRS 17 Ready: Automated CSM (Contractual Service Margin) mechanics and Risk Adjustment tracking**、**Docker-Ready**；**⚠️ 這些是聲明支持的指標**，**不是已驗證的結果**。

**⭐⭐ ④ 一處必須點名的風險面：可視建模的可審計性****——**逐字**「**a visual, node-based DAG editor for designing insurance cash flow blueprints without writing code**」**；**⭐ 即**「**不寫代碼**」把模型邏輯搬進點擊序列**——**若**無藍圖版本、**變更記錄與審批痕跡**，**則**「**這次結果是哪一張圖算的**」**難以回答**。

**⭐⭐ ⑤ 與池內條目的關係**：[[vates-actuarial-engine]]、[[arcrho-reserving-platform]]、[[ifrs17-calculation-engine]]、[[detlifeinsurance]]——**⭐ 本條補上的是**「**以節點圖為建模單位、**藍圖存庫再由引擎執行**」**這一形態**。

**對 RIAA**：**⭐ 六件事值得借**：**① **模型結構外化成圖**；**② **藍圖與引擎分離**；**③ **尾部風險與負債同時給**；**④ **負債與風險調整分別跟蹤**；**⑤ **可視建模配版本化與審批**；**⑥ **容器化與反代是交付門檻**。

**⚠️ 本詞條如實標註**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次**沒有部署、**沒有運行**該平台**，**不主張**其任何指標的數值正確性**。**② ⚠️ 本次**只讀元資料與 README 文本**，**未讀**其 Python 與 Vue 源碼**。**③ ⚠️ 該倉庫無許可證檔案**——**「**自稱企業級**」與「**已授予使用許可**」是兩件事**。**④ ⚠️ **未核實**其 IFRS 17 實現是否符合準則**。**⑤ ⚠️ **未核實**其經濟情景生成器的模型與校準來源**。**⑥ ⚠️ **未核實**其是否與任何保險公司或諮詢機構相關**。**⑦ ⚠️ 本條目所記為 2026-09-11 所見**；**⚠️ 該平台是計算工具**，**不是**精算意見**，**也**不是**準則合規證明**。
entries.body_en:
This is an actuarial valuation platform that evaluates policy cash flows as a directed acyclic graph, describing itself as an actuarial valuation and risk platform and, in its own words, as an enterprise-grade platform bridging complex risk mathematics and modern user experience. **This entry belongs to the round theme of adjudicating the items earlier rounds had parked for review.**

**Verified information, all measured on 2026-09-11 from the repository interface and the description**:

**First, cash flows are modelled as a graph rather than written as a loop.** The description states that the platform evaluates insurance cash flows as a directed acyclic graph, and gives the semantics in two sentences: nodes represent financial events such as premium collection, mortality decrements, and expense payouts, while edges dictate the flow of policyholder states and cash across the timeline. **Externalising the model structure into a graph that can be saved, shown, and discussed node by node, rather than burying it in thousands of lines of code, is the most transferable choice here, because a node diagram usually explains a cash flow model to a non-technical reviewer far better than a code excerpt does, at the cost of having to demonstrate separately that what the graph shows and what the engine computes agree.**

**Second, the blueprint and the engine are separated.** The description states that the graph is compiled by the front end, saved as structured blueprint data in the database, and executed by the Python engine over projection steps. **The stated architecture is a single-page front end handling graph interaction and charting, a Python interface service, a relational database storing projects, blueprints, and stochastic results, and a reverse proxy. Blueprint and engine separate cleanly into business language such as premiums, benefits, and decrements on one side and numerical implementation such as projection steps and scenarios on the other, so one blueprint can be recomputed on another engine and the engine can be tested on its own.**

**Third, the built-in measures span liabilities, tail risk, and the international reporting standard.** The feature list names integrated economic scenario generators with Monte Carlo simulation, measures including a best estimate of liabilities, value at risk at ninety-five percent, conditional tail expectation, and quantile fan charts, automated contractual service margin mechanics with risk adjustment tracking, and containerisation with a reverse proxy. **These are claimed capabilities rather than verified results, since no valuation was run this round.**

**Fourth, one risk surface must be named: the auditability of graphical modelling.** The description calls the editor a visual node-based tool for designing cash flow blueprints without writing code. **Removing code lowers the barrier to entry while moving model logic into a sequence of clicks, so without blueprint versioning, change records, and approval traces, the question of which diagram produced a given result becomes hard to answer.** **For any graphical modelling exercise, how the blueprint is versioned and who approved it should be settled first.**

**Fifth, relative to existing entries**: pooled entries cover actuarial engines, a reserving platform, an accounting-standard calculation engine, and deterministic life calculations, **while this entry supplies the form in which a node graph is the modelling unit, stored as a blueprint and executed by an engine. This entry makes no code-level comparison against any of them.**

**For RIAA**: **six practices transfer: externalise model structure into a discussable graph; separate blueprint from engine so each can be replaced; report liabilities and tail risk together; track the liability estimate and its risk adjustment separately; pair graphical modelling with versioning and approval; and treat containerisation and a reverse proxy as delivery requirements rather than extras.**

**Marked honestly by this entry**: **first, the platform was neither deployed nor run**, no service was started, no database was created, and no simulation or standard-specific calculation was executed, **so no claim is made about the numerical correctness of any measure**. **Second, only repository metadata and the description were read**, not the Python or front-end source and not the architecture document. **Third, the repository carries no licence file**, and **describing itself as enterprise-grade is a different thing from granting a licence to use it**. **Fourth, whether its standard-specific implementation conforms to the accounting standard was not verified**, the description only claiming automated margin mechanics and risk adjustment tracking. **Fifth, the model and calibration behind the scenario generator were not verified. Sixth, whether the project relates to any insurer or consultancy was not verified**, with no stars and no organisational affiliation stated. **Seventh, this entry records what was visible on 2026-09-11 and states plainly that the platform is a computational tool rather than an actuarial opinion or a demonstration of standards compliance.**

entries.summary_en: This is a voice assistant for people covered by German statutory health insurance, describing itself in writing as an artificial-intelligence assistant for users of that system and stating that it uses voice input and plain text responses to answer common health insurance questions. **Measured this round**: created in late March and last pushed on the tenth of September, a repository under a megabyte in PHP with an MIT licence, two stars, a main branch, and a description of about five kilobytes over one hundred fifty-one lines. **This entry belongs to the round theme of adjudicating the items earlier rounds had parked for review.** **Four things are worth reading: it is aimed at the insured rather than at the insurer, which puts the assistant on the citizen side of the counter; the interaction is voice first with streamed answers, and speech input and read-aloud work offline once installed; the delivery form is a Windows installer with stated minimum requirements and a claim that no programming knowledge is needed to use it; and the privacy section states three specific facts, that questions are processed through hosted servers, that no personal data is saved permanently unless chat history is enabled, and that voice data is used only for transcription during the session.** **The assistant was neither installed nor used this round.**
entries.body:
**gkv-chatbot**（`Kelliaenvisioned219/gkv-chatbot`）**是一个**面向**德国法定医保**（GKV）**参保人**的**语音 **AI 助手****——**逐字自述为**「**gkv-chatbot is an AI-based assistant designed for users of the German statutory health insurance system (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung, GKV). It uses voice input and clear text responses to answer common questions related to health insurance.**」**。**⭐ 本条目属于本轮主题**「**把此前各轮记为「**待评**」的条目**逐条判定**」**。

**可核实信息（均 2026-09-11 GitHub 接口与 README 实测）**：

**⭐⭐⭐ ① 它站在**参保人**那一侧**，**而**不**是**保险公司**那一侧****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字写**「**designed for users of the German statutory health insurance system**」**，**并**逐字把**用途**限定为**回答**与**医保**相关的**常见问题**；**⭐ 本词条认为**这一处**值得记**：**⭐ 即**同样**是**「**保险 ＋ **AI」**，**面向**「**公司内部**」**与**面向**「**被保人**」**会**导出**完全**不同的**产品**——**⭐ 前者**关注**效率**与**一致性**，**后者**关注**可理解性**与**信任**；**⭐ 而**在**法定医保**这种**强规则**领域**，**面向**参保人的**助手**必须**能**被**核对**（**逐字**称**答案**来自**知识库**）。

**⭐⭐ ② 语音优先 ＋ **流式回答**，**且**语音**在**安装后可**离线****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**功能逐字列出**：**理解**德国医保**问题、**接受**语音命令**并**转文字、**答案**由**知识库**支撑、**边**交互**边**流式**输出（**逐字**：**SSE - Server-Sent Events**）、**语言**清楚简单、**Windows** 上**无需**特殊配置、**安装后**语音输入与**文本转语音**可**离线**；**⭐ 本词条**认为**这一组**取舍**很**务实**：**⭐ 即**把**「**必须联网**」**限制在**「**生成回答**」**这一步**，**而**让**「**输入与朗读**」**在**本地**完成**——**⭐ 对**面向**老年人**或**网络不稳**场景的**助手**，**这**通常**是**正确**的**取舍**。

**⭐⭐ ③ 交付形态是**安装包**，**并**逐字给出**最低要求****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字列出**系统要求**（**Windows 10 或以上、**至少 **4 GB 内存、**500 MB 磁盘空间、**稳定**网络用于**回答**流式输出、**麦克风**与**扬声器或**耳机）**，**并**逐字称**「**You do not need any programming knowledge to use it. Just install and start chatting.**」**；**⭐ 本词条**如实指出**：**⭐ 即**把**AI 助手**交付成**桌面安装包**，**在**保险**这种**以**网站**与**App**为主的**行业**里**属于**少数做法**——**⭐ 它**带来**的**代价**是**：**版本**分发**、**更新**与**信任**（**用户**要**装**一个 **.exe**）**都**变**重**。

**⭐⭐ ④ 隐私段落**逐字**写明三件事****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**README 逐字写**：**问题**经 **AWS** 服务器**处理**（**逐字**：**gkv-chatbot processes your questions securely through AWS servers.**）**、**除非**开启**聊天记录**否则**不**永久**保存**个人数据**（**逐字**：**No personal data is saved permanently unless you enable chat history.**）**、**语音数据**仅**用于**当次**会话**的**语音转文字**（**逐字**：**Voice data is used only to convert speech to text during your session.**）**；**⭐ 本词条认为**这一处**是**本条**最有价值**的**部分**：**⭐ 即**在**医保**这种**高敏感**领域**，**把**「**数据**去哪**」**写成**三条**可**核对**的**句子**，**比**一句**「**我们**重视**隐私**」**有用**得多**——**⭐ 对 RIAA**：**任何**面向**客户**的 **AI 功能**，**都**应**能**回答**这**三问**（**处理**在哪、**保存**什么、**用**多久**）**。

**⭐⭐ ⑤ 与池内条目的关系**：**本站 [[insurance-chatbot-finetune]] 覆盖**微调**客服机器人**、**[[mongodb-rag-insurance]] 覆盖**保险**文档问答**、**[[health-denial-appeals]] 覆盖**拒付**申诉**——**⭐ 而**本条补上的是**「**面向**参保人的**语音**助手**、**以**桌面**安装包**交付**」这一形态**；**⭐ 本词条**不对以上任何一条做代码级比较**。

**对 RIAA**：**⭐ 六件事值得借**：**① **想清**助手**站在**哪一侧**（**公司**或**客户）**；**② **把**联网**限制在**必要**步骤**，**其余**本地化**；**③ **流式**输出**改善**体感**；**④ **隐私**要**写成**可核对**的三问**；**⑤ **交付**形态**决定**信任成本**；**⑥ **最低**系统要求**必须**写明**。

**⚠️ 本词条如实标注**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次**没有安装、**没有使用**该助手**（**未下载**任何安装包、**未调用**任何模型**）**，**故**不主张**其**答案**质量**、**也**不主张**其**语音识别**效果**。**② ⚠️ 本次**只读**仓库接口返回的元数据**与 **README 文本**，**未读**其 **PHP** 源码**。**③ ⚠️ 其**README** 写法**偏**「**下载引导**」**式**（**多个**下载徽章**、**以**安装步骤**为主）**，**⚠️ 本词条**如实指出**：**⭐ 即**这类**写法**通常**伴随**较少**的**架构**说明**，**故**其**实现**细节**本次**无法核实**。**④ ⚠️ **未核实**其**知识库**内容**是否**与**德国**法定医保**规则**同步**（**⭐ 逐字**自称**答案**基于**知识库**与**经验证的**医保规则**）**。**⑤ ⚠️ **未核实**其**与**任何**德国**医保基金**或**监管**的关系**。**⑥ ⚠️ **未核实**其**数据**处理**是否**符合 **GDPR**（**⭐ 本词条**只**转述**其**隐私**段落**）**。**⑦ ⚠️ 本条目**所记为 **2026-09-11 所见**；**⚠️ 该助手**是**信息工具**，**不是**医保**决定**，**也**不是**法律或**医疗意见**。

**gkv-chatbot**（`Kelliaenvisioned219/gkv-chatbot`）**是一個**面向**德國法定醫保**（GKV）**參保人**的**語音 AI 助手****——**逐字自述為**「**gkv-chatbot is an AI-based assistant designed for users of the German statutory health insurance system (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung, GKV). It uses voice input and clear text responses to answer common questions related to health insurance.**」**。**⭐ 本條目屬於本輪主題**「**把此前各輪記為「**待評**」的條目**逐條判定**」**。

**可核實資訊（均 2026-09-11 GitHub 介面與 README 實測）**：

**⭐⭐⭐ ① 它站在參保人那一側****——**逐字**designed for users of the German statutory health insurance system**；**⭐ 即**同樣是「**保險＋AI**」**，**面向公司內部與面向被保人會導出完全不同的產品**。

**⭐⭐ ② 語音優先＋流式回答，**且**語音安裝後可離線****——**功能逐字含**語音命令轉文字、**答案由知識庫支撐、**流式輸出（**逐字**SSE - Server-Sent Events**）、**安裝後語音輸入與文本轉語音可離線**；**⭐ 即**把「**必須聯網**」限制在「**生成回答**」**，**輸入與朗讀**在本地完成**。

**⭐⭐ ③ 交付形態是安裝包****——**逐字要求**Windows 10 或以上、**至少 4 GB 記憶體、**500 MB 磁碟**；**並逐字稱**You do not need any programming knowledge to use it. Just install and start chatting.**；**⭐ 即**版本分發、**更新與信任成本都變重**。

**⭐⭐ ④ 隱私段落逐字寫明三件事****——**逐字**gkv-chatbot processes your questions securely through AWS servers.**、**「**No personal data is saved permanently unless you enable chat history.**」**、**「**Voice data is used only to convert speech to text during your session.**」**；**⭐ 即**任何面向客戶的 AI 功能**都應能回答這三問（**處理在哪、**保存什麼、**用多久**）**。

**⭐⭐ ⑤ 與池內條目的關係**：[[insurance-chatbot-finetune]]、[[mongodb-rag-insurance]]、[[health-denial-appeals]]——**⭐ 本條補上的是**「**面向參保人的語音助手、**以桌面安裝包交付**」**這一形態**。

**對 RIAA**：**⭐ 六件事值得借**：**① **想清助手站在哪一側**；**② **聯網限制在必要步驟**；**③ **流式輸出改善體感**；**④ **隱私寫成三問**；**⑤ **交付形態決定信任成本**；**⑥ **最低系統要求要寫明**。

entries.body_en:
This is a voice assistant for people covered by German statutory health insurance, stating in writing that it is an assistant designed for users of that system and that it uses voice input and plain text responses to answer common health insurance questions. **This entry belongs to the round theme of adjudicating the items earlier rounds had parked for review.**

**Verified information, all measured on 2026-09-11 from the repository interface and the description**:

**First, it stands on the insured side rather than the insurer side.** The description states that the assistant is designed for users of the statutory system and limits its purpose to answering common health insurance questions. **The same pairing of insurance and artificial intelligence produces very different products depending on whether it faces internal staff or the insured, because the first optimises for throughput and consistency while the second optimises for comprehensibility and trust, and in a strongly rule-bound system such as statutory health insurance an assistant facing the insured must be checkable, which is why the description says answers are backed by a knowledge base.**

**Second, voice comes first with streamed answers, and speech works offline once installed.** The feature list covers understanding health insurance questions, accepting voice commands with speech-to-text, answers backed by a knowledge base, responses streamed while the user interacts through server-sent events, plain language, no special setup on Windows, and offline voice input and text-to-speech after installation. **Confining the online requirement to the generation step while keeping input and read-aloud local is a pragmatic split, and for assistants aimed at older users or unstable networks it is usually the right one.**

**Third, the delivery form is an installer with stated minimum requirements.** The description lists a recent Windows version, a memory floor, a disk allowance, a stable connection for streamed answers, and a microphone plus speakers, and states that no programming knowledge is needed to install and start chatting. **Shipping an insurance assistant as a desktop installer is unusual in an industry that mostly ships websites and apps, and it makes version distribution, updates, and the trust cost of running a downloaded executable heavier.**

**Fourth, the privacy section states three specific facts.** It says questions are processed through hosted servers, that no personal data is saved permanently unless chat history is enabled, and that voice data is used only to convert speech to text during the session. **In a sensitive domain such as health insurance, writing where the data goes as three checkable sentences is far more useful than a general assurance of caring about privacy, and any customer-facing artificial-intelligence feature should be able to answer the same three questions: where processing happens, what is stored, and for how long.**

**Fifth, relative to existing entries**: pooled entries cover a fine-tuned service chatbot, insurance document question answering, and denial appeals, **while this entry supplies the form of a voice assistant for the insured delivered as a desktop installer. This entry makes no code-level comparison against any of them.**

**For RIAA**: **six practices transfer: decide which side of the counter the assistant stands on; confine the online requirement to the necessary step and keep the rest local; stream output for perceived responsiveness; state privacy as three checkable questions; recognise that the delivery form sets the trust cost; and publish minimum system requirements.**

**Marked honestly by this entry**: **first, the assistant was neither installed nor used**, no installer was downloaded and no model endpoint was called, **so no claim is made about answer quality or speech recognition**. **Second, only repository metadata and the description were read**, not the PHP source. **Third, the description is written in a download-guide style with several download badges and installation steps dominating**, and this entry notes that such descriptions usually carry little architectural detail, so the implementation could not be assessed. **Fourth, whether the knowledge base is kept in step with statutory health insurance rules was not verified**, the text only claiming that answers rest on a knowledge base and verified rules. **Fifth, no relationship to any German health fund or regulator was verified. Sixth, whether its data processing meets European data protection requirements was not verified**, only its own privacy paragraph being transcribed. **Seventh, this entry records what was visible on 2026-09-11 and states plainly that the assistant is an information tool rather than a coverage decision or legal or medical advice.**

entries.title_en: An end-to-end business intelligence project on the Chilean life insurance market that writes out both the synthetic nature of its data and six methodological limits: it describes itself in writing as an end-to-end business intelligence project using wholly synthetic data inspired by concepts and indicators of the Chilean insurance market, works on a panel of one hundred forty-four observations covering twelve fictional companies over twelve quarters with thirty-nine original variables, publishes control values down to direct premium and weighted loss ratio for the latest quarter, and states in writing that its synthetic solvency figure is an educational indicator that does not reproduce the regulator official methodology.

entries.summary_en: This is an end-to-end business intelligence project on the Chilean life insurance market, describing itself in writing as a project built on wholly synthetic data inspired by the concepts and indicators of that market. **Measured this round**: created in July and last pushed on the eleventh of September, a repository of about eighty-seven megabytes whose stated language is a spreadsheet query language, no stars, no licence file, a main branch, and a description of about eighteen kilobytes over three hundred ninety-four lines. **This entry belongs to the round theme of adjudicating the items earlier rounds had parked for review, and it fills the thinnest category on the site, life insurance, which held nineteen entries before this round.** **Four things are worth reading: the limitations are written in more detail than the conclusions, six of them stating that return on equity was excluded from the main conclusions because of a plausibility limit in the synthetic data, that the synthetic solvency figure is an educational indicator which does not reproduce the regulator official methodology, and that the net portfolio balance does not fully reconcile with the change in the stock of policyholders and is therefore not interpreted as churn, retention, or persistence; structured query language is used as a control layer before visualisation, with a published table of control values for the latest quarter covering direct premium, quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year growth, weighted loss ratio, expense ratio, technical result, technical margin, synthetic solvency, and policyholders in force; the executive recommendations argue in writing against a single score, urging that technical efficiency and capital strength be evaluated separately rather than merged with arbitrary weights; and this entry notes one internal inconsistency, since the English summary describes the project as examining the market using public regulator data while the body and the limitations state that the data are wholly synthetic.** **Neither its queries nor its dashboard model were run this round.**
